entries.name: _cl_color
entries.description: The value for the color of the player’s shirt and pants.  This single value is able to hold both of the colors required for the player’s shirt and pants. In order to store the value for the colors the following equation has to be used: ‘((shirt color) * 16) + (pants color)‘.

entries.name: _snd_mixahead
entries.summary: Mixahead seconds; 0.1 default (~10 FPS min). If stutter, try 0.2 (~5 FPS). Higher = more CPU
entries.description: Sets how far into the future to mix the sound. Every frame, the sound is mixed up to a certain point, under the assumption that the next frame will arrive before the entire mixed buffer of sound is played. So with the default value of 0.1 seconds, if your framerate dips below 10 fps, it will run off the end of the sound buffer and you'll get stuttering sound. To fix this, increase the value (e.g. a value of 0.2 will handle as low as 5 fps before stuttering). However, increasing the mixahead time means the CPU has to do that much more work mixing more sound (thus possibly lowering your framerate, defeating the purpose), so be reasonable.

entries.name: addloc
entries.description: QW LOC Creator: 'addloc ra' will add a location at your current location with the name ra. 'addlock auto' will auto create locs at all the weapon, armor, tele, powerup locations if there no duplicates. A good loc probably needs 30+ locations

entries.name: alias
entries.description: Now outputs the current command string, rather than deleting the alias (example: alias ready). If you only type alias it will print all aliases and their assignments. See command unalias.

entries.name: aliasedit
entries.description: Edit an alias. aliasedit aliasname. Press tab to after typing aliasedit to complete possibilites.

entries.name: aliaslist
entries.description: Outputs an alphabetized list of all aliases. If substring is present, lists only commands that start with substring.

entries.name: allow_download
entries.summary: Auto-download missing bsp/lit/loc from QSS server. 0=off, 1=QSS only, 2=allow FTE-style downloads
entries.description: Allow client to autodownload missing items (bsp, lit, loc) from a QSS Server. A value of 2 allows FTE server downloads

entries.name: allow_download_sky
entries.summary: Allow skybox downloads. 0=off, 1=on (auto-fetch missing skyboxes from server)
entries.description: Allow downloading of skyboxes

entries.name: ambient_fade
entries.summary: Ambient fade speed; higher = faster fade. Examples: 0.5=slow, 1=default, 2=fast.
entries.description: How quickly ambient sounds fade in/out. Higher values make the sound fade quicker.

entries.name: ambient_level
entries.summary: Ambient volume for sky/lava/water/slime. Examples: 0=off, 0.3=quiet, 1=default, 2=louder. See cl_ambient
entries.description: How loud ambient sounds are. This includes wind, water, and other ambient sounds. O nly effects the sky/lava/water/slime sounds. See cl_ambient

entries.name: apropos
entries.description: Searches for commands/cvar names for the given substring

entries.name: audiofiles
entries.description: Lists available sounds or music with audiofiles sounds|music [filter], including the package or directory supplying each file. The optional filter matches either the file path or its source.

entries.name: b_switch
entries.description: This variable allows you to define the highest weapon that the client should switch to upon a backpack pickup. The possible arguments of "b_switch" refer to the impulse that is used to switch to a certain weapon: 1-8 (the weapon numbers). Most common is b_switch 2. The server quakec controls this behavior and this sends the info to the server if supported via a infokey. Also see w_switch

entries.name: ban
entries.description: Prevent players from joining your server. Use this command to ban people from your server. Unfortunately, this command only allows for the banning of a single IP or a single domain. When this command is used without parameters ‘ban‘ it will display the list of bans. If you want to disable banning then use the command ‘ban off‘. If you want to ban a single address then use that command with just that address. If you want to ban a whole domain of IP addresses then you will have to substitute the number 0 for the part of the domain that you wish to ban and you will also have to use a mask for that domain which means that you will have to enter the IP address twice.

entries.name: -basedir
entries.description: Overrides the system supplied base directory. The "base directory" is the path to the directory holding the quake.exe and all game directories.  The sys_* files pass this to host_init in quakeparms_t->basedir.  This can be overridden with the "-basedir" command line parm to allow code debugging in a different directory.  The base directory is only used during filesystem initialization. (i.e. -basedir 'c:\quake')

entries.name: -basegame
entries.description: replaces all hardcoded dirs (read: alternative to id1) and isn't flushed on normal gamedir switches (like id1).

entries.name: begin
entries.description: This command is used by the client to inform the server to begin sending game information.

entries.name: bf
entries.description: Perform a background screen flash. The background screen flash is the same one that is produced when the player picked up a powerup in the game. This command basically serves no useful function except when people want to use it in scripts to give the user some visual feedback when an aliases is used.

entries.name: bgm_extmusic
entries.summary: Use external music files instead of CD audio. Examples: 1=enabled (default), 0=disable external music
entries.description: Disable or enable playback of external music files instead of cdaudio. default is 1 (enabled).

entries.name: bgmvolume
entries.description: Volume of background cd music.

entries.name: bind
entries.description: Assign a command or a set of commands to a key. To bind multiple commands to a key, enclose the commands in double-quotes (“) and separate them with semicolons (;). To bind bind keys which do not produce any characters use the key’s name to bind to it. Also, I have provided a listing of all the names for the keys which do not print any output to the console. The ESCAPE, and ~ (tilde) keys can only be bound from an external configuration file.

entries.name: bindedit
entries.description: Edit a bind. bindedit bindname. Press tab to after typing bindedit to complete possibilites.

entries.name: bindlist
entries.description: Lists all key bindings.

entries.name: bottomcolor
entries.description: User info keys used in QW/FTE/QSS. See setinfo and serverinfo

entries.name: -bpp
entries.description: Quakespasm: Initialize opengl with 24-bit depth buffer at 32 bpp

entries.name: campaign
entries.description: For the 2021 rerelease. Used to track whether the game was started from start.bsp as opposed to warping to a single map, in order to avoid giving you the achievement for completing the game if you just skip ahead to end.bsp. Think of it as an extra cvar that you can use for level transitions. Without the cvar declared in the engine then u get a spamfest in the console stating “unknown cvar campaign when playing mg1

entries.name: centerview
entries.description: Centers the player’s view. This command only works when the +mlook function is disabled. This command is basically used along with the +klook command to help to center the view.

entries.name: -certhost
entries.description: Sets the hostname used when the engine auto-generates a DTLS certificate because it can’t find/load the key+cert files. If you don’t pass -certhost, the server-side generation path defaults to "localhost" for the temporary certificate. This is mainly to make self-signed/temporary certs less confusing when connecting (especially if you’re using a named host). Example: ./quake -useice -certhost myserver.example.com (and omit -privkey/-pubkey to let it generate).

entries.name: cfg_save_aliases
entries.description: Save non-server issued aliases to conifg.cfg

entries.name: cfg_unbindall
entries.description: Unbindall before loading stored bindings

entries.name: changelevel
entries.description: Change the map without dropping the connected clients from the server. This command is used by the server to manually change the map without kicking the connected clients from the server. If you are managing the server you should use this command instead of the usual map command.

entries.name: chase_active
entries.description: Toggle the use of a chase camera. This command can be used to enable a chase camera so that the view is actually behind the player from a 3rd person perspective instead of the default 1st person perspective. Currently this command has a problem that when enabled the player will only see the weapon and the firing graphic moving around the level and not the player figure.

entries.name: chase_back
entries.description: The distance that the chase camera should be behind the player.

entries.name: chase_modelangles
entries.description: Applies a "pitch yaw roll" rotation offset to the player model while the chase camera is active, defaulting to "0 0 0". It can make the model face left, right, backward, or use a custom orientation independently of the camera.

entries.name: chase_right
entries.description: The distance that the chase camera should be to the right of the player.

entries.name: chase_up
entries.description: The distance that the chase camera should be above the player.

entries.name: cl_afk
entries.description: Add AFK to name when you minimize client so other players know you are AFK

entries.name: cl_aliasoverlap
entries.description: The cl_aliasoverlap variable controls whether aliases can override existing console variables (cvars). When enabled (1), aliases take precedence over cvars, meaning if an alias is created with the same name as a cvar, the alias will execute instead of the cvar. This allows users to define custom shortcuts or scripts that mask cvars. However, when disabled (0), the system prevents aliases from conflicting with cvars to ensure that cvars remain accessible and function as intended. In this implementation, if cl_aliasoverlap is set to 0 and a user attempts to create an alias with the name of an existing cvar, the alias is automatically renamed by appending "_a" to avoid conflicts.

entries.name: cl_alwaysrun
entries.description: Set to 1 in order to scale forward/side/up speed by "cl_movespeedkey" (usually 2), and to make "speedkey" act as "slowkey". This is a new QS cvar, for vanilla/traditional set this to 0. Not needed if speed settings for maxed. 3 variables - cl_forwardspeed, cl_backspeed, cl_sidespeed. Forward and back are set to 200. Side is set to 350. Another variable, sv_maxspeed is 320. With “always run” off, then you “walk”. If you don’t walk diagonally, then forward/back speed is 200qu/s, but sidespeed is 320qu/s because it tries to go 350 qu/s but gets clamped by sv_maxspeed. If you walk diagonally, the forward and side speed vectors are added, and then velocity clamped to sv_maxspeed. Diagonal walking is thus a lot faster than forward.With “always run” off, you hold a certain key to run. When running in this way, forward/back/side are doubled to 400/400/700, but sv_maxspeed stays the same at 320, so you will move at 320qu/s in all directions because of the speed clamping. Diagonal direction is heavily weighted to the side because the side speed is so high. With “always run” on, you don’t need to hold a key to run. You are always running. However, the behaviour is a bit different - forward and back get doubled, but side stays the same, so effective speeds are 400/400/350. Clamping to sv_maxspeed still occurs so you still move 320qu/s in all directions, but diagonal movement is now slightly weighted to the forward direction. The difference in behaviour between “always run off, but hold the run key” and “always run on” is most likely an unintended bug with the original design. In Quakespasm, there’s a third option, which is like “always run” in that you don’t hold a key, but the movement speeds are the same as vanilla “always run off, but hold run key”, so 400/400/700 (and then clamped to 320). Unlike vanilla’s “always run”, you can now hold the run key to walk. So really, the Quakespasm mode is just like a run-key inverted vanilla “always run off” aka power bunnyhopping. Power bunny hopping is bunny hopping but also briefly holding forward when landing to avoid loosing speed due to friction. Power bunny hopping can increase speeds to about 700. Ground friction is still a problem because the required view angle have to be so precise at high speeds. Power bunny hopping is not required for QuakeWorld. There is no ground friction so regular bunny hopping in QuakeWorld is faster than power bunny hopping in Netquake. Power bunny hopping is easier when "Always run" is off and the run is always pressed. To ensure this is the case, disable "always run" and run the command +speed. Power bunny hopping is still speed turning. But speed turning is different in the air vs. on the ground, and we are only on the ground for one game tick. The optimal view angle when on the ground, and moving forward, and strafing, and moving above 450 is turning slightly into the strafing direction. The optimal view angle when in the air, and not moving forward, and strafing is continually turning into the strafing direction. So power bunny hopping requires quickly and precisely switching between these two types of speed turning.The more speed you have the more ground friction reduces speed. This means that getting a single power bunny hop can take away all speed increases from several perfect speed power bunny hops. The faster you move the more friction reduces speed and the harder it is to hit good landings. This makes power bunny hopping difficult to use in general Quake situations.

entries.name: cl_ambient
entries.description: Send "stopsound" when connected to a server to disable ambient sounds. For all ambient sounds NOT sky/lava/water/slime. Set ambient_level 0 to stop other ambient sounds. DM3 computers is an example of sounds that ambient_level 0 will not disable.

entries.name: cl_anglespeedkey
entries.description: Multiplier for +speed. See alwaysrun. The speed at which you turn when running. This command allows the player to turn faster when he’s running. This is kind of a reverse of real world physics, but it works very well in the game world.

entries.name: cl_autodemo
entries.description: Auto-record settings: 0 = No auto-recording (default); 1 = Record every new map, with or without server; 2 = Record only in official CRMOD/CRCTF matches; 3 = Like 1, online only; 4 = Like 1, but splits at map change.

entries.name: cl_autovote
entries.description: 1 will auto vote yes to timelimit, 2 will vote yes to all requests

entries.name: cl_autovote_list
entries.description: cl_autovote_list is an archived string cvar that filters which server vote requests are auto-voted on when cl_autovote is enabled, accepting a comma- or semicolon-separated list of player names, map names, or vote keywords to match against. The first entry can optionally be the mode keyword include or exclude (default is exclude) — in exclude mode, votes matching any listed entry are skipped, while in include mode, only votes matching a listed entry are auto-voted on. For example, cl_autovote_list "exclude, playername, change map" will skip auto-voting on requests from playername or any change map vote, while cl_autovote_list "include, match length, frag limit" will only auto-vote on match length and frag limit requests.

entries.name: cl_backspeed
entries.description: The speed at which the player moves backward. You can set this variable to a much higher value such as 500 just in case you join a server on which the administrator allows the players to move at a faster speed.

entries.name: cl_beams_polygons
entries.description: Straight lg beam -- larger values for thicker width

entries.name: cl_bob
entries.description: The distance that you weapon moves up and down on the screen when running. If you want your weapon to stay steady when running set this variable to 0. Most hardcore players use this setting to give them a better aim when shooting on the run.

entries.name: cl_bobbing
entries.description: Quake 3 style bobbing animation up and down for items (weapons, armors, etc)

entries.name: cl_bobcycle
entries.description: The time in seconds that it takes the weapon to move up and down on the screen.  If you want your weapon to stay steady when running set this variable to 0. Most hardcore players use this setting to give them a better aim when shooting on the run.

entries.name: cl_bobup
entries.description: The time in seconds that the weapon stays in the up position.  If you want your weapon to stay steady when running set this variable to 0. Most hardcore players use this setting to give them a better aim when shooting on the run.

entries.name: cl_chat_autocomplete
entries.description: Enables the new inline word-completion suggestion for message-mode chat and console lines recognized as chat, defaulting to 1. Suggestions come from the generated high-confidence word dictionary and are only offered at the end of the current input.

entries.name: cl_chatmode
entries.description: If turned on (1), everything that Quake can't interpret (not command or cvar or alias) is sent as chat. Similar to QW clients, you don't have to type "say " every time you wanna say something. Default value is "1". A value of 2 will add a leading space to every console line so you will not run into commands/aliases/cvars and can type freely. cl_say 3 acts like cl_say 2 but if a console string does not have a leading space it performs the normal search for string that happens when cl_say is 0

entries.name: cl_contentfilter
entries.description: A value of 1 will hide IPs in MP menu, and user name prints for condump and screenshots. A value of 2 will add filtering a variety of bad words from chat.

entries.name: cl_ctf_pub_modelswap
entries.description: Enables automatic replacement models for recognized CTF PUG servers, defaulting to 0. It substitutes supported Threewave-style flag, hook, chain, and weapon models when the server is detected as compatible.

entries.name: cl_damagehue
entries.description: Shifts viewmodel orange tint on damage taken to let the player know they have recieved damage. Values: 0 - no shift, 1 - shift on, 2 - shift AND shift crosshair (Default: 1)

entries.name: cl_damagehuecolor
entries.description: Set any RGB value for damage hue or traditonal 1-13 quake colors

entries.name: cl_deadbodyfilter
entries.description: Filter dead bodies. Some mods will do this themselves, this ensures all bodies are removed regadless of mod

entries.name: cl_demo_eyecam
entries.description: Use cl_demo_eyecam 1 during demo playback to turn a third-person chasecam recording into a first-person view from the chased player’s eyes.

entries.name: cl_demo_format
entries.description: Selects the format used when recording demos, defaulting to dem. Supported builds also accept dz to create a compressed DZip archive.

entries.name: cl_demo_minframes
entries.description: Hides demos shorter than the specified number of frames from the demo browser, defaulting to 0 for disabled. Negative values additionally delete newly recorded demos that fall below the absolute threshold.

entries.name: cl_demoeyes
entries.description: Instead of seeing eyes for invisible players you see a transparent player model

entries.name: cl_demoreel
entries.description: The cl_demoreel setting controls the game's attract mode, cycling through gameplay demos. When set to 0 (off), the attract mode is disabled, and the game does not automatically play demos. At 1 (startup only), a demo plays during startup but does not continue looping. For values greater than 1 (on), attract mode is fully enabled, continuously looping through demos indefinitely, creating a classic arcade-style experience.

entries.name: cl_demoreel_playback_controls
entries.description: Controls whether normal playback-control keys operate during startup demo-reel playback, defaulting to 0. When disabled, those keys open the menu instead of manipulating the demo.

entries.name: cl_discord_presence
entries.description: Controls Discord Rich Presence through local IPC, defaulting to 0 for off. Mode 1 publishes all supported states, while mode 2 publishes only connected cooperative or multiplayer activity.

entries.name: cl_display_server_hostnames
entries.summary: Shows cached server hostnames in place of numeric addresses; 0 keeps raw addresses.
entries.description: Enabled by default and saved to config. Uses the hostname cache to display a known hostname for a server IP address. When disabled or no matching cache entry is available, the numeric address remains visible.

entries.name: cl_downloadbegin
entries.description: cl_downloadbegin is an internal command sent by the server to your client to initiate a server-to-client file transfer for a missing file you requested. It signals the start of the download process and provides the client with the expected total size and the name of the file being sent. Upon receiving this command, your client prepares a temporary file to store the incoming data and notifies the server it's ready to begin receiving the file chunks.

entries.name: cl_downloadfinished
entries.description: cl_downloadfinished is an internal command sent by the server to your client after it has finished transmitting all the data for a requested file download. The server includes the final file size and a checksum hash with this command, which your client uses to verify the integrity of the downloaded temporary file. If the verification succeeds, the client renames the temporary file to its proper name and location; otherwise, the download is considered failed, and the temporary file is deleted.

entries.name: cl_forwardspeed
entries.description: The speed at which the player moves forward. You can set this variable to a much higher value such as 500 just in case you join a server on which the administrator allows the players to move at a faster speed.

entries.name: cl_fullpitch
entries.description: cl_fullpitch is not actually a standard client command or variable you can set yourself; it's registered as a command the server might send, but the client is coded to ignore it. The actual control over whether players can look fully up or down (full pitch) is handled by the server's sv_fullpitch variable. If the server has sv_fullpitch set to 1 (the default in this codebase), players can look freely, otherwise, their vertical view is restricted like in original NetQuake.

entries.name: cl_gun_drift
entries.description: Adds a configurable lag effect to the weapon viewmodel, interpolating the gun’s position and roll opposite to recent view rotation so turns feel weightier. Set to 0 to disable; positive values act as the turn- distance threshold, with higher numbers giving more smoothing before the gun catches up.

entries.name: cl_gun_fovscale
entries.description: Compensate viewmodel distortion at fov > 90 (based on code from Qrack, thanks to Andrei Drexler for the patch.) QSSM: Accept floats above and below 1 to adjust the amount of distortion and is not affected by fov. Makes weapon drawing immune to field of view settings.

entries.name: cl_gunx
entries.description: Offsets the viewmodel horizontally, with positive values moving it right and a default of 0. The applied value is clamped to the range -30 through 30.

entries.name: cl_guny
entries.description: Offsets the viewmodel vertically, with positive values moving it downward and a default of 0. The applied value is clamped to the range -30 through 30.

entries.name: cl_gunz
entries.description: cl_gunz — Offsets the viewmodel along the viewing direction, with positive values moving it forward and a default of 0. The applied value is clamped to the range -30 through 30.

entries.name: cl_idle
entries.description: Client will auto reconnect to a server (if disconnected) every "X", where X = 1 minute. cl_idle "5" will attempt to reconnect every 5 minutes after disconnect

entries.name: cl_iDrive
entries.description: Automatically cancels opposing movement keys when both are pressed simultaneously, preventing input lag or "dead zones" caused by conflicting inputs. For example, if you're holding the left movement key (A) and then press the right key (D), this feature will immediately release the A key, ensuring smooth directional transitions. Without this, both keys might cancel each other out, causing a momentary stop in movement. While similar behavior can be achieved using complex keybinding scripts, these solutions are often clunky and unreliable across different systems. Modern analog keyboards—such as those made by Wooting or Zaer—implement this behavior natively for seamless control. This feature is commonly referred to as SOCO (Simultaneous Opposing Cancel Output), and it's especially useful in fast-paced games where responsive directional movement is critical.

entries.name: cl_lightning_zadjust
entries.description: Adjusts the vertical origin of the local player’s corrected lightning beam, defaulting to 16. Values are clamped between 0 and 16 and work alongside cl_truelightning and v_viewheight.

entries.name: cl_mapshots
entries.description: Controls downloaded and cached map screenshots, defaulting to 1. Mode 0 disables them, mode 1 enables them in the Levels menu, and mode 2 also shows them during loading and console-based map changes.

entries.name: cl_mapshots_brightness
entries.description: Applies a user brightness multiplier after automatic gamma compensation when drawing mapshots, defaulting to 0.8. A value of 1 preserves the source image’s compensated brightness, while lower values dim it.

entries.name: cl_maxpitch
entries.description: Modify client-side pitch clamping. Default 90 (straight down.) Set to 80 to mimic normal quake.

entries.name: cl_maxroll
entries.description: Sets the maximum absolute client view-roll angle, defaulting to 50 degrees. Runtime use clamps the configured limit between 0 and 180 before constraining the view angle.

entries.name: cl_menucrosshair
entries.description: Display crosshair when menu is active

entries.name: cl_migration_schema
entries.description: Stores the version of the persistent CVar-migration process, defaulting to 0. The engine advances it after updating legacy settings, so users generally should not change it manually.

entries.name: cl_minpitch
entries.description: Modify client-side pitch clamping. Default -90 (straight up.) Set to -70 to mimic normal quake.

entries.name: cl_modmenu
entries.description: Enables context-sensitive menus for supported multiplayer mods, defaulting to 1. When connected to a recognized mod such as CRMod7, opening the menu can show mod-specific commands instead of the normal main menu.

entries.name: cl_movespeedkey
entries.description: The multiplier value for the player movement speeds when using the +speed command. The value from this variable is used to multiply the values in the cl_backspeed and cl_forwardspeed variables when the +speed command is used. If you set this variable to a value lower than it is you can make the player walk slower or even crawl.

entries.name: cl_muzzleflash
entries.description: Disable/enable flash when players shoot

entries.name: cl_noclip_speed
entries.description: Sets the accelerated noclip speed used while holding the jump key in a local game, defaulting to 720. It only affects a locally hosted player in noclip mode and does not alter the normal movement-speed CVars.

entries.name: cl_nocsqc
entries.description: Blocks the loading of any csqc modules (client side QC)

entries.name: cl_nolerp
entries.description: Toggle the prediction of movement of entities. This value is a reverse toggle where the values are actually reversed. When this toggle is enabled the game will not predict the movements of entities and all moving objects in the game will seem to jump from one point to another instead of moving in a smooth motion.

entries.name: cl_nopext
entries.description: Prevent autodetection of protocol extensions, so that servers fall back to only their base protocol (without needing to reconfigure the server. Requires reconnect. Keep demo recordings cross compatible

entries.name: cl_nopred
entries.description: If 0, clientside prediciton is enabled. Use iconjunction with sv_nqplayerphysics. cl_nopred 1; sv_nqplayerphysics 1 is very much the nq default

entries.name: cl_onload
entries.description: Customize the initial behavior of the game client based on user preferences stored in cl_onload. The function provides several ways to control startup behavior: basic commands like "menu" (default) to show the main menu, "console" to open the console, or "demo" for demo playback (which respects cl_demoreel settings). It also includes menu shortcuts where "browser" opens the server browser (menu_slist), "bookmarks" shows saved servers (menu_bookmarks), "save" opens the load game menu (menu_load), and "history" displays the game history (menu_history). Additionally, it supports any valid command that takes arguments, such as "connect server.com" to join a server or "exec config.cfg" to execute a configuration file. The cl_onload cvar determines which of these actions is taken when the game starts.

entries.name: cl_pitchspeed
entries.description: Keyboard movement. The speed at which the commands +lookup and +lookdown work. This command is basically used to control the speed at which the player looks up and down when using keys bound to the above mentioned commands. If you feel that player is not looking up and down fast enough you should increase this value. This variable is only used when using the keyboard and has no effect on the speed of other controllers when using a mouse or a joystick to control the player.

entries.name: cl_portpingprobe_delay
entries.description: The cl_portpingprobe_delay cvar controls the pause in milliseconds between each individual port probe when scanning for the best server port, defaulting to 0 for no delay. Setting a value like 10 or 25 throttles the probe rate, which can help avoid triggering rate-limiting or firewall rules on the server side at the cost of a longer total scan time. Suggested values from tab-completion range from 0 (fastest, no delay) up to 100 ms (most conservative), for example cl_portpingprobe_delay 25 is a reasonable middle ground. The value must be zero or positive; negative values are clamped to 0 automatically.

entries.name: cl_portpingprobe_enable
entries.description: The cl_portpingprobe_enable cvar toggles the port ping probe system on or off, defaulting to 0 (disabled); set it to 1 to enable automatic scanning of source ports for the lowest-latency connection when joining a server. When enabled, the client tests multiple random source ports before connecting and selects the one with the best round-trip time, which can meaningfully reduce ping on some network paths. Setting it back to 0 immediately aborts any in-progress probe, clears cached results, and reverts to default connection behavior. Use cl_portpingprobe_enable 1 alongside companion cvars like cl_portpingprobe_probes and cl_portpingprobe_delay to tune how many ports are tested and how aggressively they are scanned.

entries.name: cl_portpingprobe_port_probes
entries.description: Sets how many repeat measurements are taken from each finalist source port during port-ping calibration, defaulting to 5. It is clamped from 1 to 5, trading faster probing for more reliable latency measurements.

entries.name: cl_portpingprobe_probes
entries.description: The cl_portpingprobe_probes cvar controls how many random source ports are tested during a port ping probe scan, defaulting to 500 and clamped between 1 and 1000. Lower values like 50 or 100 finish quickly but may miss a better port, while higher values like 500 or 1000 are more thorough at the cost of a longer scan, for example cl_portpingprobe_probes 200 is a good balanced choice. Tab-completion suggests presets: 50 (fast test), 100 (light probe), 200 (balanced), 500 (default), and 1000 (max). The best port found across all probes is cached and used as the client's source port for the connection, so more probes generally means a better chance of finding the optimal low-ping path.

entries.name: cl_predict
entries.description: Supress QE message. Does nothing.

entries.name: cl_r2g
entries.description: Replaces the rocket model with grenade, 0 by default. (popular in deathmatch)

entries.name: cl_recordingdemo
entries.description: Print the name of the currently-recording demo

entries.name: cl_rollangle
entries.description: The angle in degrees at which the player tilts when strafing right and left. Some hardcore players set this variable to 0 in order to prevent the player from tiling when he’s moving left and right. This enables them to switch rotations during circle strafing battles without throwing off their aim. If 0, cl_rollspeed will is not applicable

entries.name: cl_rollspeed
entries.description: The speed at which the player recovers to a straight posture after tilting left or right. If you feel that the player is not recovering fast enough after strafing left and right you should set this variable to a lower value.

entries.name: cl_rot
entries.description: cl_rot is an archived client-side cvar that stores your custom spin rules for specific models so they rotate locally without any QC or server changes. Its value is a semicolon-separated list of entries in the form "ax ay az mdl1[,mdl2...]; ...", where ax ay az are degrees per second around the X/Y/Z axes (right, up, forward) and mdl is the model name exactly as model->name (for example: cl_rot "0 180 0 progs/armor.mdl; 0 90 0 progs/backpack.mdl,progs/g_shot.mdl"). You normally edit this via the rotatemodel command: rotatemodel <ax> <ay> <az> <mdl1[,mdl2...]> to add/update entries, rotatemodel list to see the current runtime list and the raw cl_rot string, rotatemodel reload/revert to re-parse cl_rot, and rotatemodel save to serialize the current runtime list back into cl_rot so it’s persisted to your config. An empty cl_rot string means no client-side rotations are applied.

entries.name: cl_screenangle
entries.description: Tilts screen left or right (Specifcally used in Blood Rails)

entries.name: cl_screenangle_speed
entries.description: The speed/smoothness screenangle rolls to each side and back

entries.name: cl_serverextension_download
entries.description: cl_serverextension_download is a server-sent command that informs your client about the server's file downloading capabilities. When a server sends cl_serverextension_download 1, it signals that it supports the DarkPlaces/FTEQW style download protocol, allowing your client to request missing files (like maps or models) directly from the server. You don't need to use this command yourself; it's part of the automatic handshake between your client and the server to determine if server-side downloads are possible.

entries.name: cl_shownet
entries.description: Toggle the display of information about network packet transmissions. This toggle was basically used during the game’s development to gather information about network packets.

entries.name: cl_sidespeed
entries.description: The speed at which the player moves left and right. You can set this variable to a much higher value such as 500 just in case you join a server on which the administrator allows the players to move at a faster speed.

entries.name: cl_smartspawn
entries.description: Spawning in mutliplayer with +attack is bad, you may accidently shoot a teammate. A value of 1 will not allow you spawn using +attack so as to train you to use spacebar

entries.name: cl_smoothcam_cubic
entries.description: Enables Hermite-style cubic angle interpolation for live smooth-camera observer views, defaulting to 0. It uses cubic interpolation only when a healthy aligned sample history is available and falls back to linear interpolation otherwise.

entries.name: cl_truelightning
entries.description: Toggle lightning gun beam appearing to be straight ahead at all times.

entries.name: cl_upspeed
entries.description: The speed at which the player moves up and down. You can set this variable to a much higher value such as 500 just in case you join a server on which the administrator allows the players to move at a faster speed.

entries.name: cl_voip_autogain
entries.description: Attempts to normalize your voice levels to a standard level. Useful for lazy people, but interferes with voice activation levels.

entries.name: cl_voip_bitrate
entries.description: For codecs with non-specific bitrates, this specifies the target bitrate to use.

entries.name: cl_voip_capturingvol
entries.description: Volume multiplier applied while capturing, to avoid your audio from being heard by others. Does not affect game volume when other speak (minimum of cl_voip_capturingvol and cl_voip_ducking is used).

entries.name: cl_voip_codec
entries.description: 0: speex(@11khz). 1: raw. 2: opus. 3: speex(@8khz). 4: speex(@16). 5:speex(@32).

entries.name: cl_voip_codecs
entries.description: The cl_voip_codecs command lists all the audio codecs that the game client knows about for Voice over IP (VoIP) communication. It checks the system to see which codecs are actually supported and available for use, determining if the necessary libraries (like Speex or Opus) are present. Finally, it prints a list of these codecs to the console, indicating whether each one is fully available, only usable for decoding (receiving voice), only usable for encoding (sending voice), or completely unavailable.

entries.name: cl_voip_ducking
entries.description: Scales game audio by this much when someone is talking to you. Does not affect your speaker volume when you speak (minimum of cl_voip_capturingvol and cl_voip_ducking is used).

entries.name: cl_voip_micamp
entries.description: Amplifies your microphone when using voip.

entries.name: cl_voip_noisefilter
entries.description: Enable the use of the noise cancelation filter.

entries.name: cl_voip_play
entries.description: Enables voip playback. Value is a volume scaler.

entries.name: cl_voip_send
entries.description: Enable sending of voice (voip) to the server.

entries.name: cl_voip_showmeter
entries.description: Shows your speech volume above the standard hud. 0=hide, 1=show when transmitting, 2=ignore voice-activation disable

entries.name: cl_voip_test
entries.description: Sends voice-over-ip data to the server whenever it is set.

entries.name: cl_voip_vad_delay
entries.description: Keeps sending voice data for this many seconds after voice activation would normally stop

entries.name: cl_voip_vad_threshhold
entries.description: This is the threshhold for voice-activation-detection when sending voip data

entries.name: cl_warncmd
entries.description: The cvar cl_warncmd, internally known as cmd_warncmd, primarily manages the client's communication protocol with game servers. When enabled (set to "1", its default), it instructs the client to avoid auto-detecting and using any advanced protocol extensions the server might support, forcing a fallback to the server's basic protocol. This behavior can enhance compatibility or stability without requiring server-side reconfiguration, though a client reconnect is necessary for changes to this setting to take effect.

entries.name: cl_web_download_url
entries.description: Web download URL for maps/etc. This is a much faster method of downloading than from servers. If blank it will only try from the connected server

entries.name: cl_web_download_url2
entries.description: Second web download URL for maps/etc. This is a much faster method of downloading than from servers. If blank it will only try from the connected server

entries.name: cl_wheel_order
entries.default: shotgun axe lg rl gl sng ng ssg prox laser mjolnir lavang lavasng multigl multirl plasma
entries.summary: Sets weapon-wheel order using a space-separated list of weapon IDs.
entries.description: Saved to config. Supply weapon IDs in the order you want them on the weapon wheel, such as axe shotgun lg. Unknown IDs and duplicates are ignored. An empty value uses the wheel definition's default order; the built-in default also preserves the default order supplied by a custom wheel definition.

entries.name: cl_yawspeed
entries.description: The speed at which the +left and +right commands make the player turn left and right. This command is basically used to control the speed at which the player looks left and right when using keys bound to the above mentioned commands. If you feel that player is not looking left and right fast enough you should increase this value. This variable is only used when using the keyboard and has no effect on the speed of other controllers when using a mouse or a joystick to control the player.

entries.name: clear
entries.description: Clears the console screen of any text.

entries.name: clearhistory
entries.description: Clears the in-memory console command history. It also deletes the saved history file so old commands do not return after restarting.

entries.name: clearlocs
entries.description: QW LOC Creator: clear added locations to start over

entries.name: cmd
entries.description: Send a command directly to the server.

entries.name: cmdline
entries.description: Display the parameters used on the command line to start the game. With this command you can take a look at the parameters that were used to start the game. If you started the game with the command ‘game.exe -nosound +map mymap +volume 0.7‘, this command would give you output like ‘ -nosound +map mymap +volume 0.7‘.

entries.name: cmdlist
entries.description: Outputs an alphabetized list of all commands. If substring is present, lists only commands that start with substring.

entries.name: cmdtoggle
entries.description: A command to toggle between two existing commands. Example: bind "n" "cmdtoggle ready notready"

entries.name: color
entries.description: QSSM now allows random colors with color x x. Set the color for the player’s shirt and pants.  If you use this command without any parameters it will report the current shirt and pants color for the player. If you use this command with a single parameter for the color both, the shirt and pants colors will match. If you use two different parameters for this command you will be able to set the shirt and pants colors individually. The available colors in the game range from 0 to 13. All colors above that just make the player look blue. color 0xff00ff 0x00ff00

entries.name: com_protocolname
entries.description: The game name used for dpmaster queries

entries.name: con_autohint
entries.description: Enables inline console completion hints, defaulting to 1. Disabling it also suppresses the ghosted chat-word suggestion shown on cl_chatmode console lines.

entries.name: con_clear_input_on_toggle
entries.description: Controls whether toggling the console erases the current input line, defaulting to 0. Enabling it gives the console Qrack-style clean-input behavior whenever it is opened or closed.

entries.name: con_coldirection
entries.description: direction of multiple tab match columns if mutiple columns used. if 0, top to bottom, if 1 left to right. see con_colmax

entries.name: con_colmax
entries.description: print tab matches on multiple columns if possible. <=0 = no limit,  >0 = maximum number of columns

entries.name: con_cursorcolor
entries.description: Change the color of the blinking cusor in the console (0=white, 1=red, 2=gold)

entries.name: con_filter
entries.description: Filter no weapon, ammo pickups, and other useless notifications in multiplayer from appearing in console

entries.name: con_logcenterprint
entries.description: If 1, centerprint messages will be logged to the console in sp/coop. If 2, they will also be logged in deathmatch. Default 1. condump or -condebug can write the console log to a file.

entries.name: con_mm1mute
entries.description: If 1, if you are on a team in a match you will only hear the message mode sound for say_team, not say

entries.name: con_notifydiscord
entries.description: Add a webhook to this cvar and you will get a notification for con_notifylist

entries.name: con_notifyfade
entries.description: Fade console messages with opacity

entries.name: con_notifyfadetime
entries.description: Fade console messages with opacity. How long the fade lasts

entries.name: con_notifylines
entries.description: Number of notify messages (chat, \"you got the nails\", ..) drawn on the screen.

entries.name: con_notifylist
entries.description: When these words are mentioned in the console, the client will flash your attention if in the background. Your name may be long, and people refer to you by your short name

entries.name: con_notifyposition
entries.description: Vertical position of notifylines, ie: chat. Positive values will move the position down screen.

entries.name: con_notifytime
entries.description: The time in seconds that messages are displayed on the screen. The default value is usually adequate. If it is desired that messages should stay on the screen for a long time then the value should be increased. If this variable is set to a negative number the message will not be displayed on the screen but instead they will just appear in the console.

entries.name: con_savehistory
entries.description: Controls whether console command history is persisted to disk between sessions, defaulting to 1. Setting it to 0 disables persistent history and the disk-backed console portion of the history viewer.

entries.name: con_typing
entries.description: Enables the console indicator showing which connected players are currently typing, defaulting to 1. It is normally suppressed during demo playback unless the menu’s live-preview system is demonstrating the feature.

entries.name: -condebug
entries.description: Save console log to "qconsole.log". SDL2 builds no longer generate stdout.txt/stderr.txt

entries.name: condump
entries.description: Writes the console buffer to condump.txt.

entries.name: connect
entries.description: QSSM add: Tab to autocomplete server history, connect last to connect to the last server connected to. Connect to a game server. This command can be used to connect to a server by it’s IP address, DNS hostname, or the server’s name if the server is on the local network. By default the port that this command will connect to is 26000. If you want to connect to a server which is using a different port you will have to set the port variable to the port number that the server is using in order to connect. If you want to find all of the servers on your local network you might want to use the slist command.

entries.name: -consize
entries.description: console buffer size can now be set.  The command line option "-consize" allows you to specify the buffer size in kilobytes.  For reference, fitzquake's default buffer size is 64k, and glquake's is 16k.  16k is also the smallest size fitzquake will allow you to set.  Note: this buffer lives in the heap, so if you want to have a HUGE buffer, you might need to increase -heapsize also. default is 65536

entries.name: contrast
entries.description: It may be a useful alternative to the existing gamma control for laptops in a bright environment, etc. Raising contrast gives less of a gray/washed out look than raising gamma, but at a disadvantage: colors near white get clipped to white.

entries.name: coop
entries.description: Toggle the usage of the cooperative game mode. The cooperative game mode is used by the server to allow a group of players to cooperatively play the game against the monsters just like a single-player game. This mode is the opposite of the deathmatch game mode where all of the players play against each other.

entries.name: crosshair
entries.description: Sets types of crosshairs. Changed the deault '+' to a '•'. It uses the default character from conchars and can be adjusted with scr_crosshairscale. Values: 0 - no crosshair, 1 - white, 2 - colored (Default: 1) -- See cl_damagehue "2" for blinking crosshair on damage. Values up to 7 for different options

entries.name: crx_ignorethis
entries.description: Mute various invalid stuffcmds

entries.name: csqc_progcrc
entries.description: csqc_progcrc is an internal command historically sent by the server providing a CRC (Cyclic Redundancy Check) checksum for the Client-Side QuakeC (CSQC) program file. The client could compare this checksum against its local file to verify integrity and ensure it wasn't modified or corrupted, which was important for cheat prevention. This specific command is often ignored now, with integrity checks sometimes using different hash methods provided in the serverinfo.

entries.name: csqc_progname
entries.description: csqc_progsize is an internal command historically sent by the server to inform the client of the exact size, in bytes, of the required Client-Side QuakeC (CSQC) program file. This size information was used, along with other checks, to verify the client had the correct version of the CSQC code. Players don't typically interact with this command, as its function is now largely handled within the serverinfo string.

entries.name: csqc_progsize
entries.description: csqc_progsize is an internal command historically sent by the server to inform the client of the exact size, in bytes, of the required Client-Side QuakeC (CSQC) program file. This size information was used, along with other checks, to verify the client had the correct version of the CSQC code. Players don't typically interact with this command, as its function is now largely handled within the serverinfo string.

entries.name: -current
entries.description: start game with current desktop resolution settings of width, height, refreshrate, bpp, and fullscreen

entries.name: cvarlist
entries.description: Outputs an alphabetized list of all console variables. If substring is present, lists only cvars that start with substring.

entries.name: cycle
entries.description: Cycle a cvar through a list of values. Note: this command will get stuck on a list that contains the same value more than once, such as "cycle blah 1 2 1 3". If you're doing anything that complex you can just use aliases. See toggle.

entries.name: deathmatch
entries.description: Toggle the deathmatch game mode.  It is recommended to use the setting of 3 when setting up a public server. Most people don’t like to play in free-for-all games where the weapons disappear. When playing a one-on-one match most people use the original setting of 1 because it allows for a new type of a strategy which deals with the control of crucial weapons on the map. The setting of 2 is never used anymore, it’s a left over setting from the old days of Doom deathmatch games.

entries.name: -dedicated
entries.description: Starts Quake ready to be a dedicated server for up to <n> players. If you do not specify a number <n> after -listen it will default to 16 (changed in qssm). The maximum allowed value is 16. A dedicated Quake server stays in text mode. This is the Quake console with most commands still available; those that make no sense (like vid_mode) are ommitted.

entries.name: demos
entries.description: Play demos which have been queued with the startdemos command.

entries.name: developer
entries.description: Toggle the use of developer mode and the display of internal game information. If this toggle is enabled the game will output a lot of developer mode information and internal game information. This mode is used by developers to track the progress of the game and to find any bugs. The information presented by this command is not very useful to a casual player that’s why this toggle is disabled by default.

entries.name: devstats
entries.description: If 1, prints various the current and peak values of various stats that change over time, such as packetsize, and edicts. Note: even if devstats is set to 0, fitzquake will keep track of peak values so when you turn it on, the peaks are accurate. Devstats display scale follows console text scale. Default 0.

entries.name: dir
entries.description: Command is designed to help you list files within the game's directories that match specific patterns you provide. This can be particularly useful for finding files, checking the contents of directories, or verifying the presence of game assets. Use * to match any number of characters and ? to match a single character. For example, *.txt will list all TXT files. To search for all files with a name that starts with config, regardless of their extension, you would use: config*. You can use the ? wildcard to substitute for the single unknown character in the filename. In this case, you would use level?.cfg as your search pattern: level?.cfg. ls * will list all the files. Examples: "*.pak *.txt", "*", "pak1.pak", "?onfig.cfg". Same as: ls, dir, flocate, which

entries.name: disablecsqc
entries.description: While disablecsqc is registered as a client command and calls a function to disable CSQC (Host_DisableCSQC_f), it doesn't appear to be used as the signal during the initial client-server negotiation in the same way enablecsqc is. It's more likely called internally based on other conditions (e.g., the server indicating it doesn't support CSQC, or the user changing a relevant cvar like cl_csqc_enable to 0) or potentially used as a manual command (cmd disablecsqc) to force CSQC off on the client, which might cause issues if the server expects it to be on.

entries.name: disconnect
entries.description: Disconnect from a game server. This command is primarily used to disconnect from a game server. However, this command can also be used to stop a single-player game or to stop the playback of startup demos.

entries.name: download
entries.description: "download aerowalk.bsp" will attempt downloading using cl_web_download_url. Can also downloads .lit, .wav, .loc". 'download ctf' or 'download ra' will download the client files for those mods

entries.name: echo
entries.description: Print text on the console.  If this command is used without parameters it will print a blank line on the console. If parameters are provided for this command they will be printed to the console without any alterations. The character “ cannot be printed using this command. Also some characters such as (, ), {, }, : will have a heading and a trailing space when printed so a string like ‘{this(is:a)test}‘ would be printed as ‘ { this ( is : a ) test } ‘. Also the character combination // starts a comment line and anything after those characters will not be printed to the console.

entries.name: edgefriction
entries.description: The amount of imaginary friction when standing on an edge. This variable controls the amount of friction when the player is standing on an edge. This variable was necessary in order to prevent players from slipping off edges and falling to their doom.

entries.name: edict
entries.description: Display information about a game entity. This command will output all of the information about a given entity object on the map. This command is used by map makers to get information about the objects on their maps. Some of the information that describes entities is their size, their position in the world, the model file that represents them, if they are solid objects, if they are visible objects, the function that they execute when activated, the angle which they are facing, or their type. Entities are objects such as the player, an ammo box, a door, a monster, or virtually any object which moves or is not part of the map.

entries.name: edictcount
entries.description: Display the number of entities on the map. This command will show the total number of entities on the map, it will also show how many entities are still active, how many the player can actually see, how many the player can actually interact with, and how many are solid to the player.

entries.name: edicts
entries.description: Display information about all of the entities on the map.  This command will print out screens of information about all of the entities on the map. The information printed out is the same as the information from the edict command.

entries.name: enablecsqc
entries.description: enablecsqc isn't really a command for users to execute directly. It functions as an internal signal sent automatically by the client to the server during connection. This signal tells the server, "This client supports and wants to use Client-Side QuakeC," allowing the server to enable CSQC features for that specific client if the server also supports it.

entries.name: entdump
entries.description: Copy .ent from currently loaded map and copy to id1 folder

entries.name: entities
entries.description: Display a list of all the visible entities on the map. This command will print out a list of all the entities that are currently visible to the player. The list will contain information about the location of the entity on the map, it’s orientation, and the model that is used to represent it. This command should be very useful to map developers who want to measure the amount of objects that a player can see at the same time from a given location. The lower the number of objects that the player can see the lower the number of entity packets that the server has to send to the client thus the improved network performance. If too many entities are visible at the same time, some entities will not be rendered on the player’s screen. Each line of the put put gives information about the location and filename of the model, the current frame currently being displayed, the location of the model on the map, and the angle that the model is facing on the map.

entries.name: exec
entries.description: Execute a console script file. This command is used to execute a script file which contains console commands. All lines in a script file will be executed. If lines are prefixed with the // character combination all text after that will be treated as a comment and will not be executed. Console scripts can have any extension, but the extensions .cfg and .rc are the most popular. Scripts can be executed by their filename or by providing a path relative to the current path and then the filename. Also using the character \ or / is permissible for separating the path names. The character combination of .. is used to signify one directory higher than the current directory and can be used in a relative path. The current path can be determined with the use of the path command in order to determine the relative paths to other script files. Usually the current path is quake/id1/. Absolute paths such as c:\quake or d:/games/quake/ctf cannot be used by this command.

entries.name: exectrigger
entries.description: Mute various invalid stuffcmds

entries.name: external_ents
entries.description: Added support for loading external entity files

entries.name: external_ents_dir
entries.description: Set a directory where external ents will be loaded from. .ents are loaded from maps directory so you can set external_ents_dir "ctf" and it will load the .ent from that directory for the map instead of the .ent that is in the maps dir.

entries.name: external_lits_dir
entries.description: The gl_loadlitfiles cvar controls colored lighting file loading with four modes: 0 disables all .lit files, 1 loads only standard .lit files from the game directory, 2 prefers external .lit files from the external_lits_dir directory with fallback to standard files, and 3 randomly chooses between external and standard .lit files for variety. To use external .lit files, set external_lits_dir to your custom lighting directory (e.g. "custom_lighting") and gl_loadlitfiles to 2 or 3. This allows you to organize custom lighting files separately while maintaining compatibility with standard .lit files as a backup.

entries.name: external_vis
entries.description: Support for external vis files.

entries.name: -f
entries.description: Alias for fullscreen, see fullscreen

entries.name: f_status
entries.description: This sets the flag status for CTF on crx. Values are on or off

entries.name: find
entries.description: Searches for commands/cvar names for the given substring

entries.name: -fitz
entries.description: To disable some changes added to Fitzquake in Quakespasm

entries.name: flocate
entries.description: Command is designed to help you list files within the game's directories that match specific patterns you provide. This can be particularly useful for finding files, checking the contents of directories, or verifying the presence of game assets. Use * to match any number of characters and ? to match a single character. For example, *.txt will list all TXT files. To search for all files with a name that starts with config, regardless of their extension, you would use: config*. You can use the ? wildcard to substitute for the single unknown character in the filename. In this case, you would use level?.cfg as your search pattern: level?.cfg. ls * will list all the files. Examples: "*.pak *.txt", "*", "pak1.pak", "?onfig.cfg". Same as: ls, dir, flocate, which

entries.name: flush
entries.description: Empty the game memory cache of all game information and objects. This command is usually used by developers to flush the memory of all game information and objects to test if the mechanism which handles the loading of the necessary files into memory works properly. Sometimes the game cache can become filled with unnecessary information and may need to be flushed manually. This is usually not necessary since the game automatically flushes all the data between every map.

entries.name: fly
entries.description: Force fly mode to be enabled or disabled. (e.g. "fly 1" will enable fly mode regardless of its current state.)

entries.name: fog
entries.description: Sets global fog, for testing purposes. All four values should be in the range 0...1. Set density to 0 to disable fog. Black fog [fog 0.05 0.0 0.0 0.0], white fog [fog 0.03 1.0 1.0 1.0], light brown [fog 0.03 0.7 0.3 0.3]

entries.name: fov
entries.description: The size in degrees of the field-of-vision that the player sees. The minimum value for this variable is 10, the maximum value is 170. The Players can use this variable to enlarge or shrink the amount of space that the player sees to his left and right. By default the player sees 45 degrees to his left and 45 to his right, thus making his complete field of vision 90 degrees. If the field-of-vision is enlarged the player will see more area and objects will appear further away from the player. If the field-of-vision is decreased the player will see less area and objects will appear closer to the player. This command has been used by many players to create aliases which enable the player to zoom onto far away objects by shrinking the field-of-vision.

entries.name: fov_adapt
entries.description: Implemented Hor+ style field of view (FOV) scaling, useful for widescreen resolutions. Configured by new cvar fov_adapt: set it to 1 and your fov will be scaled automatically according to the resolution. Enabled by default. In short, it ensures that players on widescreen monitors see more to the sides (peripheral vision) rather than having the top and bottom of the view cut off.

entries.name: fraglimit
entries.description: The amount of kills necessary to proceed to the next map in deathmatch games. This variable is usually set by server administrators to allow the cycling of maps after a player receives a certain number of kills on that map. A good number to set the fraglimit to is 30 because it allows the players to play for a little while before changing the map, you might also wish to set the timelimit variable to 20. Settings the variable too high or too low will result in annoying the players with short maps or boring them with maps that never seem to end.

entries.name: -fsaa
entries.description: Antialiasing (FSAA) support (command line: -fsaa x, where x can be 0, 2, 4, 8).

entries.name: fui
entries.description: fui (Full User Info) is an internal command sent by the game server to the client, usually during connection or when a player's full details change significantly. It completely replaces the user information string (containing details like name, colors, and custom settings) for a specific player slot with the new data provided by the server. Like fullserverinfo, this is part of the engine's communication protocol and is not a command players typically enter manually.

entries.name: -fullscreen
entries.description: Start in fullscreen mode

entries.name: fullserverinfo
entries.description: fullserverinfo is an internal command used by the game server during the connection process. Its purpose is to transmit the complete set of server configuration details, such as map name, player limits, and game rules, to your client. As a player, you typically do not need to use this command directly, as it's handled automatically by the engine when you join a server.

entries.name: game
entries.description: Loads a mod. See command mods. Same as gamedir command

entries.name: -game
entries.description: Set a different game directory on start. Quakespasm allows loading new games (mods) on the fly in console with "game gamename"

entries.name: gamecfg
entries.description: gamecfg is a general-purpose console variable for the QuakeC game code, and its specific meaning is defined by the mod being played.

entries.name: gamecontrollerdb_reload
entries.description: Reloads SDL game-controller mappings from the available controller databases. It attempts to reopen the currently selected controller after refreshing the mappings.

entries.name: gamedir
entries.description: Loads a mod. See command mods. Same as game command

entries.name: games
entries.description: Lists all child folders of quake directory which contain either a progs.dat or a pak file. See command game. Same as mods command.

entries.name: gamma
entries.description: Brighten or darken the screen to compensate for differences between monitors. This is now supported by using your video card's gamma support (works on 3dfx cards, too! I think.) Just like in winquake, values less than 1 are brighter and values greater than one are darker. Default 1.

entries.name: give
entries.description: Gives you armour. If value is between 0 and 100, armortype is green. If value is between 101 and 150, armortype is yellow. If value is between 151 and 200, armortype is red. 1-9 weapons (9 - laser canon), r - rockets, c - cells, n - nails, s - shells, h - health, l - lava nails (rogue), m - multi rockets (rogue), p - plasma ammo (rogue) - Example: give 1;give 2;give 3;give 4;give 5;give 6;give 7;give 8, give s 100;give n 100; give r 100;give c 100, give a 200. impulse 9 will give all weapons as well -- QSSM you can now use readable names like give shells 100, give rockets 50, give health 250, give armor red, give quad, give keys, give sigils, or specific weapons like give ssg, give rl, give mjolnir, plus macros like give weapons (all weapons + ammo) and give all (complete loadout). It syncs HUD ammo so the status bar updates, prints a clear “Gave …” confirmation to the client/console, adds CompleteGive so give <TAB> suggests valid items and common values (e.g., armor colors, 100/150/200/999), and precaches all the item/powerup sounds used by give so the feedback audio always plays correctly.

entries.name: gl_affinemodels
entries.description: The gl_affinemodels console variable controls whether the OpenGL renderer attempts to replicate the characteristic texture warping seen in the original software-rendered Quake, specifically for alias models (players, monsters, weapons). By default, gl_affinemodels is set to "0", causing these models to be rendered using standard, mathematically accurate perspective-correct texture mapping. Setting it to "1", however, activates an alternative rendering path, likely implemented in the r_aliafffs.c file, which mimics the look of affine texture mapping. This intentionally disables perspective correction for alias model textures, making them appear closer to their software-rendered counterparts, often desired for visual nostalgia or stylistic preference.

entries.name: gl_alias_instancing
entries.description: Enables the portable instanced rendering path for repeated opaque alias models, defaulting to 1. Unsupported or ineligible render states automatically fall back to the ordinary per-entity drawing path.

entries.name: gl_bmodel_instancing
entries.description: Enables instanced rendering for repeated opaque brush models, defaulting to 1. It requires compatible GLSL/VBO support and automatically falls back when models have dynamic lighting, translucency, effects, grass, or unsupported render states

entries.name: gl_caustics
entries.description: gl_caustics controls the rendering of light patterns that appear on surfaces beneath water, simulating how light refracts and focuses. Enabling this feature adds shimmering, realistic light effects to underwater scenes, enhancing visual immersion. However, rendering caustics requires additional computational resources and may impact performance on some systems.

entries.name: gl_clear
entries.description: gl_clear "1" tells the OpenGL renderer to clear the screen (color and depth buffers) before drawing each new frame. It's the default and generally recommended setting for robust rendering, although setting it to "0" might offer a marginal performance boost on some systems at the risk of visual artifacts

entries.name: gl_cshift_contents_auto
entries.description: Generates liquid color shifts from the map’s liquid textures, defaulting to 0. Mode 1 fills in colors missing from worldspawn data, while mode 2 forces sampled colors even when the map supplies its own values.

entries.name: gl_cshiftpercent
entries.description: Global opacity/transparency percent of screen shift color change for ALL cshifts

entries.name: gl_cshiftpercent_bonus
entries.description: Opacity/transparency percent of screen shift color change when a bonus is achieved

entries.name: gl_cshiftpercent_contents
entries.description: Opacity/transparency percent of screen shift color change when in water/slime/lava

entries.name: gl_cshiftpercent_damage
entries.description: Opacity/transparency percent of screen shift color change when taking damage

entries.name: gl_cshiftpercent_dead
entries.description: Opacity/transparency percent of screen shift color change when you dead

entries.name: gl_cshiftpercent_powerup
entries.description: Opacity/transparency percent of screen shift color change when you have pent/quad/ring

entries.name: gl_cull
entries.description: Toggle the use of internal OpenGL functions for removing covered objects. When this toggle is enabled the game will depend on the OpenGL driver to use it’s culling functions to remove certain objects from the calculations because they are covered up and would not be seen anyways. It is a good idea to leave this toggle enabled because it will increase rendering performance.

entries.name: gl_describetexturemodes
entries.description: Lists all texturemodes.

entries.name: gl_enemycolor
entries.description: Google: "color picker" to find HEX RGB value and then prefix with 0x. 0xff00ff = magenta, 0x00ff00 = bright green. Using player color values (0-13) set a color that will be on ALL enemies, regardless of their scoreboard color. gl_enemycolor "12" makes all enemies yellow. gl_enemycolor "0x00ff00" for bright green. Type color in console for examples. Best used with gl_overbright_models "2"

entries.name: gl_farclip
entries.description: Sets the distance of OpenGL's far clipping plane. Note that the skybox will always be drawn somewhat closer than this value. Default 16384. Set to 4096 to mimic glquake.

entries.name: gl_finish
entries.description: Toggle the calling of the gl_finish() OpenGL function after each rendered frame.

entries.name: gl_flashblend
entries.description: Toggle the rendering of a ball of light around dynamic light sources. When this toggle is enabled every dynamic light source will have a sphere of light surrounding it. When this toggle is disabled the light sources will not have the ball of light around them and lighting will be displayed properly on walls, just like in WinQuake. When this toggle is enabled there will be a slight decrease i

entries.name: gl_fullbrights
entries.description: Toggle supported textures displaying in full brightness regardless of the surrounding lighting. Not to be confused with gl_fullbright, which sets all textures to 100% brightness. Set to 0 to disable fullbrights. Default 1.

entries.name: gl_info
entries.description: Displays opengl info which was previously displayed during initialization: vendor, renderer, version, and extensions

entries.name: gl_laserpoint
entries.description: Add a laser beam to the crosshair that adjusts to view height, variable to how close you are to object. A value of 2 only adds a light with no wall dot

entries.name: gl_laserpoint_alpha
entries.description: Transparency for laser line. Dot on all configured in r_particledesc cfg "r_part laserpoint"

entries.name: gl_lightning_alpha
entries.description: Adjust transparency of lighting bolt to player does not get blinded in fights. Values: 1 - full alpha, default, 0 - full transparnecy. Example: gl_lightning_alpha .5 will display half transparency. (Default: 1)   Add arg 2 and 3 for bolt1 and bolt3

entries.name: gl_load24bit
entries.description: Enable loading of external 24bit textures placed in id1/textures or gamedir/textures. QSSM: A value of 2 will load 24bit for all but floors/walls.

entries.name: gl_load24bit_hud
entries.description: Disable external HUD images for mods or separate from other external images

entries.name: gl_load24bit_skins
entries.description: If player skins in textures as player.mdl_0 they auto load, toggle this to stop loading

entries.name: gl_loadlitfiles
entries.description: Enable or disable loading of external .lit files for colored lighting

entries.name: gl_max_size
entries.description: Now defaults to 0. If 0, textures will be as large as the hardware allows. Positive values can be used to impose a limit smaller than the hardware's reported maximum. In QSSM this only applies to walls/floors. Negative values add greyscale.

entries.name: gl_motion_blur
entries.description: gl_motion_blur is a console variable that controls a post-processing motion blur effect that creates a trailing effect by blending the current frame with the previous frame to simulate motion blur, giving the game a more cinematic appearance during movement. The cvar accepts float values from 0.0 to 0.95, where 0.0 disables the effect completely, and higher values (up to 0.95) create increasingly stronger blur effects by controlling the alpha blending between the current and previous frame textures. When enabled, the system maintains a texture buffer of the previous frame and blends it with the current frame using OpenGL's blending functions, creating a ghosting effect that trails behind moving objects and camera movements. The implementation automatically manages texture memory allocation, handles non-power-of-two texture sizes, and applies the blur effect after the main scene rendering but before view scaling, with the alpha value being clamped to prevent excessive blurring that could make the game unplayable. Screen Tearing: Motion blur can help mask screen tearing by making the visual artifacts less noticeable. When screen tearing occurs, the motion blur effect can help smooth out the visual discontinuity between the torn frames, making the tearing less jarring to the eye Lower Refresh Rate Monitors: Motion blur can be particularly beneficial on monitors with lower refresh rates (like 60Hz) because it helps create the illusion of smoother motion. When you have fewer frames per second, motion blur can fill in the gaps between frames, making movement appear more fluid than it actually is. However, there are important caveats: Motion blur is not a true solution to these problems - it's more of a visual band-aid.

entries.name: gl_nocolors
entries.description: If you set gl_nocolors to 1 (or any non-zero value), the player model will then be drawn using its default skin texture without any player-specific colors applied.

entries.name: gl_overbright
entries.description: This variable controls overbright lighting on the world polygons. (For lighting on models, use gl_overbright_models.) If 1, overbright will be enabled and lighting will resemble software Quake. If 0, overbright will be disabled and lighting will resemble GLQuake. Default 1.

entries.name: gl_overbright_models
entries.description: If 1 (qss default), models will be rendered using 2x overbrightening and will appear at roughly the same brightness as they do in software quake, which is noticably brighter than the default fitzquake / glquake appearance. Default 1. Set to 0 to mimic glquake (and speed things up if your card doesn't support texture combiners or multitexture.)

entries.name: gl_picmip
entries.description: The level of detailed for textures used on walls. You can use this variable to lower the texture detail used on walls thus increasing the game’s performance.

entries.name: gl_playermip
entries.description: The level of detail for texures used on player models.  If you are experiancing a noticable slowdown during multiplayer games when a lot of players appear on the screen at the same time you might need to increase this variable in order to shrink the textures for the player models. You will lose a lot of detail but at least your name will be faster. The recommended setting for this variable is 2.

entries.name: gl_polyblend
entries.description: Toggle the use of pallet color blending and flashing effects. When this toggle is enabled the player’s screen will change color when the player is hurt or when he’s submersed in water. If you wish to disable the color changing effects you can disable this toggle. If you disable this toggle you might find it hard to notice when you are being hurt because your screen will not change color to the usual red to alert you. QSSM: Added a value of 2 that only applies to sceen edges

entries.name: gl_powerupshells
entries.description: The gl_powerupshells variable determines how powerup effects are visually represented. A value of 0 disables the effect entirely, while 1 enables a standard glowing shell around the player model, using animated textures for a dynamic look. Setting it to 2 focuses on enhancing lighting effects, providing a subtle glow or light intensity on the player model instead of a full shell, offering a less intrusive visual cue for active powerups.

entries.name: gl_powerupshells_alpha
entries.description: “intensity” knob for colored powerup shells and their lighting. Low values give a very subtle glow while higher values quickly ramp up to a strong, saturated effect

entries.name: gl_smoothmodels
entries.description: Toggle the smoothing of textures used for models.

entries.name: gl_subdivide_size
entries.description: The value used to divide the sky into individual brushes. The sky is dynamically divided into individual brushes by the game. This variable controls the size of the individual brushes. It is a good idea to set this variable to 256 in order to limit the number of brushes used for the sky thus increasing the game’s performance.

entries.name: gl_teamcolor
entries.description: Google: "color picker" to find HEX RGB value and then prefix with 0x. 0xff00ff = magenta, 0x00ff00 = bright green.
