Using player color values (0-13) set a color that will be on ALL enemies, regardless of their scoreboard color. gl_teamcolor "12" makes all enemies yellow. gl_teamcolor "0x00ff00" for bright green. Type color in console for examples. Best used with gl_overbright_models "2"

entries.name: gl_texture_anisotropy
entries.description: Controls the amount of anisotropy in texture filtering. If 1 or less than 1, texture filtering is normal (isotropic.) If greater than 1, increasing degrees of anisotropic filtering are used, up to the hardware maximum. Set value to 2 for 2x anisotropic, 4 for 4x, etc. Default 1 [on]. Value choices: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Anisotropic filtering is a texture filtering technique that significantly improves the clarity and sharpness of textures viewed at oblique angles, which is exactly what happens when you look at distant surfaces in a 3D game

entries.name: gl_texturemode
entries.description: The mode used for rendering textures.  It is best to leave this variable at the default setting because this is the setting that gives the higher level of performance. You might however want to experiment with other modes to achieve a level of detail for distant textures. GL_LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR: Trilinear interpolation. Highest quality, lowest performance. [glquake-like] , GL_LINEAR_MIPMAP_NEAREST: Bilinear interpolation. [for glquake], GL_LINEAR: No blending. [a weird one to choose], GL_NEAREST_MIPMAP_LINEAR: GL_NEAREST but with even more quality for far objects. [winquake-like], GL_NEAREST_MIPMAP_NEAREST: GL_NEAREST but with a bit more quality for far objects. [winquake-like], GL_NEAREST: Point sampled (software-like). Lowest quality, highest performance. [a bit shimmery]

entries.name: gl_triplebuffer
entries.description: Toggle the use of triple buffering for video modes that support it.  If this toggle is enabled the game will try to use triple buffering for the video modes that support this feature. Triple buffering will increase the level of performance of the game but at the cost of video memory.

entries.name: gl_waterfog
entries.description: Selects the underwater fog algorithm, defaulting to 0 for disabled. Mode 1 uses linear fog and mode 2 uses exponential fog, subject to liquid contents and r_fogalpha.

entries.name: gl_waterfog_density
entries.description: Controls the strength of client-generated underwater fog, defaulting to 0.5. Values range from 0 for clear water through 1 for maximum density.

entries.name: gl_zfix
entries.description: Flickering is most likely bmodel/world z-fighting, which the original software renderer was immune to but GL engines are not. Setting "gl_zfix 1" enables a workaround which should fix the flickering, with some small side effects (you can see a thin seam around some secret wall panels, etc.)

entries.name: -glslgamma
entries.description: Explicitly prefers the GLSL gamma-correction path. This overrides the engine’s normal decision to use hardware gamma in some configurations.

entries.name: god
entries.description: Force godmode to be enabled or disabled. (e.g. "god 1" will enable godmode regardless of its current state.)

entries.name: goto
entries.description: Moves the calling cooperative player to a safe location near another living player. It is unavailable in deathmatch, during transitions, or when no suitable destination can be found.

entries.name: gyro_calibration_x
entries.description: Gyro drift calibration offsets for each axis. Set automatically by the in-game calibration routine; not normally edited by hand.

entries.name: gyro_calibration_y
entries.description: Gyro drift calibration offsets for each axis. Set automatically by the in-game calibration routine; not normally edited by hand.

entries.name: gyro_calibration_z
entries.description: Gyro drift calibration offsets for each axis. Set automatically by the in-game calibration routine; not normally edited by hand.

entries.name: gyro_enable
entries.description: Enables gyroscope aiming on supported controllers (DualSense, DualShock 4, Switch Pro). Gyro input is added on top of stick aiming.

entries.name: gyro_mode
entries.description: Controls when gyro is active. 0 = always off, 1 = always on, 2 = active while a designated button is held, 3 = active while a button is NOT held.

entries.name: gyro_noise_thresh
entries.description: Angular velocity threshold below which gyro input is ignored, filtering out hand tremor and sensor noise.

entries.name: gyro_pitchsensitivity
entries.description: Multiplier for gyro vertical look speed. Can be set independently from yaw for comfort.

entries.name: gyro_turning_axis
entries.description: Selects which physical gyro axis controls yaw. 0 = yaw axis (turning the controller flat), 1 = roll axis (tilting left/right).

entries.name: gyro_yawsensitivity
entries.description: Multiplier for gyro horizontal turning speed. Higher values make gyro yaw more responsive.

entries.name: -heapsize
entries.description: Same as -mem but in KB. So 256mb * 1024 = 262144. Example: -heapsize 262144. Default is 256 MB. A map like ad_tears requires more.

entries.name: -height
entries.description: Specify window height

entries.name: hints
entries.description: Display cool feature client QSS-M hints

entries.name: -hipnotic
entries.description: add mission pack requests (only one should be specified)

entries.name: history
entries.description: Print console command history in history.txt

entries.name: horde
entries.description: Exposes the Horde-mode state expected by the 2021 rerelease and compatible QuakeC, defaulting to 0. It primarily serves as a compatibility/game-state CVar rather than directly implementing Horde gameplay in the engine.

entries.name: host_cvar_migrate
entries.description: Applies versioned migrations to settings created by older QSS-M releases. It preserves user customizations where possible and updates the migration schema after completing them.

entries.name: host_framerate
entries.description: The time adjustment value for the game. The default value of 0 sets the game time to proceed at normal speed. If the value is set to a fraction such as 0.01 game time will pass more slowly, if the value is set to a large fraction such as 0.5 the game time pass quicker. You can use this command to tailor the game to the speed that you wish to play it at. This command is also useful when playing back demos so that you can play a demo in slow motion or in super speed.

entries.name: host_maxfps
entries.summary: Caps rendering FPS; 0 uncaps gameplay rendering. Negative values select a separate network/simulation rate.
entries.description: Defaults to 250. Positive values cap rendering between 10 and 5000 FPS; 0 removes the gameplay cap. Vsync can still limit rendering, and the disconnected menu has its own cap. Negative values leave rendering uncapped and request a network/simulation interval between 10 and 150 Hz: for example, -72 requests 72 Hz. Zero and positive values above 72 use a 72 Hz interval. These are scheduling targets, not guarantees of a particular packet rate or lower latency.

entries.name: host_speeds
entries.description: Toggle the display of the game engine’s performance statistics.  When this toggle is enabled the game will print out a constant list of performance times for the game engine. The values displayed show the time in milliseconds that it takes the game engine to complete certain tasks. In the listing the first number represents the total time that it took the engine to render a single frame, the next number represents the time taken for calculating all of the game information, the number after that represents the time that it took to render the frame, and the last number represents the amount of time which was spend on producing the sound for that frame. Also, in order to receive the correct statistics on sound playback you will need to enable the snd_noextraupdate toggle.

entries.name: host_timescale
entries.description: Scales the passage of time on client and server. Set to 0 or 1 for normal speed, less than 1 for slow motion, and greater than 1 for fast-forward. If greater than 0, overrides host_framerate. Default 0.

entries.name: hostname
entries.description: The name of the server. This variable holds the name of the server as it should appear to other players that want to connect to it. Usually, the name of the server is setup by the administrator to identify his server, names such as ‘The Mosh Pit‘ are assigned to the servers. If the server is running some kind of a custom modification game then the name of the server could be ‘DeathPit Capture The Flag‘. Its usually a good idea to give a meaningful name to the server to inform the players what they might be getting into.

entries.name: hunk_print
entries.description: Typing hunk_print into the console executes a function that displays information about the current usage of the hunk memory allocator, likely showing a summary of allocated blocks and potentially free space. This is primarily a debugging tool for developers to inspect memory usage.

entries.name: -hwgamma
entries.description: Explicitly prefers hardware gamma ramps. It is mainly useful for testing or working around problems with GLSL gamma correction.

entries.name: identify
entries.description: Identifies a player by their IP Address. Type status and then identify their number. ProQuake maintains a database of player names/ip addresses. When you are connected to a server, the other players are added to the database every time you check scores.  There are three ways to see the list of aliases associated with a player's ip address: 1) Use the "status" command to determine the player's number, e.g. #3 iPimpU then type identify <player number>, e.g. identify 3 2) Use the first three fields of an ip address, e.g. identify 198.168.1 3) Use a substring of the player's name, e.g. identify beatnik. ProQuake un-funs the names before comparing them, so the above example will correctly find a player named [tog].b34tn1k. If you only type idenitfy it will attempt to identify the last connected player (added above proquake for QSSM)

entries.name: if
entries.description: if <cvar> [operator <value>] <command(s)>: execute command(s) based on the comparison of cvar to <value>. Supported operators: ==, !=, <, >, <=, >=. If no operator is provided, non-zero cvar will trigger the command(s). Example: if vid_fullscreen "exec end.cfg". bind "F1" "if vid_width == 3840 2k;if vid_width == 1920 4k". bind "k" "if gl_max_size == 0 textureless_off;if gl_max_size > 0 textureless"

entries.name: ignore
entries.description: The ignore command hides all chat messages from a specified player — type ignore <name> while connected to mute someone, or ignore with no arguments to list all currently ignored players. To restore chat from an ignored player, use unignore <name>. Both commands support partial name matching (for example, ignore tim will match a player named “timbo”), work client-side in singleplayer/listen servers and server-side when sent from a connected client, and the ignore list is cleared when you disconnect.

entries.name: ignorethis
entries.description: Mute various invalid stuffcmds

entries.name: imagedump
entries.description: Originally from Fitzquake. Dumps all loaded textures from opengl into tga files. This shows the textures as they exist in opengl texture memory. Texture names containing '*' will be renamed with '#' instead. A second argument will filter the dumped images with that search field.

entries.name: imagelist
entries.description: Originally from Fitzquake.  Displays a list of loaded textures, and their dimentions. A second argument will filter the list with that search field.

entries.name: impulse
entries.description: Pass an impulse to the server to perform a game function.  It is necessary to use impulses in order for the client to communicate with the server. The impulse command is passed to the server and the server executes the desired function assigned to an impulse. There is a maximum of 255 impulses available. The idea behind impulses was to allow mod authors to let the player perform some special new functions for a mod and not have to intoduce any new commands into the game’s console. Also, the number keys which select the weapons all have impulse commands bound to them to allow the player to switch weapons.

entries.name: in_bind
entries.description: Darkplaces compatibility. Same as 'bind'

entries.name: in_debugkeys
entries.description: Show SDL scancodes for keyboard and mouse inputs; prints to console

entries.name: in_disablemacosxmouseaccel
entries.description: Disables mouse accelaration in macos so it doesnt effect game sensitivity

entries.name: in_mouseinfo
entries.description: Prints diagnostic information about the current mouse input configuration. The report includes focus, relative mode, cursor visibility, mouse position, buttons, and platform-specific input paths.

entries.name: in_unbind
entries.description: Darkplaces compatibility. Same as 'unbind'

entries.name: inc
entries.description: Increments a cvar's value by amount. amount defaults to 1.

entries.name: ip
entries.description: Display local and external ip addresses. Add arg of local or ext to copy the ip to clipboard

entries.name: -ip
entries.description: For multi-homed machines (machines with more than one network adapter and IP adress), you can force WinQuake to bind to a specific IP address.  There is a command line option "-ip" that takes an IP address as its parameter.

entries.name: -ip6
entries.description: Specify the IPv6 address to use

entries.name: ipdump
entries.description: Use the "ipdump" command to dump all database entries to the file "iplog.txt" in your game directory.

entries.name: ipmerge
entries.description: ipmerge <filename> - Merges IP log data from another file into your current IP log, with filenames relative to your quake directory. IP log files are now stored in the id1/backups/ folder, so you would use "ipmerge id1/backups/iplog.dat" to merge the current log file, or "ipmerge id1/iplog.dat" for legacy files in the old location, or "ipmerge beatnik_iplog.dat" for files in your quake root directory. If quake has trouble finding the file, specify the full pathname such as "ipmerge c:\games\quake\id1\backups\beatnik_iplog.dat".

entries.name: ipnames
entries.description: The ipnames command prints a sorted, deduplicated list of every player name recorded in your local IP log, displayed in neat columns that fit your console width. The IP log is built automatically as you play; each time a player's address and name are seen, they are stored persistently so ipnames can recall them across sessions. This is useful for checking what names a particular server regular has used, and it pairs with the related ipdump command, which exports the full IP-to-name log as a text file, and ipmerge, which imports an external IP log

entries.name: it
entries.description: For item timer stuffcmd from CRx -- // it[cur / ]duration x y z radius 0xRRGGBB "timername" owningent

entries.name: joy_always_active
entries.description: When set to 1, controller input is processed even when the game window is not focused. Useful for background play setups.

entries.name: joy_deadzone_look
entries.description: Fraction of look stick travel to be deadzone, between 0 and 1. Default is 0.175.

entries.name: joy_deadzone_move
entries.description: Same as above, but for the move stick. Default is 0.175.

entries.name: joy_deadzone_trigger
entries.description: Fraction of trigger range required to register a button press on the analog triggers, between 0 and 1. Default 0.2.

entries.name: joy_device
entries.description: Selects which connected controller to use by index. Use 0 for the first controller, 1 for the second, and so on.

entries.name: joy_enable
entries.description: Set to 0 to disable controller support. Default 1.

entries.name: joy_exponent
entries.description: For the look stick, the stick displacement (between 0 and 1) is raised to this power. Default is 3. A value of 1 would give a linear relationship between stick displacement and fraction of the maximum angular speed.

entries.name: joy_exponent_move
entries.description: For the look stick, the stick displacement (between 0 and 1) is raised to this power. Default is 3. A value of 1 would give a linear relationship between stick displacement and fraction of the maximum angular speed.

entries.name: joy_flick
entries.description: Enables flick stick mode, where pointing the right stick in a direction instantly rotates the camera to face that way. Designed to be paired with gyro aiming.

entries.name: joy_flick_adjust_speed
entries.description: Speed in degrees per frame for smooth stick-rotate adjustments after the initial flick. Controls how fast held rotations track.

entries.name: joy_flick_deadzone
entries.description: Threshold (fraction of full tilt) the right stick must reach to register a flick. Prevents accidental flicks from partial input.

entries.name: joy_flick_noise_thresh
entries.description: Angular noise threshold in degrees for flick stick rotation. Small angle changes below this value are filtered out to prevent jitter.

entries.name: joy_flick_recenter
entries.description: Speed at which the camera recenters after releasing a flick. Set to 0 to disable recentering entirely

entries.name: joy_flick_time
entries.description: Duration in seconds for the flick rotation animation. Lower values make the camera snap faster

entries.name: joy_invert
entries.description: Set to 1 to invert the vertical axis of the look stick.

entries.name: joy_outer_threshold_look
entries.description: Outer deadzone for the look stick, between 0 and 1. Default 0.02.

entries.name: joy_outer_threshold_move
entries.description: Outer deadzone for the look stick, between 0 and 1. Default 0.02.

entries.name: joy_rumble
entries.description: Vibration intensity as a fraction from 0 to 1. Scales all rumble feedback from weapon fire and damage. Set to 0 to disable.

entries.name: joy_rumble_triggers
entries.description: Controls the strength of independent controller-trigger rumble, defaulting to 0. Values are clamped from 0 through 1 and only work with SDL and controllers that support trigger motors.

entries.name: joy_sensitivity_pitch
entries.description: Max angular speed in degrees/second when looking. Defaults are 300 for yaw (turning left/right) and 150 for pitch (up/down).

entries.name: joy_sensitivity_yaw
entries.description: Max angular speed in degrees/second when looking. Defaults are 300 for yaw (turning left/right) and 150 for pitch (up/down).

entries.name: joy_swapmovelook
entries.description: Set to 1 to swap the left and right analog stick functions. Default 0, move on the left stick, look on the right stick.

entries.name: joy_touchpad
entries.description: Enables using the first controller touchpad finger as a menu pointer, defaulting to 1. It operates only while controller input is enabled and the native menu is open.

entries.name: jumpdemo
entries.description: jumpdemo seeks to a specific point in a demo by frame, percentage, time, or seconds — for example, jumpdemo 500 jumps to frame 500, jumpdemo 50% jumps to the halfway point, jumpdemo 1:30 jumps to one minute thirty seconds, and jumpdemo 90s jumps to ninety seconds. Prefix any value with + or - for relative seeking from the current position, like jumpdemo +1000 to skip ahead 1000 frames or jumpdemo -0:30 to rewind thirty seconds. Tab completion also provides example formats as a quick reference.

entries.name: kick
entries.description: Remove a player from the server.  This command can be used by server administrators to remove certain players from the game. This command should be used if the player has become extremely abusive to the server or to the other players. The administrator can use the status command to get the player’s number and kick him using that information instead of the player’s name. It is also possible to pass a message the the player that was kicked to explain the reason why he was kicked.

entries.name: kill
entries.description: Make the player commit suicide. This command should be used if the player became stuck somewhere in on the map or if cannot continue any longer When this command is used in deathmatch games 1 kill will be subtracted from the player’s score. If this command is used in a single-player game the map will restart and the player will have to continue from the beginning all over again.

entries.name: lastid
entries.description: Displays the last ghost code assigned by CRMOD / CRCTF, even if disconnected/client crash. Your ghost id is saved to ghost.txt in id1/backups

entries.name: levelview
entries.description: Immediately sets the player’s view pitch to level. It also stops automatic pitch drifting so the view remains centered vertically.

entries.name: like
entries.description: Likes the last command in the console for communication with other players. Will print -> woods likes "uns: dm sucks"

entries.name: listen
entries.description: Toggle if the server will look for incoming connections. This variable is used to tell the server if it should look for incoming connections from the network. It is necessary to set this variable to 1 if you wish to setup a game server and have other people connect to it.

entries.name: -listen
entries.description: Starts Quake ready to be a non-dedicated server for up to <n> players. If you do not specify a number <n> after -listen it will default to 8. The maximum allowed value is 16.

entries.name: load
entries.description: Load a saved game.  This command is used to load saved games. The saved game files are usually stored in the quake/id1/ directory. The filenames for the saved games will start with s0.sav and go onto s11.sav. The save file from the Quick Save feature will have the filename quick.sav. It is possible to load saved games from other directories by appending path information to the filename for this command. The special character combination .. can be used in the relative path to point to a directory higher than the current directory.

entries.name: loadas8bit
entries.description: Toggle the loading of sound samples in 8-bit mode. When this toggle is enabled the sound samples will be loaded in 8-bit mode thus making them a little smaller. This will give a little performance boost when playing the game at the cost of quality for the sound samples.

entries.name: loadloc
entries.description: QW LOC Creator: 'loadloc' will load all the locations into memory from a existing .loc file

entries.name: lookspring
entries.description: Toggle the centering of the screen after the -klook command. When this toggle is enabled the screen will automatically center itself after the -klook command is issued and the player takes a single step in any direction. This is a command that basically helps out keyboard players when they have to look up or down manually.

entries.name: lookstrafe
entries.description: Toggle the automatic strafing when the +klook command is used. When this toggle is active and the player used the +klook command, the keys that are bound to the +left and +right commands will now act as if they were bound to +moveleft and +moveright. This command was put it in order to allow keyboard player to combine the +strafe and +klook commands into one. This command also has effect on the mouse controls. When this toggle is enabled moving the mouse left and right will make the player move left and right instead of making him turn left and right.

entries.name: ls
entries.description: Command is designed to help you list files within the game's directories that match specific patterns you provide. This can be particularly useful for finding files, checking the contents of directories, or verifying the presence of game assets. Use * to match any number of characters and ? to match a single character. For example, *.txt will list all TXT files. To search for all files with a name that starts with config, regardless of their extension, you would use: config*. You can use the ? wildcard to substitute for the single unknown character in the filename. In this case, you would use level?.cfg as your search pattern: level?.cfg. ls * will list all the files. Examples: "*.pak *.txt", "*", "pak1.pak", "?onfig.cfg". Same as: ls, dir, flocate, which

entries.name: m_forward
entries.description: The level of precision when the mouse is used to move the player forward and back. This variable can be used to control how fast the player should move forward and back when the mouse is moved forward and back. This command has no effect if the +mlook command is in effect because when the mouse is moved forward and back the players looks up and down instead of moving forward and back. Some players might want to set this variable to 0 if they happen not to use +mlook constantly and they only want to use the mouse to turn the player. Setting this variable to 0 will prevent the inadvertent movement of the player forward and back while trying to make precise turns with the mouse.

entries.name: m_pitch
entries.description: The level of precision when the mouse is used to make the player look up and down while the +mlook command is in effect. By default this variable is set in such a way that moving the mouse forward makes the player look up and moving the mouse backward makes the player look down. Some people prefer to have this movement inverted just like it is inverted for airplane controls. If you wish to use this inverted mouse movement then you should set this variable to a negative value -0.022. It is a matter of preference which movement method is used by players. Also lowering the value for this variable will increase the level of precision when the mouse is used to make the player look up and down. This variable can be used separately from the sensitivity variable to provide greater control over the mouse sensitivity for movement along the pitch. It is advisable to keep the value for this variable constant at 0.022 or -0.022 and instead use the sensitivity variable to change the overall sensitivity of the mouse. Also, some script writers lower the value for this variable along with a lowered value for the fov variable in order to provide more precision when the fov variable is used to zoom.

entries.name: m_side
entries.description: The level of precision when the mouse is used move the player left and right. When the +strafe command is active or when the lookspring toggle is enabled this variable is used to control the level of precision when the mouse is moved left and right to make the player move left and right.

entries.name: m_yaw
entries.description: The level of precision when the mouse is used to turn the player left and right. Basically this command controls how fast the player turns left and right when the mouse is moved left and right. It is recommended that this variable be left alone and instead the sensitivity variable is used to change the level of precision. If you set this variable to a negative value you will reverse the mouse movement. Some script writers use this variable to increase the level of precision when the fov variable is used to zoom the screen.

entries.name: map
entries.description: Change the current game map. This command will change the map that is currently being played. When used on a server this command will disconnect all of the players from the server before changing the map. It is recommended that the changelevel command be used instead of this command to change maps for game servers. Additional maps should be put in the id1/maps/ directory from where they can be loaded by the game.

entries.name: maplock_status
entries.description: Lists cvars whose values are being treated as map-scoped or server-controlled. It shows each cvar’s saved value, effective value, and lock or stuffcmd status.

entries.name: mapname
entries.description: Outputs the short name of the current level (e.g. "e1m5")

entries.name: maps
entries.description: Lists all maps and their worldspawn descriptions. A second arguement will search all the maps. Example: maps chamber will find e3m6

entries.name: mapshot
entries.description: Resolves or asynchronously downloads a screenshot for a map with mapshot <map> [force] and reports whether it is ready, unavailable, disabled, or still being fetched. The force argument clears cached misses and retries the lookup.

entries.name: mapsize
entries.description: mapsize reports BSP surface-area stats for the current map or any named map, showing floor, wall, ceiling, and total area in both square feet and square meters using the project’s player-height-normalized scale. Use mapsize for the currently loaded map, mapsize e1m1 for a specific map that is not loaded, or mapsize e1m1 e1m2 e1m3 to print multiple maps and then show a floor-area comparison sorted from smallest to largest with per-map deltas. Use mapsize -l or mapsize list to list all known maps by cached floor area, and mapsize -clearall to clear all cached size data from mapdesc.json so it can be rebuilt.

entries.name: markdemo
entries.description: markdemo adds a bookmark to the demo you are currently recording, so if you type markdemo during record duel1 the finished file will include a saved marker and can be tagged with _mark or _marks if you use it multiple times. On CRMod7, markdemo integrates with the server path, so when a player marks the demo the server can broadcast the marker to all connected QSS-M recorders and announce it to the match at the same time. During playback, jumpdemo mark seeks forward to the next marker in the current demo, so a workflow like playdemo duel1_mark.dem followed by repeated jumpdemo mark calls will step through each saved moment. When you are not recording, markdemo shows your saved mark history, and commands like markdemo aerowalk or markdemo clear let you filter or manage those entries.

entries.name: massacre
entries.description: Kills all enemies in one command instantly in SP

entries.name: max_edicts
entries.description: Sets the maximum number of entites on both the client and server. Acceptable values range from 256 to 32000. Set to 600 to mimic standard quake. Changes won't take effect until the next time a map is loaded. Note: if a client connects to a server, and the client's maximum is lower than the server's, the client will probably crash if it ever sees an entnum higher than its local max_edicts. Warning: you may need to increase -heapsize if you want a high max_edicts value. Default 1024.

entries.name: maxplayers
entries.description: The maximum number of players allowed on the server. For single-player games this variable will always be set to 1. When a listen server is started the value for this variable will be set to 4. When the server is started in dedicated mode with the usage of the -dedicated command line parameter this variable will be set to 8. The maximum number of players allowed on a server is 16 and the only way to start a server like that is to use the -listen 16 or -dedicated 16 command line parameters. It is not recommended to run a listen server as a public access server.

entries.name: mcache
entries.description: Display information about all cached models. This command will display information about all models which are currently loaded in the memory. The first model reported is always the map itself. The memory address at which the model is located is reported along with the path and filename for the specific model.

entries.name: -mem
entries.description: Heapsize, but in MB. Example: -mem 256. Default is 256 MB

entries.name: menu_cmd
entries.description: Load menu qc

entries.name: menu_restart
entries.description: Runs on menu initiation

entries.name: menu_search
entries.description: Opens or toggles the native menu command palette, moving to the Options menu first when necessary. It refuses to open during modal dialogs, key binding, MenuQC use, or when menu_search_enable is disabled.

entries.name: menu_search_debug
entries.description: Enables verbose menu-search diagnostics, including normalized queries and the score assigned to each candidate, defaulting to 0. It is a non-archived developer aid and therefore does not persist in the normal configuration.

entries.name: menu_search_enable
entries.description: Enables the native menu command palette and its shortcuts, defaulting to 1. Setting it to 0 hides the related Options entry, prevents implicit opening, and makes menu_search report that it is disabled.

entries.name: menu_search_validate
entries.description: Runs a verbose integrity check over the menu-search providers and registered rows. It reports invalid provider contracts, duplicate identifiers, label drift, capacity overflow, and the final validation result.

entries.name: messagemode
entries.description: Display the text line for sending messages to other players. When you use this command you will have access to the line where you can type messages to all the players on the server. You can type in the message and then press the ENTER key to send the message. If you do not want to send a message press the ESCAPE key to exit this mode. You can also create bindings by using the say command so you don’t have to manually type messages which are used often like “Hello all!“.

entries.name: messagemode2
entries.description: Display the text line for sending messages to players only on your team. By default this command is not bound, but it is recommened that you bind this command to the Y key so you can send private messages to the players on your team. This command is very helpful in team games because it allows you to talk about strategy with your team without having the other team overhearing anything that you say. When you use this command your name will be displayed in parentheses (Player) so that the players on your team know that the message that you send them is only heard by the team. You can create bindings using the say_team command if you wish to have a couple of messages which you can use all the time to inform your team.

entries.name: -minmemory
entries.description: The -minmemory command-line parameter forces the Quake engine to start using the absolute minimum amount of RAM it deems necessary. This overrides any larger memory allocation that might have been requested via the -heapsize parameter or the engine's default calculation. It's primarily a troubleshooting or diagnostic option for running the game under extreme memory constraints, potentially at the cost of performance or stability.

entries.name: -mixspeed
entries.description: New -mixspeed option sets the rate for mixing sfx and music, and output to the OS (default 44100), setting it to 11025 reverts to 0.85.9 behaviour

entries.name: mod_ignorelmscale
entries.description: Typically, lightmaps in BSP files have a standard scale that defines how texels (texture pixels) map to luxels (light pixels) on a surface. The mod_ignorelmscale flag, when set, instructs the loader to ignore custom scaling values stored in the map and instead use a default scale for lightmaps. This helps maintain consistent lighting across surfaces without variation caused by user-defined scales in different map files.

entries.name: mod_lightgrid
entries.description: Mostly for debugging

entries.name: mod_lightscale_broken
entries.description: Match vanilla's brokenness bug with dlights and scaled textures. decoupled_lm bypasses this obviously buggy setting because zomgletmefixstuffffs

entries.name: mods
entries.description: Lists all child folders of quake directory which contain either a progs.dat or a pak file. Same as games command.

entries.name: modvote
entries.description: Displays or participates in a multiplayer vote to switch the active mod. When enough eligible players vote for the same mod, the server applies that choice.

entries.name: modvote_startmap
entries.description: Starts the configured default map after a mod-vote transition. It validates sv_defaultmap and falls back to start when the configured name is unsafe or invalid.

entries.name: music
entries.description: Tracks should be named like "track02.ogg", "track03.ogg" ... (there is no track01) and placed into "Quake/id1/music". Can play various external music formats, including MP3, OGG and FLAC. Notice that you don't have to type the file extension.

entries.name: music_jump
entries.description: Jump to given order in music, like Unreal's music change - only for module (tracker) music.

entries.name: music_loop
entries.description: Make music loop

entries.name: music_pause
entries.description: Pauses music

entries.name: music_preview
entries.description: Plays a music file through the isolated preview system without replacing normal gameplay music state. Its subcommands provide pause, resume, stop, status, looping, gain, and fractional seeking controls.

entries.name: music_resume
entries.description: Resumes paused music.

entries.name: music_stop
entries.description: Stops playing music.

entries.name: mute
entries.description: Mute volume. CTRL-M works as well.

entries.name: muteall
entries.description: For voip

entries.name: name
entries.description: QSSM will allow you edit the name by just typing name; good for names with specials chars. The name of the player. It is recommended to use the name command to set the player’s name instead of this command.

entries.name: name
entries.description: QSSM will allow you edit the name by just typing name; good for names with specials chars. The name of the player. It is recommended to use the name command to set the player’s name instead of this command.

entries.name: namebk
entries.description: Internal usage for auto name backups

entries.name: namehistory
entries.description: Lists player names saved in the local name history. Options can display last-used dates or clear the stored history.

entries.name: net_connectattempts
entries.description: How many retries when connecting to server.

entries.name: net_connectsearch
entries.description: Controls whether connect performs a local host search before attempting the requested connection, defaulting to 1. Disabling it avoids that discovery step and proceeds directly with the supplied destination.

entries.name: net_connecttimeout
entries.description: After requesting a connection, the client must reply within this many seconds or be dropped (cuts down on connect floods). net_connecttimeout is a configurable console variable, typically defaulting to 10 seconds, that serves as a timeout for network connections that have been initiated but then stall before the full handshake completes. When first attempting to connect, the client makes several rapid, short-timed attempts to get an initial server response; if these all fail, a "No Response" error occurs quickly. However, if an initial connection is made but then communication ceases during the handshake phase, net_connecttimeout dictates how long the client will wait before aborting. This mechanism prevents the client from hanging indefinitely on a partially formed connection and offers some protection against certain network attacks.

entries.name: net_getdomainname
entries.description: Enables reverse-DNS lookup when converting network addresses into display names, defaulting to 0. Leaving it disabled avoids potentially slow or unwanted hostname-resolution attempts.

entries.name: net_ice_show
entries.description: Prints ICE diagnostics to the console. With no argument, it dumps debug info for all ICE connections (even ones not currently attached to a socket). With a name, it filters to ICE sockets and only prints entries whose ICE “true address” matches that name (the code compares against trueaddress+1, so you typically pass the room name without the leading /). Example: net_ice_show for everything, or net_ice_show myroom to focus on /myroom.

entries.name: net_master_ignore
entries.description: net_master_ignore is a comma-separated list of server names or addresses to hide from the server browser, useful for suppressing noisy, duplicate, or unwanted master results. Each entry can be a full address like 15.181.21.196:26000, a host-only address like 159.196.122.212 or la.quakeone.com, or a server name like CRMOD 7 - DENVER.QUAKEONE.COM; matching is case-insensitive, and starred names also match if you omit the leading *. Example: net_master_ignore "159.196.122.212, 15.181.21.196:26000, la.quakeone.com, CRMOD 7 - DENVER.QUAKEONE.COM" will hide any browser entry matching one of those values.

entries.name: net_messagetimeout
entries.description: The maximum amount of time in seconds between receiving network packets before the client determines the connection to be lost. The client will keep the game open waiting for another game packet to come through, if a packet does not come in the amount of time set by this variable the client will determine that the connection has been broken and that it is lost. The client will shutdown the current game and go back to the console. 60 may be a good number vs 300

entries.name: net_stats
entries.description: Display network statistics. This command will display statistics about the network packets which have been send and received by the client. This command is mostly used by game developers to test the game for bugs and such. It can also be used by causal players to test the quality and performance of their network connection to the server. You can judge the quality of your network connection by looking at the values for the packetsReSent, receivedDuplicateCount, shortPacketCount, and droppedDatagrams. If you notice high numbers for any of those fields then you will need to investigate your network connection or find a server to which you have a better connection. Unreliable packets are the usual game packets for player movement and player actions. These packets can be lost during the transmission without having a negative effect on the game, because they will only cause some jerkyness in the movement of the player. The reliable packets are the ones that are sent which must arrive a the client or the server in order to keep the game synchronized and working properly. Reliable packets contain messages send by players, death messages, map change information, and information about objects picked up by the player. These messages must be send with a reliable method in order to keep the client updated about such important information.

entries.name: netdrops
entries.description: Prints a server-side packet-drop report for connected clients. Players are ranked from best to worst by map packet drops per minute, with ping and total-drop statistics included.

entries.name: netfps_probe
entries.description: Samples actual rendered frame timing while connected to a map. It estimates sustainable network update rates and recommends an appropriate negative host_maxfps value.

entries.name: nextdl
entries.description: Requests a particular chunk of an active chunked download from the server. Negative chunk numbers cancel the transfer, while invalid or out-of-range requests are ignored.

entries.name: -noadd
entries.description: Disable texture_env_add

entries.name: noclip
entries.description: Move through map walls in singleplayer

entries.name: -nocombine
entries.description: Overbright models now uses GL_EXT_texture_env_combine if supported (TNT and later, voodoo4 and later,) which saves one or two passes on model rendering when gl_overbright_models is 1. The command line option -nocombine will disable this.

entries.name: noexit
entries.description: Toggle if players are allowed to exit the level in multiplayer games.  It is recommended that public servers set this toggle to 2 in order to prevent players from abusing the server and interfering with game play by constantly changing maps. This setting will also allow players to choose the episode that they wish to play when the server defaults to the start map.

entries.name: -noextmusic
entries.description: Disable: Quakespasm can play various external music formats, including MP3, OGG and FLAC

entries.name: -nofastlightmapupload
entries.description: Disables optimized partial uploads of changed lightmap regions. Dynamic lightmaps are uploaded using the broader fallback path.

entries.name: -noglsl
entries.description: Disable all glsl for gamma and alias

entries.name: -noglslalias
entries.description: New, faster mdl renderer using GLSL. Disable with "-noglslalias"

entries.name: -noglslgamma
entries.description: New gamma correction implementation using GLSL. Fixes all known gamma issues (affecting the full display, persisting after quitting, or darkening the screen on OS X). Disable with "-noglslgamma".

entries.name: -nohome
entries.description: Prevents Unix and macOS builds from using a separate user-data directory. Configuration, saves, and generated files instead use the installation base directory.

entries.name: -noice
entries.description: Forces ICE networking disabled, even if it would otherwise be enabled. This is mainly a “hard off” safety/troubleshooting flag; the ICE driver checks -noice (and also refuses to init in safe mode). Default is “not present,” meaning it doesn’t change behavior unless you add it. Example: ./quake -useice -noice (ICE will still be disabled), or ./quake -noice to guarantee you’re not using ICE.

entries.name: -nojoy
entries.description: Disable joystick

entries.name: -nolan
entries.description: Disable all networking; will not be able to connect. Disables IPX, TCP/IP, and serial support.

entries.name: -nolightmappbo
entries.description: Disables persistent pixel-buffer-object staging for dynamic lightmap uploads. The renderer falls back to its non-PBO upload path.

entries.name: nomonsters
entries.description: Toggle the presence of monsters on the map. This command is supposed to remove all of the monsters from the map but it does not seem to work. You can use the notarget command instead, which will allow you to keep the monsters on the map but they will not react to the player. QSSM Fixes this cvar

entries.name: -nomouse
entries.description: Deprecated

entries.name: -nomtex
entries.description: Deprecated: Mutitexture disabled at command line

entries.name: -nopackedpixels
entries.description: Disables packed-pixel texture support. This forces the renderer away from its higher-precision packed lightmap format.

entries.name: -noparalleltextureprep
entries.description: Disables parallel texture preparation completely. Texture-loading work is restricted to one participant regardless of tex_workers

entries.name: nosound
entries.description: Toggle the playback of sound effects in the game. When this toggle is enabled the game will not play any sound effects in the game. When this toggle is used while the player is currently in a game it will disable the playback of all sound effects except the environment sounds. In order to totally disable the playback of all sound effects the game needs to be restarted or maps must be changed.

entries.name: -nosound
entries.description: Disables hardware sound

entries.name: notarget
entries.description: Force notarget mode to be enabled or disabled. (e.g. "notarget 1" will enable notarget mode regardless of its current state.)

entries.name: -notexturenpot
entries.description: Disable support for opengl non-power-of-two-textures extension

entries.name: -noudp
entries.description: Disable networking; will not be able to connect

entries.name: -noudp4
entries.description: Disable IPv4 networking, which is to force IPv6 only.

entries.name: -noudp6
entries.description: Disable IPv6 networking, which is to force IPv4 only.

entries.name: -novbo
entries.description: Support for OpenGL vertex buffer objects (VBO, OpenGL 1.5 or newer) for world and brush models (disable with command line: "-novbo".)

entries.name: -nowarpmipmaps
entries.description: Disables automatic mipmap generation for turbulent water and warp textures. It provides a compatibility fallback for problematic OpenGL drivers.

entries.name: -nowildpaks
entries.description: Disable loading paks that aren't numbered

entries.name: open
entries.description: Open folders inside the game directory. (Example: open screenshots, open id1) will open the folder on your system

entries.name: paknames
entries.description: mute various invalid stuffcmds

entries.name: paks
entries.description: mute various invalid stuffcmds

entries.name: -particles
entries.description: Specify max number on-screen particles, 2048 default

entries.name: password
entries.description: To establish a password-protected Quake server, the server administrator must first define the desired password by setting the password console variable (cvar). This can be achieved either by adding a line such as password "your_secret_password" to the server's configuration file (commonly server.cfg), which applies the password upon server startup, or by directly typing this command into the running server's console for immediate effect. Once the server has its password set, any player wishing to connect must configure their client accordingly. The player needs to open their game console and set their own password cvar to match the exact password chosen by the server administrator, for example, by typing password "your_secret_password". After correctly setting this client-side password, the player can then use the standard connect <server_address> command to join the now-secured server. If the client's password matches the server's, the connection will be accepted; otherwise, the server will typically reject the attempt with a "bad/missing password" notification.

entries.name: path
entries.description: Display information about the current path locations used by the game. This command will display the fully qualified paths which are being used by the game. The default paths always start in the id1/ directory in order for the game to be able to find all of the necessary game files. Also, .pak files are considered to be path locations because they contain directory information inside them.

entries.name: pausable
entries.description: Toggle the ability of the player to temporarily stop the game. This toggle determines if the player is able to use the pause command to temporarily stop the game. When the game is in single-player mode this toggle is enabled. When the game is in multiplayer mode this toggle is disabled in order to prevent players from abusing the pausing feature of the game.

entries.name: pause
entries.description: Pause demo playback

entries.name: pext
entries.description: Show protocols

entries.name: ping
entries.description: QSSM will ping any host with ping google.com as an example. QSSM also allows you to type ping +25 when connected to a server to add synthetic lag (ProQuake). Display the network latency times for all players on the server. This command will show the network latency or ping times for all the players. This command is useful because it allows the player to see the types of connections that each player has. The latency times are calculated by recording the time in milliseconds that it takes a game packet to be send from the server to the client, and then back again. If a player has a ping of 200ms then that means that it takes 0.2 seconds for a packet to make a round trip. It is better to play on servers which allow the player to have the lowest possible ping time because the lower the ping time the more responsive the game is to the player’s movments. Normally, players will have all types of pings in all ranges. Ping times increase as the distance increases between the client and the server. Ping times also vary depending on the type of a connection that the client has. If the player is using a analog modem he will have pings above of 130ms because it takes about 60 milliseconds to modulate the information from analog to digital, and digital to analog. Some players will have pings as high has 350ms and more that means that they are a considerable distance from the server in physical terms. If a player has a ping of 0ms it means that he is running a listen server that is both a client and a server in the same program, that player has considerable advantage over all other players on the server. A ping of 999ms means that the server has lost connection with the player. Players with ping times of less than 150ms are commonly named LPBs which stands for “Low Ping Bastards“. Players with pings of 150+ are usually nick named “High Ping Whiners” or HPWs. Sometimes they will be misnamed HPBs which would stand for “High Ping Bastards” because the player would derive the term from the term LPB. It is widely known that a lot of HPWs resent LPBs because of their lower pings and the advantage of lower pings.

entries.name: pingplreport
entries.description: Receives the first block of server-provided ping and packet-loss values. It updates the corresponding entries in the client scoreboard.

entries.name: pingplreport2
entries.description: Receives continuation blocks of ping and packet-loss values for larger servers. Its first argument identifies the scoreboard slot where the continuation begins.

entries.name: pings
entries.description: Requests a DarkPlaces or FTE-style ping and packet-loss scoreboard report. QSS-M servers split large reports into pingplreport and pingplreport2 messages.

entries.name: play
entries.description: Play a sound file. You can use this command to listen through all of the sounds which come with the game. Most sound files are recorded in PCM Wave format at 11,025Hz in 8-bit mono mode. Some sound files are recorded at 22,050Hz in 16-bit mono mode. You can use the loadas8bit command to limit all files to 8-bit mode. You should be aware that by default all sound files are stored under the sound/ directory so when you issue a command like ‘play shamber\shurt2‘ it actually plays the sound\shambler\shurt2.wav file. Keep in mind the sound/ directory prefix when you decide to play your own sound files.

entries.name: play2
entries.description: Version with attenuation 0

entries.name: playdemo
entries.description: Playback a recorded game demo. The demo file is actually a collection of game information that would normally be send from the client to the server. Also, below is a list of the three demo files that come with the game. For more information about demo files and for information about their structure you can visit the Demo Specs web site at http://www.planetquake.com/demospecs/.

entries.name: playvol
entries.description: Play a sound file at a given volume. This command works exactly like the play command except that with this command you can specify the volume at which the sound file should be played at. You can refer to the list of sound files which is provided with the play file. The volume parameter for this file can only be between 0.0 and 1.0 because it is a percentage value of the general volume.

entries.name: pm_airstep
entries.description: These pm_ CVARs only apply when using the pmove physics system, which is enabled by setting sv_nqplayerphysics 0 or by having a custom QuakeC physics function. Allows players to step up onto surfaces while airborne, such as when jumping. When enabled, you can land on and climb steps/ledges even when not touching the ground. This makes navigation more fluid by removing the requirement to be grounded for step-up mechanics.

entries.name: pm_autobunny
entries.description: These pm_ CVARs only apply when using the pmove physics system, which is enabled by setting sv_nqplayerphysics 0 or by having a custom QuakeC physics function. Enables automatic bunnyhopping by removing the need to manually time jump releases. When active, holding jump will automatically perform optimal bunnyhopping without requiring precise input timing. The comment calls this "pogostick mode, for lazy noobs" indicating it's meant to make advanced movement accessible.

entries.name: pm_bunnyfriction
entries.description: Controls whether standard Quake ground friction is applied on the frame when the player jumps, defaulting to 1. Setting it to 0 preserves more speed during bunnyhopping, while 1 applies the normal friction behavior in both legacy and predicted movement.

entries.name: pm_bunnyspeedcap
entries.description: These pm_ CVARs only apply when using the pmove physics system, which is enabled by setting sv_nqplayerphysics 0 or by having a custom QuakeC physics function. Controls bunnyhopping speed limits by capping strafe-jumping acceleration. When enabled with a value, it prevents players from endlessly accelerating beyond the specified multiplier of maxspeed. Default empty value means no cap, allowing unlimited bunnyhopping acceleration.

entries.name: pm_edgefriction
entries.summary: Pmove only (sv_nqplayerphysics 0/QC pmove). Edge friction multiplier: 2=double; 1=normal; 4=quad
entries.description: These pm_ CVARs only apply when using the pmove physics system, which is enabled by setting sv_nqplayerphysics 0 or by having a custom QuakeC physics function. Multiplies friction when the player is near a ledge or drop-off. When moving near edges, this increases friction to prevent accidental falls. Default value of "2" doubles friction at edges compared to normal ground friction.

entries.name: pm_flyfriction
entries.description: These pm_ CVARs only apply when using the pmove physics system, which is enabled by setting sv_nqplayerphysics 0 or by having a custom QuakeC physics function. Sets the friction coefficient applied when in fly or noclip movement modes. Controls how quickly velocity decays when not actively moving in these special movement states. Lower values allow longer coasting, while higher values make movement feel more responsive.

entries.name: pm_ktjump
entries.description: These pm_ CVARs only apply when using the pmove physics system, which is enabled by setting sv_nqplayerphysics 0 or by having a custom QuakeC physics function. Enables "KeepThings" or threshold jumping mechanics where jump timing affects jump height. This allows skilled players to achieve higher jumps through precise timing. The feature modifies the standard jump velocity based on input timing.

entries.name: pm_pground
entries.description: These pm_ CVARs only apply when using the pmove physics system, which is enabled by setting sv_nqplayerphysics 0 or by having a custom QuakeC physics function. Implements a persistent ground detection system for more precise onground state tracking. While theoretically more accurate than standard ground detection, it can cause interaction issues with game code that expects traditional behavior. It maintains ground state across frames more consistently than the default system.

entries.name: pm_slidefix
entries.description: These pm_ CVARs only apply when using the pmove physics system, which is enabled by setting sv_nqplayerphysics 0 or by having a custom QuakeC physics function. Prevents the player from getting stuck or "bumping" when moving down slopes. When enabled (default "1"), it smooths movement down inclined surfaces that would otherwise cause collision issues. This eliminates the jarring stop-start motion that can occur on steep terrain.

entries.name: pm_slidyslopes
entries.description: These pm_ CVARs only apply when using the pmove physics system, which is enabled by setting sv_nqplayerphysics 0 or by having a custom QuakeC physics function. Makes slopes slippery like in vanilla NetQuake, causing gradual sliding down inclined surfaces. When enabled, players will slowly slide down slopes due to gravity rather than maintaining perfect footing. This recreates the classic Quake feel where steep surfaces are difficult to stand on.

entries.name: pm_stepdown
entries.description: These pm_ CVARs only apply when using the pmove physics system, which is enabled by setting sv_nqplayerphysics 0 or by having a custom QuakeC physics function. Makes the player "stick" to the ground when walking down steps or slopes. When enabled, it automatically moves the player downward to maintain ground contact instead of launching into the air. This creates more realistic walking behavior but can feel unusual compared to standard Quake physics.

entries.name: pm_stepheight
entries.description: These pm_ CVARs only apply when using the pmove physics system, which is enabled by setting sv_nqplayerphysics 0 or by having a custom QuakeC physics function. Defines the maximum height in units that a player can automatically step up onto. Controls how tall obstacles can be climbed without jumping. Standard Quake uses 18 units, allowing players to walk up onto most steps and small obstacles.

entries.name: pm_walljump
entries.description: These pm_ CVARs only apply when using the pmove physics system, which is enabled by setting sv_nqplayerphysics 0 or by having a custom QuakeC physics function. Enables wall-jumping mechanics where players can bounce off walls to gain momentum. When enabled, collision with walls can redirect velocity rather than simply stopping movement. This adds advanced movement techniques similar to those found in games like QuakeWorld or Defrag.

entries.name: pm_watersinkspeed
entries.summary: Pmove only (sv_nqplayerphysics 0/QC). Idle water sink speed; 0=float, 20=default, 40=sink faster
entries.description: These pm_ CVARs only apply when using the pmove physics system, which is enabled by setting sv_nqplayerphysics 0 or by having a custom QuakeC physics function. Controls how fast the player sinks when idle in water without any movement input. Sets the downward velocity applied when standing still in water. Higher values make you sink faster, while lower values allow more floating behavior.

entries.name: pointfile
entries.description: Load a point file to display leaks on the map. This command allows for the loading of a point file which is generated by QBSP in order to find leaks on the map. A leak will be displayed by a trail of little dots on the map. It is necessary to close all leaks on a map in order to avoid problems and possible crashes.

entries.name: port
entries.description: The UDP port used by the game for the TCP/IP network protocol. By default the game uses the 26000 UDP port. Sometimes if there is more than one server running on the same computer each server can use a different port address. In order to start a server with a different port number you must use the -port command line parameter instead of this command. If you want to connect to a server which is using a different port number than the default you will have to set this variable to match the port number of the server before you can connect.

entries.name: -port
entries.description: Specify the port, default is 26000 (i.e. -port 26001)

entries.name: pq_fullpitch
entries.description: Mute various invalid stuffcmds

entries.name: pq_lag
entries.description: Set the amount of lag in ms (0-400). Also use ping +X

entries.name: pr_checkextension
entries.description: If a mod malfunctions in QSS but not QS, then try using pr_checkextensions 0. This will prevent the mod from being able to autodetect any qc extensions, and thus result in the same behaviour. If this does not work then please report this as a QSS bug. Note that this may also break any mod that depends upon those extensions. Will 'trick' the qc code into thinking that the engine doesn't support extensions

entries.name: pr_dumpplatform
entries.description: Writes out a qsextensions.qc file. id1/src folder needs to exist

entries.name: pr_engine
entries.summary: Engine identification string, initialized from the compiled QSS-M version.
entries.description: Initialized from ENGINE_NAME_AND_VER in the source header. A normal QSS-M build combines the engine name with its compiled version; a build using QSS_DATE uses the QSS date string instead.

entries.name: precache
entries.description: Toggle the preloading of all necessary sound files before the map starts. Normally this toggle is enabled which in turn enables the game to load all of the necessary sound files for that specific map before the game starts. If this toggle is disabled the game will not preload the sound files during the start of the map, instead the sound files will only be loaded when they are necessary. The sound files will stay in memory after they are loaded in order to increase performance of the game by not having to reload the same sound files from the hard drive every time that the sound file is used.

entries.name: prespawn
entries.description: Spawn the player entity on a given respawn spot. This command is used internally by the game and it is send from the server to the client when the server determines that the client is ready to start the game. This command will spawn the player entity on a given respawn spot.

entries.name: printtxt
entries.description: Prints a text file into the console.

entries.name: -privkey
entries.description: Specifies the private key file used for DTLS credentials (server-side in the ICE module when DTLS is compiled in). If you don’t provide it, the code falls back through a search order: on Unix it tries /etc/ssl/private/privkey.pem, then it tries files in com_basedir (privkey.pem, then privkey.der as part of the full .der pair logic). If nothing is found, it can generate temporary credentials and save them to disk. Example: ./quake -useice -privkey /path/to/privkey.pem -pubkey /path/to/fullchain.pem.

entries.name: profile
entries.description: Display information about the amount of CPU cycles spend on processing game information. This command will display a list of program functions and the number of CPU cycles spend on executing each game function. The information for this command is updated every frame. This command was mostly used by the game programmers to check on the speed of the game code and to check for any problems with the code such as unnecessary processing or loops.

entries.name: -protocol
entries.description: New "-protocol x" command line option. Accepted values for 'x' are 15 (NetQuake), 666 (FitzQuake, default), and 999 (RMQ).

entries.name: -pubkey
entries.description: Specifies the certificate / fullchain file used alongside -privkey for DTLS. If not provided, it falls back to looking for fullchain.pem (and also cert.pem) in the game’s filesystem root/basedir search paths; server-side DTLS also tries /etc/ssl/certs/fullchain.pem on Unix before checking com_basedir and .der fallbacks. Like -privkey, if it still can’t find a usable pair, it will generate temporary credentials (when DTLS is enabled) and write them out. Example: ./quake -useice -privkey privkey.pem -pubkey fullchain.pem.

entries.name: -qmenu
entries.description: Using the -qmenu command-line parameter when launching the game explicitly prevents the engine from loading and using a custom menu.dat file. This forces the engine to fall back to its older, hardcoded C menu functions (the ones defined throughout the rest of menu.c). This could be used for troubleshooting menu issues or if a user prefers the classic menu style over a custom MenuQC implementation provided by a mod.

entries.name: quit
entries.description: Exit the game and return to the operating system. This command is used to leave the game and return to the operating system. When this command is used and the player is in console mode the game will just exit normally. If the game is in regular mode this command will bring up the same menu as the menu_quit command.

entries.name: -quoth
entries.description: add mission pack requests (only one should be specified)

entries.name: qwatch_aura
entries.description: Enables the local QSS-M Aura service that sends Quad Damage and Pentagram state to a paired Apple Watch, defaulting to 0. Disabling it closes the listener and stops publishing aura state.

entries.name: qwatch_pair
entries.description: Enables the QSS-M Aura listener if necessary and generates a secure six-digit Apple Watch pairing code. Each code is valid for five minutes and pairs the watch with the engine’s persistent authentication token.

entries.name: qwatch_port
entries.description: Selects the local TCP port used by the Aura companion service, defaulting to 27999. Values outside the valid non-privileged range of 1024 through 65535 fall back to the compiled default port.

entries.name: qwatch_status
entries.description: Prints whether Aura is enabled and listening, the bound port, and the token-file location. It also reports whether a pairing code is currently valid, expired, or already used.

entries.name: qwmaplist
entries.description: Displays information about the cached remote QuakeWorld map list. The reload subcommand clears and refreshes that cache.

entries.name: r_aliaslightcache
entries.description: Caches light-point samples for stationary alias models, defaulting to 1. Moving or otherwise ineligible entities continue to calculate lighting normally, preserving correctness while accelerating static model rendering.

entries.name: r_alphasort
entries.description: Attempt to sort translucent entities properly by distance

entries.name: r_ambient
entries.description: Adds a new r_ambient cvar that lets you inject a uniform ambient light level directly into the world’s lightmaps, brightening dark areas without going fullbright. When r_ambient is non-zero (and you’re not in an online deathmatch), the engine adds a clamped 0–255 ambient value into each lightmap sample and immediately rebuilds all lightmap atlases so the effect applies right away. The value is automatically clamped to the valid range, redundant rebuilds are avoided, and changes are blocked during live online deathmatch: if you try to set r_ambient there, it’s forced back to 0 and you get a one-time warning that the cvar is disabled in that mode.

entries.name: r_beaminfo
entries.description: Debug Info

entries.name: r_bmodelcache
entries.description: Enables cached indexed geometry for eligible moved brush models, defaulting to 1. The renderer falls back for translucent, dynamically lit, effected, or otherwise unsupported brush entities.

entries.name: r_bouncysparks
entries.description: Controls weather particles are allowed to bounce or no. This cvar controls bouncing particles and particles that convert to other particles on impact.

entries.name: r_brokenturbbias
entries.description: Replicates QS's bug where it ignores texture coord offsets for water (breaking curved water volumes). we do NOT ignore scales though.

entries.name: r_clearcolor
entries.description: Observer mode flyme / noclip background color outside of map. Specify a palette index from 0 to 255. Default 2.

entries.name: r_coloredpowerupglow
entries.description: Turns forced coloration of powerup glow for quad and pentagram on/off, 1 by default.

entries.name: r_decal_noperpendicular
entries.description: When enabled, decals will not be generated on planes at a steep angle from clipped decal orientation.

entries.name: r_drawcandle
entries.description: Controls whether client-side candle models are rendered for supported mods such as Copper and Arcane Dimensions, defaulting to 1. Setting it to 0 hides these automatically generated decorative candles without affecting their associated lighting.

entries.name: r_drawentities
entries.description: Toggle the display of object entities on the map. When this toggle is disabled the game will not draw any object entities on the map. This command is useful to map authors who wish to have a look at their map without drawing any objects such as lifts, buttons, or items. Mostly used for testing the maps.

entries.name: r_drawflame
entries.description: Controls whether standard progs/flame.mdl and progs/flame2.mdl entities and their associated particle effects are drawn, defaulting to 1. Setting it to 0 hides those flame models without globally disabling particles.

entries.name: r_drawflat
entries.description: If 1, polygons will be drawn as a solid color with no lightmap or texture. Default 0.

entries.name: r_drawviewmodel
entries.description: Toggle the rendering of the player’s weapon. When this toggle is disabled it will cause the rendered not to display the weapon model in front of the player. Some players like to disable this toggle which allows them to see more of the game screen and instead they depend on the crosshair for aiming. QSS Add: Accepts alpha values.

entries.name: r_drawworld
entries.description: If 1, draw world as usual. If 0, don't draw the world. Default 1. (compare r_drawentities)

entries.name: r_dynamic
entries.description: Toggle the rendering of dynamic lighting. When this toggle is disabled the game will not render any dynamic lighting, this means that when a rocket is flying or when it explodes no light will be emitted. There is a considerable amount of performance to be gained when this toggle is disabled. This will turn off powerup glows too, not good for multiplayer

entries.name: r_explosionlight
entries.description: Size of the light effect around explosions.

entries.name: r_fastsky
entries.description: If 1, sky will be rendered as solid color, for added performance. If 2, check for 24-bit external sky textures before falling back to fast sky mode, using a priority system that first looks for regular skyboxes (6-sided cubes in gfx/env/), then external sky textures (24-bit+ back/front pairs in textures/), and only falls back to solid color fast sky if neither are available. This means r_fastsky 2 will render high-quality external sky textures when they're present, providing optimal visual quality while still offering the performance benefits of fast sky mode when no sky textures are found.

entries.name: r_fastskycolor
entries.description: The color of the sky when r_fastsky 1 is set. Accepts RGB values using HEX or traditional quake color values 1-13

entries.name: r_fastturb
entries.description: Simple textures for water, teleporters, lava, slime. Like r_fastsky

entries.name: r_flatlightstyles
entries.description: If 1, styled lights (torch flicker, etc.) will be displayed as a steady light. If 2, the peak intensity will be used instead of the average intensity. Default 0.

entries.name: r_fogalpha
entries.description: This gives you a global way to control fog thickness across the entire game without having to modify individual maps. A value of 1 keeps fog the same, values below one will reduce the itensity/alpha of the fog.

entries.name: r_fullbright
entries.description: Toggle the use of lights at full brightness on the map. When this toggle is enabled the renderer system will render all textures on the map at full brightness. This will allow map authors to remove all of the lighting effects from the map. This command does not work in multiplayer games in order to prevent cheating.

entries.name: r_globalsky
entries.description: r_globalsky forces a skybox on every map by overriding the map’s sky, skyname, or qlsky worldspawn key; for example, r_globalsky dusk loads gfx/env/dusk* everywhere, while r_globalsky "" clears the override and returns to each map’s normal skybox. If the override skybox cannot be loaded, the engine automatically falls back to the map-defined sky, so values like r_globalsky storm or r_globalsky space1 are safe to test globally.`

entries.name: r_grass
entries.description: Enables and configures procedural surface grass, defaulting to 0. A single value controls the amount, while an eight-value form configures amount, blade mode, density, height, distance, movement, LOD, and gust scale.

entries.name: r_grass_tex
entries.description: Specifies which world texture names are eligible to receive procedural grass. Its default list includes ground1_1, ground1_6, wgrnd1_6, and wgrass1_1, with tokens separated by spaces, commas, or semicolons.

entries.name: r_lavaalpha
entries.description: For fine-tuning specific liquid opacities (from DirectQ/RMQEngine, non-archived, default to 0), and new worldspawn keys _wateralpha, _lavaalpha, _slimealpha, _telealpha, _skyfog (unique to Quakespasm, similar to the behaviour of the "fog" worldspawn key).

entries.name: r_lerpmodels
entries.description: If 1, do interpolation on model animations, with exceptions for torches (r_nolerp_list) & muzzleflares (interpolation is suspended for two frames if EF_MUZZLEFLASH is encountered, on the assumption a muzzleflare happens at the same time.) If 2, lerp all animations, without exception. If 0, disable interpolation (to mimic standard quake.) Default 0. QSSM Adds option 3 to allow more animations but with adjusted frames.

entries.name: r_lerpmove
entries.description: If 1, do movement interpolation on MOVETYPE_STEP entities (i.e. monsters.) If 0, disable interpolation (to mimic standard quake.) I recommend that you use r_lerpmove and r_lerpmodels together, or turn them both off, otherwise monsters will move strangely. Default 0.

entries.name: r_lightflicker
entries.description: The r_lightflicker console variable determines whether the dynamic lights associated with particle effects exhibit a flickering behavior in their radius. When set to its default value of "1", the calculation for the light's radius incorporates a variable component derived from a flicker value, causing the radius to fluctuate over time and creating a simulated flickering effect. Conversely, setting r_lightflicker to "0" replaces this variable term with a constant factor, resulting in a stable, non-flickering radius for the particle's dynamic light. In essence, r_lightflicker "1" enables this radius flicker for particle lights, while "0" disables it, keeping the light size constant.

entries.name: r_lightmap
entries.description: All textures will be replaced with plain white, leaving only lighting information. You can check lightmaps in a GL or DirectX source port using the r_lightmap console variable

entries.name: r_lightmap_extra4
entries.description: Enables bounded multi-sample filtering that approximates ericw-tools -extra4 smoothing for legacy lightmaps, defaulting to 0. Sampling is clamped to each surface’s lightmap bounds to avoid bleeding from neighboring atlas regions.

entries.name: r_lightmap_format
entries.description: r_lightmap_format controls which OpenGL texture format is used for brush lightmaps, allowing HDR-capable packed formats or standard 8-bit uploads. Valid values include rgb9_e5/rgb9e5/e5bgr9, rgb10_a2/rgb10a2/rgb10, rgba8/rgbx8, and bgra8/bgrx8; for example, r_lightmap_format rgb9_e5 selects GL_RGB9_E5, while r_lightmap_format rgba8 forces a normal 8-bit RGBA lightmap upload. The cvar’s default value is "", which acts as auto: if left blank or set to an unsupported value, the engine falls back to rgb9_e5, then rgb10_a2, then rgba depending on renderer support.

entries.name: r_model_light_desat
entries.description: r_alias_light_desat is a console variable that controls the desaturation (removal of color) of lighting on alias models (3D models like players, weapons, and items) to create a more neutral or monochromatic appearance. The cvar accepts integer values from -2 to +2, where 0 disables the effect completely, positive values (1 or 2) apply desaturation only to models listed in the r_alias_light_desat_list cvar, and negative values (-1 or -2) apply desaturation to either all models except viewmodels (-1) or use different effects for viewmodels versus other models (-2). When enabled with positive values, it converts colored lighting to grayscale by averaging the RGB components while preserving brightness (effect type 1), or forces full white lighting (effect type 2), and the r_alias_light_desat_list cvar contains a comma-separated list of model names (like "progs/player.mdl,progs/bolt.mdl") that determines which specific models are affected by the desaturation effect.

entries.name: r_models_light_desat_list
