entries.description: Models on this list will be affected when r_alias_light_desat has a value

entries.name: r_nolerp_list
entries.description: Contains a comma-separated list of filenames of models to exclude from lerping. Filename must include the relative path and extension, for example "progs/flame.mdl". The default is "progs/flame.mdl,progs/flame2.mdl,progs/braztall.mdl,progs/brazshrt.mdl,progs/longtrch.mdl,progs/flame_pyre.mdl,progs/v_saw.mdl,progs/v_xfist.mdl,progs/h2stuff/newfire.mdl". This should include all torches in id1, quoth, and bastion, which look bad when lerped, and the zerstorer chainsaw and xmen fist, which also look bad lerped.

entries.name: r_nooutline_list
entries.description: Excludes models from outlines when r_outline is enabled. Default: "progs/bolt1.mdl,progs/bolt2.mdl,progs/bolt3.mdl,progs/bit.mdl, progs/star.mdl"

entries.name: r_norefresh
entries.description: Toggle the redrawing of the game screen.

entries.name: r_noshadow_list
entries.description: Disable shadows for these models if r_shadows enabled.

entries.name: r_novis
entries.description: Toggle the use of VIS information from the map data. When this toggle is enabled the game will calculate it’s own VIS information on the fly instead of using the information stored in the map data. This will cause a server drop in performance in the game. When this toggle is enabled and the variable r_wateralpha has a value lower than 1 the player will be able to see through liquids. This is a nice effect to see but it is not recommended to keep this toggle enabled because of the server performance penalty. It is possible to enable transparent water and still keep this toggle enabled. You would have to visit the official Water VIS site at http://www.sod.net/ and download the vispatch program along with the patch data files which you would use to update the VIS data for all of your game maps.

entries.name: r_oldskyleaf
entries.description: If 0, surfaces inside sky leaves will be skipped by the renderer. If 1, they will be drawn whenever they are in your PVS, just like any other surface. Default 0.

entries.name: r_outline
entries.description: Accepts values 0-5, adds outline to models. Exclude models using r_nooutline_list

entries.name: r_outline_minpixels
entries.description: Sets the projected-pixel cutoff for ordinary model outlines, defaulting to 1. Outlines fade as they approach the cutoff and are skipped below it to avoid invisible extra rendering passes; 0 disables this optimization.

entries.name: r_part_beams
entries.description: This toggle controls the rendering and spawning of beam‑style effects (e.g., lightning‑gun shafts and laser streaks). When set to 0 the engine skips both beam allocation and their GPU draw calls, giving a large CPU and GPU win on effect‑heavy maps. Values are 0 (disable) or 1 (default ‑ enable). Use it when lightning‑gun visuals are less important than raw framerate.

entries.name: r_part_contentswitch
entries.description: r_part_contentswitch enables dynamic particle behavior based on the content type of the environment, making effects context-sensitive. This is useful for enhancing realism by altering particles' visual behavior according to whether they are in air, water, or other environments.

entries.name: r_part_cullbehind
entries.description: Enables culling particles that are safely behind the camera, defaulting to 1. Particle radius and velocity are considered so large or fast-moving effects are not removed prematurely.

entries.name: r_part_density
entries.description: Reduce particles for more minimal effect. When r_part_density is set to a higher value, more particles are generated for each effect, leading to denser and potentially more visually striking particle effects. Conversely, a lower value reduces the particle count, making effects appear lighter or more sparse.

entries.name: r_part_mapdecals
entries.description: Enables static map decal entities such as misc_decal, defaulting to 1. Changing it rebuilds or removes decals generated from the current map’s entity data.

entries.name: r_part_maxdecals
entries.description: Sets the hard limit for live decal fragments such as bullet holes or scorch marks. When the pool is full, the oldest decals are recycled to keep memory bounded. Raising the limit keeps marks visible for longer but increases RAM and may impact streaming to the GPU. Lowering it (e.g., 2048) is an easy way to trim VRAM on low‑end systems.

entries.name: r_part_maxparticles
entries.description: Defines the maximum number of live particles that can exist at once. If the pool is exhausted the engine starts re‑using the oldest particles, which can shorten certain effects. A smaller cap reduces memory and prevents rare spikes where mods spawn millions of particles, but too small (e.g., below 16384) may cause visible popping in big battles. Tune it alongside r_part_density for best balance.

entries.name: r_part_rain
entries.description: Master on/off switch for the sky‑based rain/snow system driven by the map’s sky surfaces. Setting it to 0 disables all weather, eliminating per‑frame surface scans and thousands of extra particles outdoors. Use 1 (default) to keep weather visuals, then fine‑tune intensity with r_part_rain_quantity. Recommended to disable on integrated GPUs for a quick FPS boost.

entries.name: r_part_rain_quantity
entries.description: Scales the number of raindrops or snowflakes emitted per sky surf when weather is enabled. 1 is the reference density defined by the particle script; fractions like 0.25 quarter the drop count, giving a big perf win while still hinting at weather. Has no effect if r_part_rain is 0. Can be bumped above 1 for cinematic downpours on high‑end rigs.

entries.name: r_part_sparks
entries.description: Toggles simple, un‑textured spark particles often used for bullet impacts and metal hits. 0 disables them entirely, while ‑1 (if supported) converts them to invisible placeholders so mods that query the effect still run. Because each spark may perform collision and bounce traces, disabling them can meaningfully cut CPU cost in firefights. Combine with the next two cvars to fine‑grain spark variants.

entries.name: r_part_sparks_textured
entries.description: Controls textured spark billboards, a nicer‑looking but slightly heavier variant of plain sparks. Turning it off (0) reverts those definitions to the faster un‑textured path (provided r_part_sparks is still 1). Disabling both this and r_part_sparks removes all spark effects. Ideal for players who want sparks but can sacrifice the extra overdraw of textures.

entries.name: r_part_sparks_trifan
entries.description: Enables the triangle‑fan spark mode, which draws each spark as a mini cone for bloom‑style glints. This adds three times the geometry versus single‑quad sparks; switching to 0 falls back to the cheapest point or billboard form. Visual difference is subtle, so lowering it is a free optimisation on cluttered scenes. Has no effect if sparks are globally disabled.

entries.name: r_part_vbo
entries.description: Enables streaming particle geometry through OpenGL vertex buffers. It defaults to 1 on most platforms but 0 on Apple, where synchronous buffer updates can be slower than client arrays.

entries.name: r_particle_tracelimit
entries.description: Sets a hard upper bound on the number of collision traces the particle system may perform per frame. The default is effectively “unlimited (0x7fffffff is unlimited),” letting ricocheting sparks bounce as much as they like—great for fidelity, bad for CPU spikes. Clamping to something sane (e.g., 64) prevents runaway costs on dense effects while still allowing convincing bounces. Once the budget is hit, additional particles skip their collision step until the next frame. One of the better 80/20 fixes for faster particles

entries.name: r_particledesc
entries.description: Select a particle set in id1/particles or gamedir/particles

entries.name: r_particles
entries.description: 0 = no particles, 1 = circular particles (glquake), 2 = square particles (winquake) Default 1.

entries.name: r_partinfo
entries.description: Full list of effects

entries.name: r_partredirect
entries.description: Add an emit/trail effect to all ents using said model

entries.name: r_player_xray
entries.description: The r_player_xray cvar renders player models as colored silhouettes visible through walls, accepting a flexible string format of "<hexcolor> <alpha> <distance> [targets] [pcolor] [gametype=N]" where all parameters are optional. Set it to something like "0xFF0000 0.8 2048 enemy" to see red enemy outlines at 80% opacity within 2048 units, or use "0x00FF00 0.5 4096 both gametype=2" to show green x-ray for all players within 4096 units but only in 2v2 or smaller matches. You can also use "pcolor 3072 both" to render each player's outline in their own shirt/pants colors instead of a fixed color, or add enemycolor=0xFF0000 teamcolor=0x00B7FF to split team and enemy colors explicitly. Set it to "0" to disable the effect entirely.

entries.name: r_pos
entries.description: Show player position.

entries.name: r_poweruplightflicker
entries.description: Enables classic randomized radius flicker on powerup and dim entity lights, defaulting to 0. When disabled, those lights use stable radii of 416 and 216 rather than a randomized 32-unit range.

entries.name: r_quadparticles
entries.description: If 1, particles are drawn as GL_QUADS instead of GL_TRIANGLES. Quads use 4 verts instead of 3, but the fillrate cost is 1/2 that of triangles. Depending on your card, either one may be faster. This cvar has no effect on the appearance of particles. Default 1.

entries.name: r_remove_collinear_vertices
entries.description: Removes redundant collinear brush-surface vertices to avoid zero-area triangles, defaulting to 1. It is only compiled and registered when MACBOOK_ARM_HACK is enabled, so it will not appear in ordinary Windows builds.

entries.name: r_replacemodels
entries.description: The r_replacemodels cvar allows you to specify a comma-separated list of file extensions that the engine will attempt to use for loading models before defaulting to the extension specified in the game code (QC). For each model, the engine will try to load a file with the original name but appended with each extension from this list, in the order provided. For example, if r_replacemodels is set to "iqm,md3" and the game tries to load progs/monster.mdl, the engine will first look for progs/monster.iqm, then progs/monster.md3, and if neither is found, it will finally attempt to load progs/monster.mdl. The actual model format is determined by the file's header, not the extension itself; supported formats include IQM, MD5Mesh, MD3, MDL (Quake Alias), SPR (Sprite), and BSP (Brush). If you intend for your replacement models to be optional, perhaps tied to performance presets, you might use a distinct extension like .md3 so they might be skipped if a 'fast' preset is active (assuming the preset logic or user configuration omits .md3 from r_replacemodels). Conversely, to ensure your replacement models are always used across all presets or to avoid potential naming conflicts and hacks, you could rename your replacement model file to match the exact filename and extension that the QC expects, or use r_replacemodels with an extension that you know will take precedence. For instance, setting r_replacemodels "iqm" would prioritize .iqm files for all models where such a replacement exists. Using the IQM format can be a strong choice if your replacement models feature numerous animations or require sophisticated control over individual parts via QC, offering advantages over formats like MD3 which can sometimes exhibit disjointed appearances for complex player models. As another example, if you only want to replace a specific weapon model, say progs/v_shotgun.mdl, with an MD5 version, you could place your progs/v_shotgun.md5mesh file in your mod directory and set r_replacemodels "md5mesh"; the engine would then load your custom shotgun model while leaving other models unaffected unless corresponding .md5mesh files exist for them too.

entries.name: r_rocketlight
entries.description: Original behavior or a rocket emitting light

entries.name: r_scale
entries.description: Set to 2, 3, or 4 to render the view at 1/2, 1/3, or 1/4 resolution

entries.name: r_scenecache
entries.description: The r_scenecache console variable controls a performance optimization for caching scene geometry. Although its literal default value is an empty string (""), the engine effectively treats this default as a numeric value of 1. This 1 setting enables the scene cache and attempts to "bake" static-looking brush model entities (like stationary doors or platforms) into the cache alongside the main world geometry for faster rendering. Setting r_scenecache specifically to 2, however, disables only the brush model baking part of this optimization; the cache will still contain the static world geometry, but all brush models will be drawn dynamically. Conversely, setting r_scenecache to 0 disables the scene cache entirely. Therefore, mode 2 prevents the optimization of baking static brush models, which might be useful for debugging cache-related rendering issues or ensuring simpler cache behavior, potentially at the cost of performance compared to the effective default mode 1.

entries.name: r_shadows
entries.description: Toggle the rendering of shadows for models. When this toggle is enabled the game will try to render shadows under all objects and players. The shadows sometimes look out of place. The implementation of this toggle was only to see if the designers could create dynamic shadows and it wasn’t meant for general use.  Adjust opacity with values below 1. Example: r_shadows .4

entries.name: r_shadows_bmodels
entries.description: Apply shadows to brush models like r_shadows. Float values accepted

entries.name: r_shadows_buffered
entries.description: Enables indexed-buffer rendering for brush-model shadows, defaulting to 1. It uses cached geometry and a shared VBO when available, with immediate-mode rendering retained as the fallback.

entries.name: r_shadows_groundcheck
entries.description: verify shadows cast only on the ground for rotating models (e.g., ultrav quad, ctf2m8 quad)

entries.name: r_showbboxes
entries.description: If 1, draw a wireframe bounding box around each entity. Note that these are the server-side per-edict physics bounding boxes, not the client-side per-model rendering bboxes. If 0, disable this feature. Default 0. QSSM: For the old (white) version use negative values for r_showbboxes (-1 = all entities, -2 = PVS only)

entries.name: r_showbboxes_filter
entries.description: filter "r_showbboxes" entities by classname substring

entries.name: r_showfields
entries.description: r_showfields displays a debug overlay for the server entity closest to the crosshair, including its classname, relevant fields, and linked targets. Set r_showfields 1 to show the full field panel in the bottom-right corner, or r_showfields 2 to anchor that panel near the focused entity in the world. Typical examples are r_showfields 1 for stable inspection while testing a map, r_showfields 2 for in-world debugging of triggers and targets, and r_showfields 0 to turn the overlay off.

entries.name: r_showhull
entries.summary: Displays collision hulls for debugging; 0 disables the display.
entries.description: Use h0 for the point-collision boundary, h1 for the normal-player origin boundary, or h2 for the large-monster origin boundary. Optional ,diff and ,info suffixes provide comparison and diagnostic views. The default is 0.

entries.name: r_showlocs
entries.description: A value of 1 will show all the locs loaded into memory using the QW LOC creator commands, a value of 2 will show the loaded locations from the automatically loaded loc if there is one for the level. Values of 2 support both NQ and QW locs, whereas values of 1 only support QW locs (single point system). A value of 3 only shows in text the location on screen, see r_showlocs_y to adjust vertical location on screen

entries.name: r_showlocs_y
entries.description: Vertical position on screen for r_showlocs 3

entries.name: r_showtris
entries.description: If 1, draw wireframe outlines for every triangle in the scene. Like in Quake 3, the lines will be visible even through solid geometry. If 2, draw the outlines only on visible surfaces (like r_showtris 2 in Medal of Honor.) If 0, disable wireframe overlay. Default 0.

entries.name: r_sky_quality
entries.description: Higher number divides the sky more, for a smoother effect and slower performance. Default 12. Range 1-64

entries.name: r_skyalpha
entries.description: Sets the alpha of the front sky layer. Note that if sky alpha is less than 1.0, the sky will be drawn in two passes even if you have multitexture. Default 1.

entries.name: r_skyfog
entries.description: Controls how much the sky is obscured by the fog. 0 = sky is completely unfogged, 1 = sky is completely fogged. Default 0.5. skyfog affects the skybox rendering, fog does not. an overlay of the fog color over the sky. skyfog helps to blend the fog into the skybox better. at skyfog 1 the sky will be a flat color, the color of your fog

entries.name: r_skyspeed
entries.description: Speed of tradional sky. Float values up to 100

entries.name: r_skywind
entries.description: The r_skywind cvar adds an animated scrolling wind effect to skybox textures, simulating drifting clouds or atmospheric movement. When set to a single value like r_skywind 1, it acts as a rate multiplier that enables the effect and looks for wind parameters from config files or worldspawn; when set to four values like r_skywind "1 45 30 0", it directly specifies distance (wind strength, -2 to 2), yaw (direction in degrees), period (seconds per full scroll cycle), and pitch (vertical angle). Setting it to 0 disables the effect entirely. Skywind supports a layered configuration system with multiple sources of wind parameters. Map authors can embed wind settings directly in their BSP by adding a "skywind" key to worldspawn (e.g., "skywind" "0.5 90 60 0"), which takes priority and provides per-map tuning without any client-side files. For per-skybox configuration, place a file named <skyboxname>_wind.cfg in gfx/env/ (e.g., gfx/env/mak_cloudysky4_wind.cfg) containing a line like skywind 0.3 270 40 0, and it will automatically load whenever that skybox is active. If neither a worldspawn key nor a per-skybox config is found, the system falls back to the global default config or the cvar value itself. For a global default that applies across many skyboxes, place a skywind_default.cfg in gfx/env/. This file begins with the wind parameters in the format skywind <distance> <yaw> <period> <pitch> (e.g., skywind 1 45 30 0), followed by optional include and exclude rules that control which skyboxes receive the effect. The filtering logic operates in two distinct modes depending on whether any include lines are present. If the file contains no include lines at all, it runs in exclude-only mode — the wind effect applies to every skybox by default, and only skyboxes explicitly listed with exclude <skyname> are skipped. This is the simpler approach when most of your skyboxes look fine with wind and you just need to blacklist the few that do not. For example, adding exclude city_night would disable wind for that sky while leaving it active on everything else. If the file contains at least one include line, it switches to whitelist mode — the wind effect is restricted to only the skyboxes explicitly named with include <skyname>, and all others are ignored. This is ideal when you have many skyboxes installed but only a handful that actually look good with scrolling clouds, such as include day, include mak_nighsky3_, include overcast_sky. The exclude directive always takes priority over include — if a skybox name appears in both, the exclude wins and that sky will not get wind. This lets you maintain a broad whitelist while surgically removing individual entries without deleting the include line. Note that skywind works best with skyboxes featuring soft, diffuse cloud patterns — skyboxes containing hard-edged objects like suns, moons, or mountains will produce visible distortion artifacts since the texture is being physically shifted. Slow, subtle movement (low distance values like 0.3–0.5 with longer periods) tends to look the most natural. Related commands like skywind_save, skywind_load, skywind_lookdir, and skywind_rotate are available for interactively tuning and persisting wind settings.

entries.name: r_slimealpha
entries.description: For fine-tuning specific liquid opacities (from DirectQ/RMQEngine, non-archived, default to 0), and new worldspawn keys _wateralpha, _lavaalpha, _slimealpha, _telealpha, _skyfog (unique to Quakespasm, similar to the behaviour of the "fog" worldspawn key).

entries.name: r_softemu
entries.description: Applies palette-based software-renderer emulation as a postprocess, defaulting to 0. Modes are 1 for a dithered WinQuake-like look, 2 for chunkier filtered output, and 3 for raw banded output without dithering.

entries.name: r_speeds
entries.description: Toggle the display of information about the renderer performance. This command will give some statistics about the speed of the renderer. The information is displayed for every frame. The first value shows the total time required to render that frame, the next three values display the number of polygons which were rendered, and the last value is the number of surfaces which have been rendered.

entries.name: r_stereo
entries.description: If nonzero, the scene will be rendered once in red, and again in cyan, with the two views shifted slightly. If you have 3D glasses you can appreciate this (assumes that the left eye is red and the right eye is cyan.) The value of r_stereo sets the eye separation. If your glasses have red on the right eye, use a negative value to flip the views. Default 0.

entries.name: r_stereodepth
entries.description: Sets the distance at which the two views will converge when stereo rendering is active.

entries.name: r_telealpha
entries.description: For fine-tuning specific liquid opacities (from DirectQ/RMQEngine, non-archived, default to 0), and new worldspawn keys _wateralpha, _lavaalpha, _slimealpha, _telealpha, _skyfog (unique to Quakespasm, similar to the behaviour of the "fog" worldspawn key).

entries.name: r_textureless_dither
entries.description: Dithers textureless world lighting to conceal visible 8-bit lightmap bands, defaulting to 0. The shader applies it specifically when textureless rendering is selected through gl_max_size 1.

entries.name: r_vfog
entries.description: Is a placeholder for volumetric-fog rendering with a nominal default of 1. Its implementation functions are empty and its registration is commented out, so it is not currently a usable console CVar.

entries.name: r_viewmodel_quake
entries.description: Set to 1 for WinQuake gun position (from MarkV).

entries.name: r_wateralpha
entries.description: For fine-tuning specific liquid opacities (from DirectQ/RMQEngine, non-archived, default to 0), and new worldspawn keys _wateralpha, _lavaalpha, _slimealpha, _telealpha, _skyfog (unique to Quakespasm, similar to the behaviour of the "fog" worldspawn key).

entries.name: r_waterwarp
entries.description: If 0, no underwater warping will take place. Default 1.

entries.name: randmap
entries.description: Load a random map.

entries.name: random
entries.description: Takes an arbitrary number of arguments, selects one at random, and sends either a 'say' command or prints to the console. This new feature allows players to randomly select an option from a given list, enhancing interactivity within the game.

entries.name: rcon
entries.description: To utilize Remote Console (RCON) for server administration, a specific password, distinct from the main server connection password, must be configured. The server administrator establishes this by setting the rcon_password console variable (cvar) on the server. This is typically done by adding a line like rcon_password "my_admin_secret" to the server's configuration file (e.g., server.cfg) or by typing this command directly into the live server console. Once the server's rcon_password is active, any administrator wishing to send commands remotely must first configure their game client with the matching RCON password. In the client's console, the administrator would type rcon_password "my_admin_secret". After their client-side rcon_password is correctly set, they can then execute commands on the server using the rcon command followed by the desired server command, for instance, rcon changelevel q2dm1. The server will only accept and process these RCON commands if the RCON password provided by the client matches the rcon_password set on the server.

The server will only accept and process these RCON commands if the RCON password provided by the client matches the rcon_password set on the server.

entries.name: reconnect
entries.description: Reconnect to the server.  If you become disconnected from the server you can use this command to quickly reconnect to the server without having to use the connect command again. This is very useful if you overflow from the server or when your network connection fails. If you have not connected to a server it will use server history (QSSM change)

entries.name: record
entries.description: Typing record with no arguments will record a demo to id1/demos with the map name and date as the file name

entries.name: -refreshrate
entries.description: Set refreshrate

entries.name: registered
entries.description: Toggle if the game is considered to be the full version or the shareware. The value for this variable will be determined during the time that the game is first started. The game will check for the presence of the pak1.pak file and also the gfx/pop.lmp file and if those files exist it will be considered that the game is the registered full version and access to all of the episodes will be provided. This variable is only useful if you have the shareware version of the game and you wish to see the ThunderBolt weapon on the start level. You can enable this toggle, set the deathmatch variable to 1, and then use the map start command to start the game. Proceed to the slipgate which leads to the 3rd episode and you will be able to see the ThunderBolt. The gfx/pop.lmp is supposed to be the proof-of-purchase file, it is only 256-bytes and it contains a ASCII picture of the letter “Q” as seen in Quake.

entries.name: removeloc
entries.description: QW LOC Creator: 'removeloc' will remove a location by the given name, for example 'removeloc ra'

entries.name: reset
entries.description: Resets a SINGLE cvar to default. Note that this is the engine default, not the default.cfg value.

entries.name: resetall
entries.description: Resets ALL cvars to defaults

entries.name: resetcfg
entries.description: Resets ONLY cvars that save to the config via internal CVAR_ARCHIVE to defaults. Not all cvars save to config and can only be set in game, or via autoexec on load.

entries.name: restart
entries.description: Restart the current game. When this command is used it will restart the current map in a single-player mode. This command is useful to map authors who have to reload their map constantly with new updates.

entries.name: resurrect
entries.description: Bring yourself back to life with 3 seconds of protection

entries.name: -rogue
entries.description: add mission pack requests (only one should be specified)

entries.name: rotatemodel
entries.description: The rotatemodel command is your main way to inspect and edit the live client-side rotation list that cl_rot persists. In its basic form, rotatemodel <ax> <ay> <az> <mdl1[,mdl2...]> assigns a spin of <ax ay az> degrees per second to one or more models (comma-separated), immediately affecting any matching entities (except player models, which are intentionally ignored). You can manage the list with subcommands: rotatemodel list prints all current entries and shows the raw cl_rot string, rotatemodel clear wipes the in-memory list (but does not touch cl_rot), rotatemodel reload/rotatemodel revert rebuilds the runtime list from the current cl_rot value, and rotatemodel save serializes the current runtime list back into cl_rot so it’s written out to your config. In practice, you tweak spins interactively with rotatemodel while in-game, then run rotatemodel save once you’re happy so those rules survive a restart.

entries.name: s
entries.description: Alias/shortcut to say (messagmode)

entries.name: samelevel
entries.description: Toggle the constant cycling of the same map on a server. When this toggle is enabled the game will play the same map over and over again all the time. If the players exit the map the game will end and the server will restart on the same map. This toggle might be useful if somebody wants to have a dedicated server which runs only one map all the time.

entries.name: save
entries.description: Save the current game to a file. This command is used to save games. The saved game files are usually stored in the quake/id1/ directory. The filenames for the saved games will start with s0.sav and go onto s11.sav. The save file from the Quick Save feature will have the filename quick.sav. You can use this command to create save games with any name. Also, you can only save games in the directories below the quake/id1/ directory such as quake/id1/save/.

entries.name: saved1
entries.description: Server variable for use custom mod use.

entries.name: saved2
entries.description: Server variable for use custom mod use.

entries.name: saved3
entries.description: Server variable for use custom mod use.

entries.name: saved4
entries.description: Server variable for use custom mod use.

entries.name: savedgamecfg
entries.description: Server variable for use custom mod use.

entries.name: saveloc
entries.description: QW LOC Creator: save a .loc file with all the added locations from 'addloc'. tab will complete name of current loaded map

entries.name: say
entries.description: Send a message to all players on the server. This command is very similar in usage to the messagemode command except that you can use this command inside aliases and in bindings to automatically send messages to other players with the press of a single key. Many players use this command and create bindings which send frequently uses messages, this saves them time typing in the same responses all the time.

entries.name: say_team
entries.description: Send a message to players only on your team. This command is very similar in usage to the messagemode2 command except that you can use this command inside aliases and in bindings to automatically send messages to other players with the press of a single key. Many players use this command and create bindings which send frequently uses messages, this saves them time typing in the same messages during team games, especially clan matches.

entries.name: scr_autoid
entries.description: Shows the name of the player you are looking at for observers and in demos. A value of 2 will show in practice mode and pre match. Float values will add a black background with adjustable transparency

entries.name: scr_autoscale
entries.description: Automatically calculates a user-interface scale from the current rendering resolution. It applies the result to the console, menus, status bar, and crosshair.

entries.name: scr_centerprintbg
entries.description: 0 = off (default), 1 = classic text box, 2 = black opague, 3 = black opague full screen

entries.name: scr_centertime
entries.description: The amount of time in seconds that center printed messages stay on the screen.  It might be necessary to set this variable to a higher value in order to read some of the large messages which are displayed in the game. A good value to set this variable to is 5, so that messages stay long enough on the screen in order to finish reading the completely.

entries.name: scr_clock
entries.description: Displays a real-time clock in the lower right corner. Values: 1 - level time (MM:SS), 2 - 12-hour system clock (HH:MM AM/PM), 3 - 24-hour system clock (HH:MM:SS), 4 - date only for screenshots (MM/DD/YYYY), 5 - date and 12-hour time (MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM AM/PM), 6 - date and 24-hour time (MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM:SS), 7 - dynamic (date MM/DD/YY when scores are visible, otherwise 12-hour time), 8 - dynamic (date MM/DD/YY when scores are visible, otherwise 24-hour time). (Default: 0)

entries.name: scr_conalpha
entries.description: This is the opacity when the console is halfscreen. Default 1. Set to 0.6 to mimic glquake.

entries.name: scr_conback
entries.description: scr_conback is a console variable that allows players to specify a custom background image for the console instead of using the default gfx/conback.lmp texture. When set to a non-empty string, the game will attempt to load the specified image file from the gfx/ directory (or use the path as-is if it already starts with "gfx/") and display it as the console background. If the custom image fails to load or if scr_conback is empty, the game falls back to using the default console background image.

entries.name: scr_concolor
entries.description: Set color to a simple color with original quake colors or RGB values via 0x00000

entries.name: scr_conscale
entries.description: Scales the console text larger, but only has an effect when scr_conwidth is 0. Default 1.

entries.name: scr_consize
entries.description: Vertical length of the console when game active, default is half screen at .5

entries.name: scr_conspeed
entries.description: The speed at which the console screen lowers. Some people prefer to have instantaneous access to the console, they usually set this variable to a very high value such as 100000.

entries.name: scr_conwidth
entries.description: Sets the virtual console width, where smaller numbers means larger text. Values larger than window width, or smaller than 320, will be clamped to that range, and all values will be rounded to a multiple of 8. If 0, the window width will be used. Note: values that divide evenly into the window width will make the text look nicest. Default 0.

entries.name: scr_crosshair_x
entries.description: Adjust x value of crosshair on screen

entries.name: scr_crosshair_y
entries.description: Adjust y value of crosshair on screen

entries.name: scr_crosshairalpha
entries.description: Set opacity/alpha to the crosshair

entries.name: scr_crosshaircolor
entries.description: The color of the crosshair. Accepts RGB values using HEX or traditional quake color values 1-13

entries.name: scr_crosshaircshift
entries.description: When cl_damaghue is enabled this is the color the crosshair will change to upon taking damage. Accepts RGB values using HEX or traditional quake color values 1-13

entries.name: scr_crosshairoutline
entries.description: Black outline aroud crosshairs for better visibility

entries.name: scr_crosshairscale
entries.description: Scales the crosshair larger. 1 = normal, 10 = maximum enlargement. Default 1.

entries.name: scr_customcursor
entries.description: Toggle using QSSM custom cursor from qssm.pak

entries.name: scr_demobar_timeout
entries.description: controls the amount of time demo info (name, playback speed/status) is displayed on screen. <0 = never show, 0 = always show, >0 = show for the given amount of time after an interaction, (default: 1 second)

entries.name: scr_fade
entries.description: Sets the duration of the startup and quit screen fades in seconds, defaulting to 0.15; 0 disables fading. Positive values fade only at startup, while negative values use their absolute duration and enable both startup and quit fades.

entries.name: scr_hints
entries.description: During a match pause, display some client hints

entries.name: scr_match_hud
entries.description: Displays CRMOD / CRCTF match timer, scores, flagstatus in upper right hand corner of screen. This is the equivalent to Qrack's scr_printstats. In practice mode no dispaly, FFA clock only. Values: 0 - no display, 1 - display on. (Default: 1)

entries.name: scr_matchclock
entries.description: CRMOD User adjustable matchclock. Supports three values: 1 for large brown digits, 2 for large red digits, and 3 for the console font. For values 1 and 2, tenths of a number, like 2.1, set the black border width.

entries.name: scr_matchclock_countup
entries.description: Chooses whether the CRMod7 match clock displays elapsed time instead of the normal countdown, defaulting to 0. Mode 1 counts upward, but only while the engine has valid CRMod7 elapsed-time information.

entries.name: scr_matchclock_x

entries.name: scr_menuscale
entries.description: Sets the scale factor for menus and other centered overlays. If 1, images will be drawn at 1:1 scale. If 2, images will be double size. Menus will never be drawn smaller than 1:1, and never larger than the size of the window. Note: integer values will make the text look nicest. Default 1.

entries.name: scr_movekeys
entries.description: Show movement keys on screen

entries.name: scr_obscenterprint
entries.description: Print server provided centerprints in observing mode

entries.name: scr_obsitems
entries.description: Display observer items and timers on CRx mods

entries.name: scr_ofsx
entries.description: The value in pixles that the game screen is offset on the x-axis. This variable can be used to move the game screen on the x-axis relative to the position of the player thus enabling the player to view the game from a different perspective. The x-axis in the game is the axis on which the player moves forward and back. You can set this variable to a value such as -100 to give the impression that the player is control a flying weapon while watching it remotely through a chasing camera.

entries.name: scr_ofsy
entries.description: The value in pixles that the game screen is offset on the y-axis. This variable can be used to move the game screen on the x-axis relative to the position of the player thus enabling the player to view the game from a different perspective. The y-axis in the game is the axis on which the player moves left and right. You can set this variable to a value such as -75 which would give the impression that the player is holding the weapon in his right hand.

entries.name: scr_ofsz
entries.description: The value in pixles that the game screen is offset on the z-axis. This variable can be used to move the game screen on the x-axis relative to the position of the player thus enabling the player to view the game from a different perspective. The z-axis in the game is the axis on which the player moves up and down. You can set this variable to a value such as -50 to give the impression that the player is driving a really small tank in the game.

entries.name: scr_ping
entries.description: Displays ping and packet loss in the lower-left corner when connected to a server. Packet loss is shown only when drops occur. Updates every 5 seconds. Values: 0 = hide, 1 = show ping (ms), 2 = show ping (no ms), 3 = show ping (ms) and packet loss (pl) text (Default: 1).

entries.name: scr_printspeed
entries.description: The speed at which the final message is displayed at the end of each episode. You might want to increase the value for this variable because the default setting is just too slow. Also, below is the ending message from the first episode of the game.

entries.name: scr_sbar
entries.description: Changes between default sbar/HUD, QW style sbar/HUD, or QE (Quake re-release). Default 1, sbar 2 for QW style, 3 for QE

entries.name: scr_sbaralpha
entries.description: Controls the transparency of the statusbar background. 0 = invisible, 1 = opaque (original quake behavior), in-between values give different levels of transparency. Pro tip: set it to 0.99 and it will still appear opaque, but the 3D view will expand to fill the area on both sides of the statusbar. Default 1.

entries.name: scr_sbaralphaqwammo
entries.description: Alpha for the background ammo counts

entries.name: scr_sbarfacecolor
entries.description: Show pants color around status bar face

entries.name: scr_sbarscale
entries.description: Sets the scale factor for the statusbar. If 1, images will be drawn at 1:1 scale. If 2, images will be double size. The statusbar will never be drawn smaller than 1:1, and never larger than the width of the window. Note: integer values will make the text look nicest. Default 1.

entries.name: scr_sbarshowqeammo
entries.description: Set to 0 to not sure QE scr_sbar 3 ammo iventory (preference for bloodrails)

entries.name: scr_scopealpha
entries.description: This cvar controls the maximum opacity of the darkened area outside the scope's central circle when you are fully zoomed in. A value of 1 makes the outside area completely black, while 0 makes it fully transparent. Adjusting this determines how much the peripheral view is obscured during zoom.

entries.name: scr_scopefadespeed
entries.description: This cvar determines the speed at which the scope overlay effect fades in and out as you zoom past the 50% threshold. Higher values create a quicker, more abrupt transition, while lower values result in a slower, smoother fade. It essentially controls the visual responsiveness of the zoom effect's vignette.

entries.name: scr_scoperadius
entries.description: This setting defines the radius of the clear, circular viewing area within the scope overlay. The value is a fraction (from 0.05 to 0.49) of the smaller screen dimension (height or width). Changing this value alters the size of the visible zoomed-in region.

entries.name: scr_scoreboard_teamsort
entries.description: Sort socreboard frags by teams when available, not by frag counts. A value of 1 to enable.

entries.name: scr_showfps
entries.description: If 1, FPS are displayed. Default 0. A value of 2 will get rid of the fps text

entries.name: scr_showgrenadecounter
entries.description: Visual grendade timer to practice grenade jumps

entries.name: scr_shownet
entries.description: Enable or disable showing the lag icon in upper left Accepts float values from 0 to 10 for seconds. 0 - no display, 5 - wait 5 seconds then display. QS default is 0.3

entries.name: scr_showscores
entries.description: Optional on screen scores (scoreboard) display in lower left corner.

entries.name: scr_showspeed
entries.description: Values 2 and 3 show a speedometer, value of 1 shows just numbers. Displays drawing of your current speed near sbar. Values: 3 - bars with power bunny errors, 2 - bars, 1 - show, 0 - no show. (Default: 0)

entries.name: scr_showspeed_y
entries.description: Vertical position in center of screen for the speedometer shown with scr_showspeed 2 or 3

entries.name: scratch1
entries.description: Server variable for use custom mod use.

entries.name: scratch2
entries.description: Server variable for use custom mod use.

entries.description: Server variable for use custom mod use.

entries.description: Server variable for use custom mod use.

entries.name: screenshot
entries.description: The 'screenshot' command now supports optional format (tga, png or jpg) and quality (1-100) arguments. bind "F11" "toggle r_drawviewmodel;toggle scr_showfps;scr_clock 0;toggle scr_ping; toggle scr_match_hud;viewsize 120;crosshair 0;wait;screenshot jpg 100;wait;toggle r_drawviewmodel;toggle scr_showfps;scr_clock 2;toggle scr_ping;toggle scr_match_hud;viewsize 100;crosshair 5" OR bind "F12" "scr_clock 4;wait;wait;wait;screenshot jpg 100;scr_clock 2"

entries.name: sensitivity
entries.description: The level of precision used for mouse movements. This is one of the most important variables in the whole game. This variable controls how sensitive the mouse is when moved. An incorrect setting for this variable means the difference between a match that was won and one that was lost. Most players set this variable to a value which they feel comfortable with. The setting for this variable is also dependent on the mouse driver used and the type of a mouse that is used. I personally have this variable set to a value of 17 while at the same time I have my sensitivity set to the 5th bar in Windows Mouse Control Panel which is 83% and I use the Logitech Trackman Marble. One of my friends also uses the same settings as I do and he uses the Microsoft Intelimouse. Other people however have settings as low as 6 and as high as 60 so there is a lot of diversity between these settings. A good way to measure if you have the correct sensitivity set is that you should be able to do a 180-degree turn with the flick of your thumb if you are using a trackball or the flick of your wrist if you are using a mouse. Do a couple of turns one after another and see if you can make a nice 180-degree turn and only be off by about 5-degrees. If you find yourself struggling to make a turn increase the value, if you find yourself m

entries.name: serverhostnames
entries.description: Lists or clears the persistent server-hostname cache. Listed entries include the hostname, address, port, connection date, and freshness state.

entries.name: serverinfo
entries.description: Display server info from client, timelimit and such. For use on QSS/FTE server

entries.name: serverprofile
entries.description: Toggle the display of server performance statistics. This command is very useful to server administrators who wish to see performance statistics for the server. This command will output the number of players currently connected to the server and also the amount of processing time in milliseconds that the server is using to calculate all of the game information. If you notice that the number of milliseconds is increasing beyond acceptable boundaries that means that you servers is struggling to calculate all of the information and it might be a good idea to lower the maximum number of players that can connect to the server.

entries.name: set
entries.description: The set and seta commands are used to manage console variables (cvars) in a game or engine, providing a way to configure and customize settings. The set command is used to temporarily create or modify a cvar and assign it a value for the current session. These changes do not persist after the game or engine is restarted, making set ideal for experimenting with settings or enabling temporary features, such as displaying the frame rate with set r_drawfps 1. The seta command, on the other hand, not only sets the cvar but also marks it as archived, ensuring it is saved to the configuration file (e.g., config.cfg) and persists across sessions. For example, seta sensitivity 2.5 adjusts the mouse sensitivity and saves it for future launches. Both set and seta can create new cvars if they don’t already exist in the engine. This feature allows players or developers to introduce custom variables for use in mods, scripts, or debugging. For instance, a mod might read a custom cvar like seta map_vote_preference "ctf" to influence gameplay decisions. Additionally, custom cvars can store temporary states, track preferences, or enable future-proofing for features not yet supported by the engine. However, creating unnecessary cvars without a clear purpose can lead to clutter. If a cvar is already archived (saved in the configuration file), the set command can still be used to override its value temporarily for the current session, which is useful for testing without altering the saved value. Similarly, the seta command can be used to update the archived value in the configuration file, ensuring that the new value becomes the default in future sessions. When it comes to manually editing configuration files, using set makes more sense than seta. The reason is that set is lightweight and does not modify the archival status of a cvar. In contrast, adding seta redundantly to the config file for already archived cvars can lead to unnecessary duplication and clutter, as archived cvars are automatically saved by the engine whenever their values are changed. This distinction is particularly useful for tailoring the experience: set is perfect for temporary adjustments, debugging, creating custom cvars, or direct use in configuration files for non-archived cvars, while seta is used to lock in preferred settings like field of view or crosshair color customization. By combining both commands, players and developers can optimize settings efficiently without unnecessary file edits, maintaining a balance between experimentation, customization, and permanence.
