entries.name: setfl
entries.description: setfl is like set/seta, but it also lets you apply cvar flags in the same command via a 3rd argument. Supported flag letters are a (archive / “seta”-style), u (userinfo), and s (serverinfo); unknown letters produce a warning and abort. Unlike set/seta, which now reject “extra args”, setfl is the intended way to do “set with flags” safely. Example: setfl name "Tim" u (userinfo) or setfl hostname "My Server" s (serverinfo), or setfl sensitivity 3.5 a (archived like seta).

entries.name: setinfo
entries.description: Lets client set serverside into via console.

entries.name: setpos
entries.description: Command to teleport you to a specific spot in the map. Type viewpos to get an x y z or you could type r_pos. QSSM added: setpos last will take you to the last position viewed by viewpos

entries.name: sfx_preview
entries.description: Plays a sound file through an isolated preview channel intended for auditioning assets. Its subcommands provide pause, resume, stop, status, looping, gain, and fractional seeking controls.

entries.name: showflags
entries.description: Allows CTF flag entities to spawn through a single-player fallback when their normal QuakeC functions are unavailable, defaulting to 0. The setting is captured when the server loads a map and applies only to single-player, non-cooperative games

entries.name: showpause
entries.description: Toggle the display of a graphical icon when the game is paused. When the game is currently paused a graphical image will be displayed on the player’s screen to inform him about the status of the game. This command will be able to toggle if that graphic is to be displayed. It’s a good idea to leave this toggle enabled so that you will know if the game is paused or not. Sometimes though, if you wish to take screen shots of the game in progress you might want to disable to toggle and use the pause command in order to stop the action in the game. That way you will be able to take screen shots in peace and exactly at the times that you want.

entries.name: showturtle
entries.description: Toggle the display of a graphical icon when the frame rate in the game drops below 10 frames-per-second. By default this toggle is disabled. You might want to enable this toggle if you wish to check the performance of your system when playing the game. If you notice this icon appearing many times during the game that means that your computer can’t perform well enough to draw 10 frames-per-second on the screen. If that’s the came you might want to think about upgrading the CPU or the video card in your computer. As an alternative you might want to use the sizedown or viewsize commands to lower the screen size in order to increase performance. If you do not wish to lower the screen size you might want to use the d_mipcap and d_mipscale commands to lower the texture detail for the maps.

entries.name: sizedown
entries.description: Decrease the screen size for the game. You can use this command in order to shrink the size of the display for the game. This might sometimes be necessary if the game is running slowly on your given system. This command works in conjunction with the viewsize variable to control the size of the screen. Every time that this command is used it will lower the value in the viewsize variable by 10 up to the minimum value of 30.

entries.name: sizeup
entries.description: Increase the screen size for the game. You can use this command in order to enlarge the size of the display for the game. This command works in conjunction with the viewsize variable to control the size of the screen. Every time that this command is used it will increase the value in the viewsize variable by 10 up to the maximum value of 120. When the viewsize variable is at 100 both status bars will be visible. When this command is used and the variable is increased the weapon status bar will disappear, when this command is used once again and the variable is increased to 120 the health status bar will disappear.

entries.name: skill
entries.description: The difficulty setting for the game. This toggle will enable the player to manually select the difficulty level for the game. Normally the player selects the difficulty that he would like to play by selecting the appropriate slipgate on the Introduction map. The setting of this toggle determines the number of monsters on the levels, the difficulty required to kill them, the amount of beneficial items available to the player on the maps, and the amount of damage that is inflicted on the player by the monsters. Also, when this toggle is set to 3 and the game is in Nightmare Difficulty mode the monsters will come back to life 30-seconds after they are killed. Any hardcore player should be able to beat the game at the Hard Difficulty mode, but only the best or the craziest of people will attempt Nightmare Difficulty. The entrance to the Nightmare Slipgate is hidden on the Introduction map. You can access it by passing through one of the three initial slipgates to get to the episode selection chamber. Then walk up the wooden stairs up to the pool of water at the entrance to the 4th episode, The Elder World. The message for that episode should give you a clue, “Your worst nightmares come true…“. When you are at the pool of water, jump in but hold down the key bound to the +jump command in order to float. Slowly release the key and move towards wall in the pool which is closest to the stairs that you just came from. When you are touching that wall, let yourself fall through the pool. You should end up standing on a wooden beam. Follow that beam to your right and you will come across a door high up in the wall. You have found the slipgate for Nightmare mode.

entries.name: sky
entries.description: Loads a skybox, for testing purposes. If skyname is "", this will turn off skybox rendering.

entries.name: skyroom
entries.description: "_skyroom" "x y z paralax rotspeed rotx roty rotz" Sample: skyroom 885 907 107 0.1 0 0 1 30 or x y z 0 yourrotationspeed 0 0 1 (make qss spin its skyroom around the vertical at yourrotationspeed). You might need to place an info_notnull or something in it, in case your qbsp fills it in otherwise. Light entities will probably work too. Add a fourth arg for a parallax effect. its value controls what proportion of the player's origin to add to the skyroom's origin (0 makes it a boring fixed position, other values require your skyroom to be big enough to handle the player moving around the map). If you have a fifth arg then that's how fast the skyroom should spin. The 6-8th args define the axis for it to spin around (so 0 0 1 makes it spin around the vertical). probably you won't bother with those args, unless its meant to be some space scene. The server will read the first three and punch a hole in the server's pvs so you can see ents in there

entries.name: skywind
entries.description: Skywind adds an animated “wind” scroll to skybox skies by offsetting the cubemap lookup over time (with a two-phase blend to avoid visible seams), and it updates automatically each frame once enabled. To use it, load a skybox and run skywind <dist> [yaw] [period] [pitch] where dist (−2..2) is strength (0 = off, negative reverses), yaw is direction in degrees, period is seconds per full cycle, and pitch tilts the wind up/down; you can also aim it with skywind_lookdir [period] [dist] or nudge it with skywind_rotate <yawdelta> [pitchdelta]. For persistence and map-specific behavior, skywind_save writes gfx/env/<sky>wind.cfg (and skywind_load reloads it), and maps can override via the worldspawn key skywind, while r_skywind can either act as a simple rate or (if set to four numbers) provide defaults in the same dist yaw period pitch format.

entries.name: skywind_load
entries.description: Loads the current skybox’s saved sky-wind configuration. It reports failure instead of silently falling back when explicitly invoked.

entries.name: skywind_lookdir
entries.description: Sets the sky-wind direction from the player’s current viewing direction. Optional arguments set the animation period and wind distance.

entries.name: skywind_rotate
entries.description: Adjusts the current sky-wind yaw and optional pitch by relative amounts. It requires an active connection and a loaded skybox.

entries.name: skywind_save
entries.description: Saves the current sky-wind parameters alongside the active skybox configuration. The generated file records distance, yaw, period, and pitch.

entries.name: slist
entries.description: Look for and display a list of all game servers on the local network. When this command is used it will broadcast a message on the local network looking for game servers. This command will then display all of the servers which have been found. You can then use the name of the server to connect to that server using the connect command.

entries.name: snd_filterquality
entries.summary: Sets sound resampling filter quality from 1 to 5; the default depends on the platform.
entries.description: Accepts values from 1 through 5. The compiled default is 5 on Windows and 1 on other platforms. A value outside this range is reset to the platform default. This variable is not saved to config.

entries.name: snd_mixspeed
entries.description: The default to 44100 and just control the sample rate we request from SD

entries.name: snd_noextraupdate
entries.description: Toggle the update of sound information for correct statistics for the host_speeds command. When this toggle is active no update information is send out for the sound statistics. This will enable correct statistical information to be displayed when using the host_speeds command but it will mess up the sound playback in progress. Only enable when collecting statistics.

entries.name: snd_restart
entries.description: Restart sound when change hz in menu

entries.name: snd_show
entries.description: Toggle the display of the number of currently playing sound files. When this toggle is enabled a list will be shown with the number of sound files which are currently being played. This includes ambiance sounds, player sound effects, enemy sound effects, and environmental sound effects. QSSM: A value of 2 is a more verbose version with sound file info

entries.name: snd_surround
entries.description: Enables multichannel output using the audio device’s preferred channel count, defaulting to 1. The engine keeps its internal stereo mix and upmixes it for SDL2 output; changing the CVar requires snd_restart.

entries.name: snd_waterfx
entries.description: A basic underwater sound filter that slightly muffles effects when in water. Accepts decimal values.

entries.name: sndspeed
entries.description: Control whether the low-pass filter is applied. If it's set to 11025 you get the low-pass filter, otherwise it's not used.sndspeed 44100 -mixspeed 44100 : same behaviour as the old "-sndspeed 44100", no low-pass filter. sndspeed <any> -mixspeed 11025 : output at 11025, same as the old "-sndspeed 11025", no low-pass filter. music is downsampled to 11025Hz.

entries.name: -sndspeed
entries.description: Set sound speed.  Usual values are 8000, 11025, 22051 and 44100. Default is 11025. Sound speed in Hz, but there is cvar to do this in-game

entries.name: soundinfo
entries.description: Display a list of all sound files loaded into memory. When this command is used it will display all of the sound settings which are currently in effect, a lot of this information is very technical and only useful to game developers. The first line displays if the sound is able to be played back in stereo mode. The next two lines display information about the sound samples being used. The samplebits line displays the maximum number of bits that are used for some playback. The only two possible settings for this line are 8 and 16. When the loadas8bit toggle is enabled this line will read a value of 8. It is unknown what the submission_chunk value means. The next line displays the highest possible frequency that should be used for sound playback. The next line should display the I/O address of the DMA buffer used for the sound card. The last line displays the total number of available channels which can be used for sound playback. The number of channels changes with every map and it is dependent on the number of sounds which can be played back on that map.

entries.name: soundlist
entries.description: Display a list of all sound files loaded into memory. This command will display a very lengthy list with information about all of the sound files which are currently loaded into memory for that particular map. The game only loads the necessary sound files for a particular map. If a sound file has the letter L next to it that designates it as a looping sound which is usually used for environment sounds such as electrical buzz or wind which are played repeatedly. The next column displays the bit rate at which the particular sound file was recorded at. The setting of 16b designates that sound file to have been recorded at 16-bit rate, a setting of 8b designates that the sound file was recorded at an 8-bit rate. The next number is the size of the sound file in bytes such as 28120. The last piece of information lists the path and filename of the sound file such as doors/meduse.wav. The last line of information for this command displays the total amount of memory used by sound files.

entries.name: spawn
entries.description: Used to inform the client that the server is ready to send over the entity information. This is an internal command used by the game’s client and server protocol. After the server sends this command to the client it will send over information about all of the entities in the game in order for the client to display them on the screen.

entries.name: st
entries.description: Alias/shortcut to say_team (messagmode2)

entries.name: startdemos
entries.description: The startdemos command is used to create a playlist of demo files that will play sequentially. You can specify up to 32 demos (MAX_DEMOS) in a single command, with each demo name separated by spaces. The command's behavior is controlled by the cl_demoreel setting - if enabled, the demos will play in sequence, but if disabled, the command will simply open the menu instead. This feature is particularly useful for setting up demo playback during the game's idle state, creating custom demo reels for showcasing gameplay, or queueing multiple demos for consecutive viewing. Demo files must exist in your Quake directory, though you don't need to specify the .dem extension when using the command. For example, you might use startdemos e1m1 dm3 quad to queue three demos for playback. Note that this command has no effect on dedicated servers, and if you attempt to specify more than the maximum allowed demos, only the first 32 will be used.

entries.name: startup
entries.description: Executes the action configured in cl_onload. It can open a menu or console, begin demo behavior, or run another permitted command.

entries.name: status
entries.description: Display information about current server status. This command is very useful to server administrators. It displays detailed information about the server. The first field host: displays the name of the server. The next field version: displays the game version of the server. All of the clients must be using the same version in order to play on the server. The tcp/ip: field displays the current IP address which the server is using. The map: field displays the name of the map on which the players are playing. The players: field displays the number of currently connected players and the maximum amount of players that the server can accomodate. Below all of that is the information about each player. The first thing that is displayed is the player’s number, such as #3, which can be used with the kick command to remove the player from the server. The next thing displayed is the player’s name, such as FooMaster. After that is the player’s score such as 9. The next piece of information is the amount of time that the player has been connected to the server, such as 0:10:52 which means 10-minutes and 52-seconds. Below that information is the player’s IP address along with the client side port, which would could look like 192.246.40.38:1049. The client side port number is chosen randomly when the client connects to the server.

entries.name: stop
entries.description: Stop the recording of a demo. You must use this command to stop the recording of a demo once it is started. After the demo is stopped it will be written to the hard drive for future playback.

entries.name: stopdemo
entries.description: Stop the playback of a demo. Use this command if you wish to stop a demo that has been playing.

entries.name: stopdownload
entries.description: Sent by the server (or issued by the user) to stop the current download for any reason

entries.name: stopsound
entries.description: Stop the playback of all sounds. If you are having problems with the playback of sounds you can use this command to stop all sounds. This command is useful if a sound got stuck in an endless loop and you want to stop it from playing back.

entries.name: stuffcmds
entries.description: Stuffcmds now parses the "cmdline" cvar rather than the args actually passed to the program. This means that if you edit "cmdline," and "stuffcmds" is called again, your changes will have effect.

entries.name: sv_accelerate
entries.description: The value for player movement acceleration. You can control the how long it takes the player to accelerate to full speed. If this value is lowered to something like 5 it will take the player twice as long to achieve the maximum running speed. It is best to leave this variable alone when running a server.

entries.name: sv_adminnick
entries.description: Nick name to use for admin messages instead of host name

entries.name: sv_aim
entries.description: The leniency value for player’s aim adjustment. This variable controls how lenient the game is when it comes to the player’s aim. The current setting allows a player to shoot a little off the target and still score a hit. This variable might be useful for single-player games but it is quite annoying in multiplayer games. Most server administrators set this variable to a value of 1 in order to remove the server’s help when it comes to the player’s aim. If you run a public server, make sure that you use this setting.

entries.name: sv_airaccelerate
entries.description: These pm_ CVARs only apply when using the pmove physics system, which is enabled by setting sv_nqplayerphysics 0 or by having a custom QuakeC physics function. Controls how quickly players can accelerate while airborne through strafe-turning. Default value of "0.7" provides moderate air control, allowing skilled players to gain speed and change direction mid-air. Higher values make air movement more responsive, while lower values reduce air control and make movement more realistic.

entries.name: sv_altnoclip
entries.description: Move just forward (no vertical component) while looking downward

entries.name: sv_autoload
entries.description: sv_autoload automatically loads the last save game when restarting levels or respawning. Set to 0 (disabled), 1 (ask first), 2 (auto-load if dead), or 3 (always auto-load). It only works in single-player mode and requires having previously saved or loaded a game.

entries.name: sv_autosave
entries.description: Enables smart background autosaving in eligible single-player maps, defaulting to 1. Autosaves wait for safe conditions such as being alive, moving slowly, and not recently taking damage or firing.

entries.name: sv_autosave_interval
entries.description: Sets the base interval used by the smart autosave scoring system, defaulting to 30 seconds. Its absolute value controls timing, 0 disables interval saves, and a negative value additionally displays the saving indicator.

entries.name: sv_cheats
entries.description: for the 2021 rerelease compatibility

entries.name: sv_defaultmap
entries.description: Upon attempt to change server to a map that doesn't exist, this sets the fallback map

entries.name: sv_freezenonclients
entries.description: Locks all monsters/entities in place

entries.name: sv_friction
entries.description: The friction value for the player’s movement. You can use this command to lower the amount of friction on the map for the player’s movement. If you set this variable to 0 you will turn the map into an ice and the player won’t be able to stop. If you set this variable to a negative value, the player will gain speed when he moves. If you increase this variable you can really slow the player down. It’s recommended that you keep this variable at it’s default setting.

entries.name: sv_fullpitch
entries.description: The pq_fullpitch setting, found in Quake engines like ProQuake, controls whether players can fully pitch their view up and down. Originally, Quake restricted vertical view angles, preventing players from looking straight up or down. Setting sv_fullpitch to 1 allows a full range from -90 to 90 degrees, enabling better aiming and exploration. Modern engines like Quakespasm now allow full pitch (90 degrees) by default. Setting sv_fullpitch to 0 reverts to the original restricted range, though some servers may enforce specific settings for compatibility or fairness.

entries.name: sv_gameplayfix_bouncedownslopes
entries.description: Fixes grenades making horrible noises on slopes

entries.name: sv_gameplayfix_elevators
entries.description: Prevents entities riding pushers from becoming incorrectly blocked by tiny collision errors, defaulting to 2. Mode 0 disables the fix, mode 1 applies it only to clients, and mode 2 applies it to all entities.

entries.name: sv_gameplayfix_fishcount
entries.description: Prevents swimming monsters from being counted more than once when their startup function executes repeatedly, defaulting to 1. Disabling it restores the older behavior that can inflate the map’s total-monster count.

entries.name: sv_gameplayfix_setmodelrealbox
entries.description: 1 to replicate a quakespasm bug, 0 for actual vanilla compat

entries.name: sv_gameplayfix_spawnbeforethinks
entries.description: This prevents PlayerPreThink etc getting called on player entities that have not actually been spawned yet, thereby preventing Arcan Dimensions from spamming at the worst possible time.

entries.name: sv_gravity
entries.description: The amount of gravity on the level. You can have a lot of fun with this variable. If you set it to 0 everybody will become weight less and will start drifting throughout the level, the grenades will also bounce in funny ways. If you set this variable to a negative value, the players will look like hot air balloons and will start rising towards the sky. It is best to leave this variable alone when running a server, not too many people like to imitate balloons when playing.

entries.name: sv_heartbeat_interval
entries.description: Move heartbeats to a worker thread to avoid periodic stalls.

entries.name: sv_idealpitchscale
entries.description: The height that the player’s view moves up when going up stairs. This variable shouldn’t be part of the server variables. It controls how much the player’s screen tilts up and down when the player is moving up and down stairs. You can only see this effect when +mlook and +klook are not active. Setting this variable to 0 might be useful to keyboard only players when they have to go up and down a lot of stairs, but nobody should be a keyboard only player anymore.

entries.name: sv_map_rotation
entries.description: Easily set a space delimited map rotation for server regardless of mod, progs. Good for a basic server

entries.name: sv_mapcrc
entries.description: This change adds an optional two-stage map CRC handshake controlled by the sv_mapcrc cvar. When enabled, the server computes and advertises a quick CRC (first 4KB) and a full CRC (entire BSP) for the current map via *mapcrc_quick and *mapcrc_full. After fully connecting, the client recomputes both CRCs for its local map and compares them to the server’s values with CL_MapCRC_Validate. If they match, the client clears the *mapmismatch userinfo key; if they differ, it sets *mapmismatch to "1". The server watches for this flag in SV_UpdateInfo and, when present, logs and prints a warning to all other players that <name> connected with a different map version. Listen servers skip this validation, and *mapmismatch is reset on disconnect so it doesn’t carry over to future games.

entries.name: sv_maxspeed
entries.description: The maximum speed that the player can achieve through running. This is the maximum running speed for the player. The player can however exceed this speed when he’s falling or when he’s being thrown by explosions. It is also possible to exceed this speed by running next to a wall and use keys bound to the +moveleft or +moveright commands in order to achieve a gliding effect with the wall thus speeding up the player’s velocity. There is also a way to increase the player’s speed by using the above mentioned keys in quick succession when running on flat ground. The constant movement of the player to the left and to the right while running straight increases the player’s speed by quite a margin, sometimes exceeding 500. Some server administrators might increase this speed to 400 or above to speed up the pace of the game.

entries.name: sv_maxvelocity
entries.description: The maximum speed that an object can achieve in the game. This variable is basically used as a cutoff point in regards to how fast objects can move. This variable is necessary in order to prevent from objects accelerating too quickly which might cause problems with some calculations. It is best to leave this variable alone. However it might be necessary to increase this variable if somebody wants to test the the game’s physics using some of the other environment changing variables.

entries.name: sv_modvote
entries.description: Enables server-side voting to change mods during cooperative games, defaulting to 0. When enabled, eligible active players use modvote, and a majority switches to the selected installed mod.

entries.name: sv_nopunchangle
entries.description: Suppresses transmission of server-generated weapon and damage punch angles, defaulting to 0. Setting it to 1 prevents clients from receiving those view-kick updates.

entries.name: sv_nostep
entries.description: Toggle the automatic climbing of steps by the player.  If this toggle is enabled the player would not automatically climb steps by moving forward. Instead the player would have to use a key bound to the +jump command in order to climb steps. It is best to leave this variable alone because nobody wants to press a key a bunch of times just to climb up a few steps.

entries.name: sv_nqplayerphysics
entries.description: For mods that don't want to include SV_RunClientCommand for whatever reason. Set to 0 or "" to force predictable player physics. Set to 1 to disable prediction. cl_nopred 1; sv_nqplayerphysics 1 is very much the nq default

entries.name: sv_protocol
entries.description: Sets the network protocol used by the server. Default is 666. Possible values are 15 (standard netquake protocol) or 666 (new fitzquake protocol.) Changes to the protocol will not take effect until the next time you load/reload a level. When running protocol 666, standard clients won't be able to connect to your server, and they won't be able to play any demos you record. When running protocol 15, only 256 models and 256 sounds can be sent to the client, which means you would see invisible entities and not hear some sounds, when running a map or mod that has more than 256 models or sounds. There is also some other data the server will suppress in protocol 15, such as per-entity alpha. Also note, dzip's special demo compression does not work on demos that use modified protocols, so you will get a compression ratio no better than standard zip compression. QSS: Added 10002 (NEHAHRABJP3). Protocol may be prefixed with FTE+ or Base- to enable/disable FTE extensions

entries.name: sv_public
entries.summary: Controls public server announcements; defaults to 1 for dedicated servers and 0 otherwise.
entries.description: The initial value is assigned at server startup: 1 for a dedicated server, 0 for a client/listen server. Setting it above 0 enables announcements to the configured master servers; 0 disables those announcements.

entries.name: sv_reportheartbeats
entries.description: Enable/Disable reporting of heartbeats to console or not. Useful in ridding heartbeat messages from log files.

entries.name: sv_settimer
entries.description: Server-side timer system that lets you schedule console commands to run automatically on the server at fixed intervals. You can use the new sv_settimer command to periodically broadcast a message to all players, for example: sv_settimer -1 60 say Remember_to_join_our_Discord!. In this command, the first argument -1 is the count, which tells the timer to run forever (a positive number would run that many times, and 0 disables the timer). The second argument 60 is the interval, which is the delay in seconds between each execution, so here the message is sent once every 60 seconds. Everything after the interval (say Remember_to_join_our_Discord!) is the command string the server will execute on each tick; in this case it’s just a standard say command, which broadcasts the text Remember_to_join_our_Discord! to all connected players each time the timer fires.

entries.name: sv_sound_land
entries.description: Can be used as an alternative for the sound

entries.name: sv_sound_watersplash
entries.description: Can be used as an alternative for the sound

entries.name: sv_spectatormaxspeed
entries.description: These pm_ CVARs only apply when using the pmove physics system, which is enabled by setting sv_nqplayerphysics 0 or by having a custom QuakeC physics function. Sets the maximum movement speed for players in spectator mode. Default value of "500" units per second allows fairly fast movement for observing gameplay. This speed limit prevents spectators from moving too quickly and helps maintain smooth camera movement when watching matches.

entries.name: sv_startdownload
entries.description: Used by server to start download of missing items when connecting to server

entries.name: sv_stopspeed
entries.description: The velocity at which the player will start slowing down to stop his movement.  If the velocity of the player stays about the value in this variable the player will continue moving. Once his velocity drops below the value for this variable he will start slowing down in order to stop. If this value is increased so that it is close to the maximum running speed the player will continue to move but once he releases the movement key he will stop instantaneously. If this variable is set to 0 it will be hard for the player to stop instead he will have to depend on friction in order to stop him. If this variable is set to a value above the sv_maxspeed value the player will move very slowly because he will continue to stop even though he is trying to run at his top speed, kind of like pressing the break and gas pedals in the car. If this variable is set to a negative value there won’t be any difference from setting it to 0 because the player will never reach negative velocity in order to start the breaking process.

entries.name: sv_voip
entries.description: Enable server VOIP

entries.name: sv_voip_echo
entries.description: Controls whether a player hears their own voice echoed back to them by the server

entries.name: sv_wateraccelerate
entries.description: These pm_ CVARs only apply when using the pmove physics system, which is enabled by setting sv_nqplayerphysics 0 or by having a custom QuakeC physics function. Sets the acceleration rate when moving through water or other liquid environments. Default value of "10" makes underwater movement fairly responsive compared to ground movement. This affects how quickly players can change direction and build up speed while swimming.

entries.name: sv_waterfriction
entries.description: These pm_ CVARs only apply when using the pmove physics system, which is enabled by setting sv_nqplayerphysics 0 or by having a custom QuakeC physics function. Controls the friction applied to player movement while in water. Default value of "4" matches standard ground friction, making water feel moderately resistive. Higher values make water feel thicker and more difficult to move through, while lower values create more slippery, ice-like water.

entries.name: svi
entries.description: The svi command is not meant for users to type. It's an internal mechanism used by the server to automatically push updates about its configuration and state (specifically, its "serverinfo" cvars) to all connected clients, ensuring their information is synchronized.

entries.name: svnextmap
entries.description: Advance server to the next map set in sv_map_rotation variable. Only server allowed to use.

entries.name: sys_throttle
entries.description: Use 100% CPU instead of sleeping. QSS: A negative value -1 will not throttle when paused or minimized

entries.name: sys_ticrate
entries.description: The amount of time in seconds between consecutive packets send out by the server to the client. This is one of the most important variables for the server. The default setting of 0.05 will send out 20 packets-per-second to the client. This number is too high for players using modems to connect to the Internet. It is recommended that server administrators set this variable to 0.1 in order to limit the number of out going packets to the clients to 10 packets-per-second. Setting this variable will make a lot of modem players happy.

entries.name: teamplay
entries.description: Toggle the settings for teamplay games. There are two different rules for teamplay games. When this toggle is set to 1 players with the same color pants will be regarded as a team. They will be unable to hurt each other and every player will also be unable to hurt himself. The second mode for teamplay games is when this toggle is set to a value of 2. In this mode players with the same color pants will be a team but they will be able to hurt each other and hurt themselves. If a player kills another player from his team that player will lose 1 point from his score. It is recommended to use the teamplay setting of 2 when playing in clan matches. This prevents people from blindly firing at the enemy without regard for the safety of their own team members. Most clans use this setting for team games.

entries.name: tell
entries.description: Send a private message to a specific player. tell wo how are you? will send a private message to woods: how are you?. The name uses a wildcard OR you can type the scoreboard number found in status. tell 2 how are you? will send the message to the #2 person on the scoreboard.

entries.name: temp1
entries.description: Empty variable. This variable was left empty on purpose. It was used as a temporarily storage variable for testing. Some mods use this variable to hold special settings.

entries.name: test
entries.description: Display information about the players connected to the server. This command can be used by clients to find out more information about the other players on the server. If a player is being annoying or is just down abusive you can use this command to find out his IP address so you can deal with him. You can also use the test2 command to find out information about the current server settings. (test denver.quakeone.com)  -- like connect command

entries.name: test2
entries.description: Display information about the current server settings. This command is very similar to the test command but this one gives information about the server settings instead of players. This is very useful if you wish to find out what teamplay mode the server is running so that you don’t have to knock one of your team mates upside the head with a rocket just to find out. (test denver.quakeone.com) -- like connect command

entries.name: tex_parallel
entries.description: Enables the staged texture-preparation path used during map loading, defaulting to 1. Setting it to 0, or launching with -noparalleltextureprep, restores the legacy serial path.

entries.name: tex_verify
entries.description: Enables texture-preparation hash diagnostics, defaulting to 0. It only emits texhash comparisons when developer 1 is also active and is intended for verifying identical results across loading modes.

entries.name: tex_workers
entries.description: Selects the number of participants used for staged texture preparation, defaulting to 0 for automatic CPU-based selection. A value of 1 exercises the staged path serially, while higher values request parallel preparation up to the engine’s bounded maximum.

entries.name: -textureworkers
entries.description: Sets the number of participants used for parallel texture preparation. The supplied value is clamped to the engine’s supported worker limit.

entries.name: timedemo
entries.description: Time the speed of demo playback to calculate the frames-per-second rate. You can use this command to test how fast your computer is by looking at the frames-per-second rate achieved by playing back a couple of demos at top speed. This command will play back all of the frames for a given demo as fast as possible and then record the amount of time that it took to play back all of the frames from that demo. Then this command will take the total number of frames in a demo, divide that number by the amount of time that it took to play back those demos, and calculate the frames-per-second rate. The frames-per-second rate will be different on different computers and at different resolutions. When calculating the speed of your computer it is best to set the viewsize variable to 100. This way the results would mimic the actual playing screen instead of being inflated by a screen that is smaller or larger. Most people use the ‘timedemo demo2‘ command to test their computer.

entries.name: timelimit
entries.description: The amount of time in minutesthat a map should be played before automatically switching to the next map. When this variable is set to any value larger than 0 the game will wait that amount of time before it changes maps. This is variable is often used by servers to cycle between maps and to keep the game going from one map to another. A good value to set this variable to is 20 because that will allow the players to play that specific map for 20-minutes before switching to the next map. Be careful of setting this variable too low or too high because players will leave the server if the maps don’t switch quickly enough due to boredom. Also, you might want to use the fraglimit variable along with this variable and set that variable to a value such as 30.

entries.name: timerefresh
entries.description: Peform a 360 degree turn and calculate the frames-per-second rate. This command can be used to test the speed of your computer at a given location in any map. When you are standing somewhere in a map and execute this command, the player’s view will turn around 360 degrees and record the number of seconds that it took for a complete turn. Then this command will divide 128 by the number of seconds that it look to complete the turn to calculate the frames-per-second rate. Be aware, that this command should only be used to get a very broad idea of the computer’s performance. The frames-per-second rate produced by this command is highly inflated when compared to the number produced by the timedemo command. If you want to test your computer, use the ‘timedemo demo2‘ command instead.

entries.name: tinfo
entries.description: tinfo is not a command for users to type. It's an internal server-to-client command, part of a team information protocol extension, used to send detailed status updates about players (primarily teammates) to clients for display on the HUD.

entries.name: toggle
entries.description: Inverts the value of a cvar (nonzero -> 0 and 0 -> 1) -- Example: "toggle volume" will mute, unmute. QSS adds  2+3 arg forms (toggle <cvar> [value] [altvalue]: toggle cvar) -- You could also use this function to toggle between more specific values. For example, suppose you have a variable named texture_detail that could be set to "low", "medium", or "high". You could switch it between "low" and "high" with the following command. See cycle.

entries.name: toggleconsole
entries.description: Lower or raise the console screen. This is the primary command used to get access to the console. This command will automatically detect if the console is in a lowered position or in a raised position and it will perform the appropriate action.

entries.name: togglemenu
entries.description: Display or close the main menu. This command will automatically detect if the menu is being displayed or not and it will perform the appropriate action when executed.

entries.name: togglezoom
entries.description: Zoom in and out. bind "b" "togglezoom"

entries.name: tool_texturepointer
entries.description: Show texture in the map that is being pointed out

entries.name: topcolor
entries.description: User info keys used in QW/FTE/QSS. See setinfo and serverinfo

entries.name: trace_any
entries.description: Draws tracers to any edict whose classname contains the value of trace_any_contains. Values < 1 for alpha of lines

entries.name: trace_any_contains
entries.description: `trace_any_contains key2` show lines to gold keys. OPTIONS: weapon_rocketlauncher, weapon_lightning, item_artifact_invulnerability, weapon_supernailgun, item_artifact_invisibility, weapon_supershotgun, item_armor2 (yl), item_armorInv (rd), item_armor1 (gr)

entries.name: tracepos
entries.description: Display impact point of trace along VPN

entries.name: -udpport
entries.description: Specifies a UDP port to be used other than the default of 26000.

entries.name: ui
entries.description: The ui command is part of the engine's internal protocol. It is sent by the server to clients to trigger an update of a player's user information, likely for scoreboard display or other UI elements. It's not intended for direct use by players in the console.

entries.name: ui_live_preview
entries.description: Enables live previews when changing supported menu options, defaulting to 1. Previewable visual settings temporarily reveal the game view, while the original value is restored if the selection is cancelled.

entries.name: unalias
entries.description: Deletes the specified alias.

entries.name: unaliasall
entries.description: Deletes all aliases.

entries.name: unbind
entries.description: Remove a binding from a key. You can use this command to remove bindings which have been assigned to keys. For the names of non-printable keys refer to the bind command. This command is mostly used by script writers to remove bindings from keys that do not need to be bound at that particular moment.

entries.name: unbindall
entries.description: Remove bindings from all keys. Be very careful when using this command because you will remove all of the bindings and thus render the game pretty much useless. This command will unbind all keys except for the ESCAPE key which is usually bound to access the menu. This command should not be used by inexperienced people and only by script writers who need to clear all bindings to load their script onto a clean configuration.

entries.name: unignore
entries.description: The ignore command hides all chat messages from a specified player — type ignore <name> while connected to mute someone, or ignore with no arguments to list all currently ignored players. To restore chat from an ignored player, use unignore <name>. Both commands support partial name matching (for example, ignore tim will match a player named “timbo”), work client-side in singleplayer/listen servers and server-side when sent from a connected client, and the ignore list is cleared when you disconnect.

entries.name: unmuteall
entries.description: The unmuteall command is typed by the user on the client to instantly unmute all players they have previously ignored using the vignore command. It works by sending a corresponding instruction to the server.

entries.name: unpak
entries.description: unpak a pak, pk3, or kpf file

entries.name: update
entries.description: Checks for, downloads, verifies, stages, and installs a QSS-M portable release. Its subcommands can only check for updates, prepare files, force installation, or open the release page.

entries.name: -useice
entries.description: Enables the new ICE networking driver at startup. Default behavior is OFF: if you don’t pass -useice, the ICE driver refuses to init (“disable by default for now”). This is the switch you need before any of the net_ice_* cvars (and net_ice_show) are even registered/usable. Example: ./quake -useice (then configure net_ice_servers, sv_port_rtc, etc.).

entries.name: user
entries.description: Show the players on the server by name

entries.name: v_centermove
entries.description: The distance that the player must move before the screen automatically centers itself when the lookspring toggle is enabled. This command is only useful to people who only play with the keyboard, have lookspring enabled and do not have +klook or +mlook enabled at that time. When the player moves the distance specified in this command the screen will pop back to the center position.

entries.name: v_centerspeed
entries.description: The speed at which the screen will automatically return to the center position.

entries.name: v_cshift
entries.description: Shift the pallet for the game screen to produce color effects. This command can be used by script authors to produce some nice color effects on the screen. This command was originally used by the game designers to test out different color effects before implementing them in the game code. Below are a couple of cool color examples that can be used with this command. Use the ‘v_cshift 1 1 1 1‘ command to return the colors back to normal.

entries.name: v_gunkick
entries.description: If 1, standard quake view kick when you fire your gun. If 2, interpolates the view kick. If 0, disables view kick entirely. Default 1.

entries.name: v_idlescale
entries.description: The amount that the screen should sway. When this variable is increased the screen will start swaying in all directions, this would be the effect if the player was drunk of had a concussion. If you want to have some real fun, set this variable to a value of 100 and run around some maps. The larger the value for this variable the more the screen will sway from side to side. By default this variable is set to 0 in order to remove any swaying effects.

entries.name: v_ipitch_cycle
entries.description: The speed at which the screen should sway up and down.

entries.name: v_ipitch_level
entries.description: The distance that the screen should sway up and down.

entries.name: v_iroll_cycle
entries.description: The speed at which the screen should roll clockwise and counter clockwise.

entries.name: v_iroll_level
entries.description: The distance that the screen should roll clockwise and counter clockwise.

entries.name: v_iyaw_cycle
entries.description: The speed at which the screen should turn left and right.

entries.name: v_iyaw_level
entries.description: The distance that the screen should turn left and right.

entries.name: v_kickpitch
entries.description: The distance that the screen should move up or down when the player is shot. Some players set this variable to 0 in order to remove the screen tiling effects when they are injured by a shot. This allows them to keep a perfect aim while being fired upon.

entries.name: v_kickroll
entries.description: The distance that the screen should roll clockwise or counter clockwise when the player is shot. Some players set this variable to 0 in order to remove the screen tiling effects when they are injured by a shot. This allows them to keep a perfect aim while being fired upon.

entries.name: v_kicktime
entries.description: The amount of time that the screen should remain tiled after the player has been shot. Some players set this variable to 0 in order to remove the screen tiling effects when they are injured by a shot. This allows them to keep a perfect aim while being fired upon.

entries.name: v_viewheight
entries.description: Adds a configurable vertical camera offset, defaulting to 0. Nonzero values are clamped from -7 through 4 and replace normal view bob with the selected fixed adjustment.

entries.name: version
entries.description: Display the version information about the game.

entries.name: vid_borderless
entries.description: Get a borderless window

entries.name: vid_bpp
entries.description: Sets the color depth of the screen in fullscreen mode. Windowed mode ignores this setting. Can be 16 or 32. Default 16. (Changes won't take effect until the next call to vid_restart.)

entries.name: vid_describecurrentmode
entries.description: Display information about the current video mode. This command will show some information about the current video mode. The first piece of information is the resolution, such as 800×600. The next part describes if the video mode is in full screen mode or in a window. The last piece of information is the video driver being used for the full screen video mode, such as LINEAR8.DRV.

entries.name: vid_describemodes
entries.description: Display information about all supported video modes. This command is useful when you want to see what video modes your current configuration supports. The first number is the number of the video mode used for switching to it. The next number is the resolution for that given video mode, such as 1024×768. After that, the video mode is labled as being full screen or windowed. Also, the name of the video driver for full screen modes is displayed, such as LINEAR8.DRV. Below is a list of all the video drivers currently supported internally by the game. The Accelerated VESA drivers are the fastest drivers for high resolution graphics. Overall the fastest driver is the Standard VGA 8-bit color driver because it is fine tuned for performance.

entries.name: vid_desktopfullscreen
entries.description: Windowed fullscreen mode

entries.name: vid_fsaa
entries.description: Full screen anti-aliasing to get rid of the jagged edges. Effects FPS heavily. Use 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 16. Most noticeable on geometry edges and fine details

entries.name: vid_fullscreen
entries.description: If 1, fitzquake will run fullscreen. If 0, fitzquake will run in a window. Default 1. (Changes won't take effect until the next call to vid_restart.)

entries.name: vid_fxaa
entries.description: vid_fxaa is a console variable that controls Fast Approximate Anti-Aliasing (FXAA), a post-processing technique that smooths jagged edges in the rendered image to improve visual quality. The cvar accepts integer values from 0 to 3, where 0 disables FXAA completely, 1 enables low-quality FXAA with minimal performance impact, 2 enables medium-quality FXAA (the default setting), and 3 enables high-quality FXAA with the most aggressive smoothing but higher performance cost. When enabled, FXAA uses OpenGL shaders to process the rendered frame and applies different quality presets with varying subpixel and edge detection parameters (low: 0.25/0.333, medium: 0.40/0.166, high: 0.75/0.063). The implementation automatically manages framebuffers and textures, cleaning up resources when FXAA is disabled and using different shader programs for lower quality levels (simple 5-tap shader) versus the high quality level (FTE directional-search shader).

entries.name: vid_height
entries.description: Sets the vertical screen/window resolution. In windowed mode, cannot be less than 200. Default 480. (Changes won't take effect until the next call to vid_restart.)

entries.name: vid_refreshrate
entries.description: Sets the refresh rate of the screen in fullscreen mode. Windowed mode ignores this setting. Possible values include 60, 70, 72, 75, 85, etc. Default 60. (Changes won't take effect until the next call to vid_restart.)

entries.name: vid_restart
entries.description: Tries to set a video mode that matches the values of vid_width, vid_height, vid_fullscreen, and, if vid_fullscreen is 1, vid_bpp and vid_refreshrate.

entries.name: vid_saveresize
entries.description: Saves manually resized window dimensions into vid_width and vid_height, defaulting to 1. It only records ordinary windowed sizes and does not overwrite them while fullscreen or desktop-fullscreen is active.

entries.name: vid_test
entries.description: Like vid_restart, except that after switching to the new mode pops up a confirmation dialogue. This is useful if you are not sure what modes your monitor can handle, so you don't get stuck with a blank screen. The dialogue has a time limit so that if you don't press a key within 5 seconds, it will revert to the previous mode.

entries.name: vid_unlock
entries.description: Used internally.

entries.name: vid_vsync
entries.description: Set to 1 to enable vertical sync, which eliminates tearing, but caps your framerate at the monitor refreshrate. Set to 0 to disable vertical sync, which allows tearing but doesn't cap your framerate. Note: If fitzquake detects that your driver settings have forced vsync to be disabled, it will post a message to the console saying so, and this cvar will have no effect. Default 0.

entries.name: vid_width
entries.description: Sets the horizontal screen/window resolution. In windowed mode, cannot be less than 320. Default 640. (Changes won't take effect until the next call to vid_restart.)

entries.name: viewframe
entries.description: Display the specified frame for the model being displayed by the viewmodel command.

entries.name: viewmodel
entries.description: Display a particular model or sprite at the location of the viewthing entity on the map.  In order for this command to work a map must be created with an entity called viewthing. Once a map like that is created you will be able to change the model which is currently displayed at the location of that entity. You can also change the current frame being displayed for that model file with the use of the viewframe command. If a viewthing entity is not located on the message “No viewthing on map” will be displayed. Below is a list of all the model or sprite files in the game.

entries.name: viewnext
entries.description: Display the next frame for the viewthing entity when using the viewmodel command.

entries.name: viewpos
entries.description: Outputs (X,Y,Z) pitch yaw roll. QSSM: Adds copy arg

entries.name: viewprev
entries.description: Display the previous frame for the viewthing entity when using the viewmodel command.

entries.name: viewsize
entries.description: The size of the viewable game screen. This variable determines how large the viewable screen size is. The lower the screen size the better the performance of the game and the higher the frame rate. Some people might need to use this variable to decrease the screen size to achieve acceptable game performance. You can also use the sizeup and sizedown commands to change the screen size in increments of 10.

entries.name: vignore
entries.description: To manage incoming voice chat, you can utilize the `vignore` command directly in your client console. This command serves to inform the server about specific players whose voice transmissions you wish to block or unblock. Upon receiving this instruction, the server adjusts its filtering rules for your connection, preventing voice packets from the specified ignored players from being relayed to you. For instance, entering `vignore 3 1` would mute the player currently occupying client slot 3, while subsequently entering `vignore 3 0` would unmute that same player, allowing you to hear their voice chat once again.

entries.name: voicetarg
entries.description: To control who hears your voice chat, use the `voicetarg` command followed by a specific target identifier. This command instructs the server about your intended audience when you activate your push-to-talk key, although the server makes the final decision based on game rules and settings. Common targets include `all`, which broadcasts your voice to everyone the server permits (often the default setting), or `team`, which restricts your voice communication solely to teammates in team-based games. You can also attempt to target an individual player directly by specifying their client ID number, for instance, `voicetarg 3` would aim your voice chat at the player connected as client 3. In practice, you should execute the `voicetarg` command *before* you press your designated push-to-talk key. For example, to speak only to your team, first type `voicetarg team` into the console and press Enter. Then, press and hold your `+voip` key (like 'V' or 'MOUSE2', depending on your binding) to transmit your voice to just your teammates. If you later wish to broadcast to everyone again, you would type `voicetarg all`, press Enter, and then use your push-to-talk key as usual.

entries.name: -voip
entries.description: Client disable VOIP

entries.name: voip
entries.description: The standalone voip command has a very specific and limited usage pattern. It only performs an action if used with the exact argument structure voip maxgain <value>, where <value> represents an integer number. For example, you would type voip maxgain 30000. If you execute the voip command by itself or with any arguments other than the literal word maxgain followed immediately by a number, the command will have no effect. This command serves a technical purpose, adjusting a specific parameter for the Speex audio library's Automatic Gain Control (AGC), and it only functions if the engine has been compiled with Speex support; consequently, it's not a command typically relevant for regular users.

entries.name: volume
entries.description: The volume for music and sound effects in the game. See inc and cycle (can be used to adjust)

entries.name: -w
entries.description: Alias for window, see window

entries.name: w_switch
entries.description: This variable allows you to define the highest weapon that the client should switch to when picking it up. The possible arguments of "w_switch" refer to the impulse that is used to switch to a certain weapon: 1-8 (the weapon numbers). Most common is w_switch 2. The server quakec controls this behavior and this sends the info to the server if supported via a infokey. Also see b_switch

entries.name: wait
entries.description: Stop the processing of commands for one game frame. This command was created in order to help script makers with complex aliases. This command must be used between each instance of the impulse command if they are used consecutively inside aliases. This command might also be used to cause a small delay between two consecutive commands which perform some timed action. The time interval for this command varies between each computer so this command cannot be used for accurate judgment of time.

entries.name: waterfog
entries.description: Overrides the density and color used for underwater fog. Running it without arguments prints its accepted forms and current values.

entries.name: which
entries.description: Command is designed to help you list files within the game's directories that match specific patterns you provide. This can be particularly useful for finding files, checking the contents of directories, or verifying the presence of game assets. Use * to match any number of characters and ? to match a single character. For example, *.txt will list all TXT files. To search for all files with a name that starts with config, regardless of their extension, you would use: config*. You can use the ? wildcard to substitute for the single unknown character in the filename. In this case, you would use level?.cfg as your search pattern: level?.cfg. ls * will list all the files. Examples: "*.pak *.txt", "*", "pak1.pak", "?onfig.cfg". Same as: ls, dir, flocate, which

entries.name: wps
entries.description: wps is an internal server-to-client command intended for sending weapon statistics, originating from mods like KTX/CSPREE. However, in this specific engine codebase, the client is currently set up to ignore this command, so it has no functional effect. It's not a command for users to type.
